headline: Paul Anthony Kelly recalls racing against time to learn tango with Jessica Lange
description: Paul Anthony Kelly reveals how he and Jessica Lange learned the tango in just one hour for 'American Horror Story'
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Paul Anthony Kelly has revealed that he had only about an hour to learn the tango with Jessica Lange before filming their scene for American Horror Story season 13.

The actor, who portrays the Devil opposite Lange's Constance Langdon, told PEOPLE that neither performer had previous experience with the dance, making the preparation particularly challenging.

“The tango-dancing, I think, was probably the most challenging, ’cause neither of us knew how to tango yet,” Kelly said in an interview ahead of the season 13 finale on October 29. He added that they had approximately an hour to learn the choreography before filming began.

The scene features Kelly's character dancing with Lange's Constance in an elaborate, candlelit room. Wearing a striking red gown, Constance discusses feeling trapped in the house before suggesting she could become the Devil's partner. However, the exchange takes an unexpected turn when he reveals that he is her father before disappearing.

Despite the limited preparation time, Kelly recalled the tango sequence as an enjoyable experience. He said the pair shared several laughs while filming whenever they made mistakes.

“That was a great experience, learning to tango with Jessica Lange,” he said, adding that he had no previous dance experience. “I have two left feet,” he joked.

Kelly also described working with Lange, Sarah Paulson, John Waters and Billie Lourd as a privilege. He praised the longtime American Horror Story cast members for their performances and the opportunity to observe how they brought their established characters to life.

The actor also discussed creating his version of the Devil, explaining that the fictional role gave him more creative freedom than portraying John F. Kennedy Jr. in Ryan Murphy's Love Story.

He envisioned the Devil as a sophisticated, suave and classic Hollywood-inspired character.

American Horror Story season 13 is now streaming on Hulu.

headline: New York state police to investigate sexual assault complaints at Cornell University
description: Cornell survivors can choose state or university police to lead criminal investigations
author: Reuters
article_text:
New York Governor Kathy Hochul has announced an agreement allowing state police to investigate sexual assault complaints at Cornell University, following criticism of the institution’s handling of a former student’s allegation that she was gang-raped at a fraternity house.

Under the agreement signed by Cornell University and New York State Police on Thursday, survivors who decide to pursue criminal charges can choose whether state police or Cornell University Police will lead their investigations.

They may also request that Ithaca Police or the Tompkins County Sheriff’s Office handle their cases, according to the university.

"Every student deserves to feel safe on their campus. And when someone reports sexual assault, they deserve to be heard, treated with compassion, and know their allegations will be taken seriously and thoroughly investigated by law enforcement trained to support survivors,” Hochul said in her statement.

The arrangement follows renewed scrutiny of Cornell’s response to allegations involving a former student, identified as Jane Doe in a civil lawsuit, who says she was pressured to consume drugs and sexually assaulted by seven members of the Chi Phi fraternity in October 2024.

The woman reported the incident to Cornell police. The local district attorney initially declined to pursue charges but reopened the criminal investigation in September 2026. Lawyers for some of the accused men have denied the allegations. The claims have not yet been established in court.

Hochul appointed New York Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor to oversee the criminal investigation. Separately, former US Deputy Attorney General Sally Yates was appointed to lead an independent review of Cornell’s handling of sexual misconduct complaints.

The university said the agreement took effect immediately and would remain in place during the independent review.

headline: Macklemore, Aurora and more unite in Paris for Free Palestine tour
description: Macklemore announced the tour after being dropped by Ed Sheeran for making pro-Palestine statements
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Macklemore brought his Free Palestine Tour to Paris on October 29, with Aurora and a host of other artists joining the rapper for a concert supporting Palestinian liberation.

The Seattle-born musician arrived in the French capital for the second stop of the three-date European tour, following his removal from Ed Sheeran’s stadium tour after making statements in support of Palestinians.

The Paris concert featured performances from artists including Norwegian singer Aurora, alongside other musicians and activists who came together to use the stage in support of Palestine.

Macklemore launched the Free Palestine Tour after being dropped from Sheeran’s US Loop Tour in September. The decision followed the rapper’s onstage calls for a free Palestine and his expressions of solidarity with Palestinians in Gaza and the occupied West Bank.

The rapper subsequently announced his own series of concerts, with proceeds going towards organisations supporting Palestinians. The tour opened in Dublin on October 26 before moving to Paris, with its final European date scheduled for London on October 30.

The concerts have drawn attention to the role of artists and their platforms in political advocacy, particularly amid attempts to restrict or silence performers speaking out about Palestine.

Macklemore has previously argued that artists should use their platforms to raise awareness and stand in solidarity with Palestinians, rather than remain silent in the face of injustice.

The Free Palestine Tour’s Paris date followed the sold-out Dublin show, which featured guest appearances from Hozier, Kneecap and other artists. The London concert is set to bring the European run to a close, while further US dates are expected to be announced.

All proceeds from the tour are set to benefit organisations supporting the Palestinian people and the movement for Palestinian liberation.

headline: Drone strikes in Ethiopia kill at least 25: witnesses
description: Attack on an Ethiopian displacement camp housing 1,800 people worsens shortages of food and medicine
author: AFP
article_text:
Multiple drone strikes have hit northern regions of Ethiopia since Thursday, killing at least 25 civilians, including children, witnesses and a medical source told AFP on Friday.

The Ethiopian government has been fighting rebels in the states of Amhara and Tigray over the past month, and has used its large supply of drones to win a decisive advantage.

But it has been accused of indiscriminate attacks that have killed civilians.

In Amhara, a witness said four drone strikes "were carried out one after another" on Thursday on a camp for displaced people.

"We have buried 14 people at the IDP centre. Two more died while receiving medical treatment," said Yasin, who requested anonymity, adding that children and pregnant women were among the victims.

Two other residents of the camp, one of whom said he had buried bodies, reported 14 and 15 deaths respectively, including several children.

The strikes at the camp, 400 kilometres (250 miles) northeast of the capital Addis Ababa, occurred "just as the students were coming home from school", recounted Ahmed, one of the two other witnesses.

'Heartbreaking'

On Friday, another drone attack in Tigray hit a grain lorry that had already been struck the night before, killing at least 11.

"Yesterday evening, around 9:00 pm, a drone strike hit a private vehicle carrying sorghum in the centre of Rama town," a resident told AFP by phone.

"This morning, people were collecting the scattered grain when another strike hit them," he said.

There were mixed reports on the number of deaths, with a medical source at a hospital confirming they had received 11 dead.

The ACLED conflict monitor said the drone strike was "believed to have been carried out by the ENDF (Ethiopian National Defence Force)... killing 12 civilians and injuring an unspecified number of people".

"It was very sad and shocking. There was another drone strike yesterday targeted armed fighters, and that did not surprise us. But today's attack was heartbreaking because it hit young civilians," said another local.

The Ethiopian army did not respond to requests for comment.

It has been fighting the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), which launched attacks against federal forces last month.

But the rebels were ultimately pushed back and forced to abandon control of their strongholds in the northern state.

The TPLF has allied with other insurgent groups in other parts of the country, including one called the Fano in Amhara.

The fighting has raised fears of an international conflict as the Ethiopian army has advanced right up to the border with Eritrea, which has sent troops to support the TPLF.

article_html:
Multiple drone strikes have hit northern regions of Ethiopia since Thursday, killing at least 25 civilians, including children, witnesses and a medical source told AFP on Friday.

The Ethiopian government has been fighting rebels in the states of Amhara and Tigray over the past month, and has used its large supply of drones to win a decisive advantage.

But it has been accused of indiscriminate attacks that have killed civilians.

In Amhara, a witness said four drone strikes "were carried out one after another" on Thursday on a camp for displaced people.

"We have buried 14 people at the IDP centre. Two more died while receiving medical treatment," said Yasin, who requested anonymity, adding that children and pregnant women were among the victims.

Two other residents of the camp, one of whom said he had buried bodies, reported 14 and 15 deaths respectively, including several children.

The strikes at the camp, 400 kilometres (250 miles) northeast of the capital Addis Ababa, occurred "just as the students were coming home from school", recounted Ahmed, one of the two other witnesses.

'Heartbreaking'

On Friday, another drone attack in Tigray hit a grain lorry that had already been struck the night before, killing at least 11.

"Yesterday evening, around 9:00 pm, a drone strike hit a private vehicle carrying sorghum in the centre of Rama town," a resident told AFP by phone.

"This morning, people were collecting the scattered grain when another strike hit them," he said.

There were mixed reports on the number of deaths, with a medical source at a hospital confirming they had received 11 dead.

The ACLED conflict monitor said the drone strike was "believed to have been carried out by the ENDF (Ethiopian National Defence Force)... killing 12 civilians and injuring an unspecified number of people".

"It was very sad and shocking. There was another drone strike yesterday targeted armed fighters, and that did not surprise us. But today's attack was heartbreaking because it hit young civilians," said another local.

The Ethiopian army did not respond to requests for comment.

It has been fighting the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), which launched attacks against federal forces last month.

But the rebels were ultimately pushed back and forced to abandon control of their strongholds in the northern state.

The TPLF has allied with other insurgent groups in other parts of the country, including one called the Fano in Amhara.

The fighting has raised fears of an international conflict as the Ethiopian army has advanced right up to the border with Eritrea, which has sent troops to support the TPLF.

headline: William Shatner and Star Trek co-stars pay tribute to Patrick Stewart: 'Godspeed, captain'
description: Stewart became internationally recognised for playing Picard in 'Star Trek: The Next Generation'
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
William Shatner and members of the Star Trek cast have paid tribute to Patrick Stewart following the actor’s death at the age of 86, remembering the man behind Captain Jean-Luc Picard as a friend, colleague and extraordinary performer.

Shatner, who famously portrayed Captain James T Kirk in the original Star Trek series, shared a heartfelt message following Stewart’s death on October 28.

“What a heartbreaking week it has been. Sir Patrick Stewart was a friend, a colleague, and a magnificent actor,” Shatner wrote.

“From the stage to the bridge of the Enterprise, he brought intelligence, grace, and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did. Captain Picard stood for the best of us, and so did the man who played him. I was filled with affection and admiration for him and his work.”

Shatner concluded his tribute by expressing his condolences to Stewart’s wife, Sunny Ozell, and his family, adding that the actor would be deeply missed.

Stewart became internationally recognised for playing Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation, taking over the captain’s chair after Shatner’s iconic portrayal of Kirk in the original series.

The two actors eventually shared the screen in Star Trek: Generations in 1994, bringing together the original and next-generation crews in a story that marked a passing of the torch between the franchise’s leading captains.

Other members of the Star Trek family also paid tribute to Stewart.

George Takei, who played Hikaru Sulu in the original series, described Stewart as a “true and irreplaceable legend” whose portrayal of Picard inspired a new generation of fans.

“As Captain Jean-Luc Picard, Patrick Stewart took the starship Enterprise to places it had never gone before,” Takei wrote. “He inspired a whole next generation of star-gazers who looked longingly ahead to a brighter future for all humanity.”

Stewart’s The Next Generation co-stars also shared messages of remembrance. Wil Wheaton, who played Wesley Crusher, posted a photograph with Stewart alongside the words “Godspeed, Captain”.

Jonathan Frakes, who portrayed William Riker, shared a photograph of Stewart and wrote, “Rest in peace, my friend.”

Akiva Goldsman, co-creator and co-showrunner of Star Trek: Picard, described Stewart as a remarkable performer whose portrayal of Picard had permanently expanded the Star Trek universe.

“Patrick was not only a true lion of the profession, he was the rarest of alchemists, one who could literally turn the written word into flesh and blood,” Goldsman said.

He added that Stewart was kind, strong, fiercely intelligent, collaborative, vulnerable and wise.

Stewart died following what his family described as a “brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia”. His family said he had been surrounded by loved ones, music, prayer, tears and laughter during his final days.

Beyond Star Trek, Stewart was also widely known for playing Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men films, with a career spanning more than six decades across television, film and theatre.

His death has prompted tributes from across the entertainment industry, with fellow actors and collaborators remembering both his extraordinary talent and the humanity he brought to his most celebrated roles.

headline: Sarah J. Maas' new 'ACOTAR' book smashes release-day record with 1.7 million copies sold
description: Sarah J. Maas' 'ACOTAR' Book 6 sells 1.7 million copies on release day, breaking the author's previous sales record
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Sarah J. Maas has achieved a major publishing milestone as the sixth instalment in her bestselling A Court of Thorns and Roses series sold 1.7 million copies on its release day.

Titled A Court of Splintered Harmony, the fantasy novel arrived on October 27 and broke the author's previous release-day sales record. According to Variety, the book's opening-day sales were 600% higher than those of A Court of Silver Flames, the fifth instalment, which debuted in 2021.

Publisher Bloomsbury confirmed that the 1.7 million figure includes preorders and first-day sales of English-language print and ebook editions across the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom and Australia. The total does not include audiobook sales or translated editions.

The impressive debut also puts A Court of Splintered Harmony on track to become the biggest book release of 2026.

Reacting to the achievement, Maas said she had been focused on the characters and stories while writing, adding that the overwhelming response from readers was difficult to comprehend. She also expressed gratitude for the support surrounding the latest release.

With the sixth book's success, Maas has now sold more than 100 million copies worldwide across her three fantasy franchises: A Court of Thorns and Roses, Throne of Glass and Crescent City.

The release was supported by an extensive promotional campaign, including merchandise collaborations with brands such as Funko and For Love & Lemons. Around 2,000 midnight launch events were also organised worldwide.

Meanwhile, fans will not have to wait long for the next instalment. A Court of Forgotten Melody, the seventh ACOTAR book, is scheduled for release on January 12. The upcoming novels form part of Maas' planned four-part Valkyrie Cycle storyline.

The franchise has also attracted television interest, although its previously announced Hulu adaptation was scrapped in February 2025.

article_html:
Sarah J. Maas has achieved a major publishing milestone as the sixth instalment in her bestselling A Court of Thorns and Roses series sold 1.7 million copies on its release day.

Titled A Court of Splintered Harmony, the fantasy novel arrived on October 27 and broke the author's previous release-day sales record. According to Variety, the book's opening-day sales were 600% higher than those of A Court of Silver Flames, the fifth instalment, which debuted in 2021.

Publisher Bloomsbury confirmed that the 1.7 million figure includes preorders and first-day sales of English-language print and ebook editions across the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom and Australia. The total does not include audiobook sales or translated editions.

The impressive debut also puts A Court of Splintered Harmony on track to become the biggest book release of 2026.

Reacting to the achievement, Maas said she had been focused on the characters and stories while writing, adding that the overwhelming response from readers was difficult to comprehend. She also expressed gratitude for the support surrounding the latest release.

With the sixth book's success, Maas has now sold more than 100 million copies worldwide across her three fantasy franchises: A Court of Thorns and Roses, Throne of Glass and Crescent City.

The release was supported by an extensive promotional campaign, including merchandise collaborations with brands such as Funko and For Love & Lemons. Around 2,000 midnight launch events were also organised worldwide.

Meanwhile, fans will not have to wait long for the next instalment. A Court of Forgotten Melody, the seventh ACOTAR book, is scheduled for release on January 12. The upcoming novels form part of Maas' planned four-part Valkyrie Cycle storyline.

The franchise has also attracted television interest, although its previously announced Hulu adaptation was scrapped in February 2025.

headline: Experts urge govts to treat manosphere and misogyny as public health issues: report
description: Call for education, mental health support and platform accountability to curb online misogyny and wider social harms
author: Life And Style Desk
article_text:
Online misogyny and the growing influence of the so-called manosphere should be addressed as a public health issue rather than treated solely as a problem of social media regulation, according to a new viewpoint published in The Lancet.

The authors argue that the online ecosystem, which includes communities promoting anti-feminist beliefs, male victimhood and hostile attitudes towards women, is contributing to a range of social and health-related harms. These include mental health difficulties among young people, violence against women and girls, and discouraging boys and men from seeking professional support.

The Lancet viewpoint describes the manosphere as a commercial network of online communities built around shared ideas about masculinity, misogyny and perceived male disadvantage. It argues that these spaces have become increasingly profitable, with platforms, influencers and content creators benefiting from material that attracts attention through controversy and outrage.

The researchers explain that the ecosystem includes groups such as incels, men's rights activists, pick-up artists and online influencers promoting particular ideals of masculinity. While these communities differ in their origins and beliefs, they share narratives that frequently portray feminism as responsible for men's difficulties.

The report also highlights how financial incentives encourage the spread of such content. Influencers and platforms generate revenue through advertising, paid subscriptions, online courses and products marketed to young men, often exploiting insecurities about appearance, relationships and financial success.

Professor Sarah Hawkes, one of the authors, told Sky News that restricting access to social media alone may not achieve the broader goal of making online environments safer.

“We want to raise the issue that just regulating or restricting access to social media of which the manosphere is part is likely to actually achieve the goals that we hopefully all want which is to make online spaces less toxic, to improve young people’s mental health, to absolutely reduce the violence amongst women and girls,” she said.

Hawkes argued that approaching the issue through public health policy would allow governments to consider interventions beyond restrictions on online content. “By seeing something as a public health problem, you open up a variety of policy leavers that are not available if not all you focus on is restriction and regulation,” she said.

The researchers draw comparisons with tobacco consumption, arguing that although the manosphere primarily targets men and boys, its consequences extend across society.

“It's like tobacco consumption. It is predominantly a male behaviour around the world. Five times more men than women smoke but the harm that is suffered on those who smoke, a lot of that is suffered through the women who live with the men who smoke,” Hawkes told Sky News.

She added that women and girls also experience the wider consequences of misogyny and gender inequality.

“That is exactly the same with the manosphere. While it is aiming to have its customer base for men and boys, the harms are experienced across the society, and particularly by women and girls who experience misogyny, gender inequality and literal violence,” she said.

The report identifies social isolation, economic insecurity, educational disengagement and loneliness as factors that can make some young men more receptive to online communities offering belonging and explanations for their difficulties. It cautions, however, that evidence establishing direct causal links between exposure to manosphere content and specific health outcomes remains limited.

The researchers argue that addressing these vulnerabilities requires more than removing harmful material. Their recommendations include improving access to mental health services for boys and young men, strengthening school-based education, promoting healthier representations of masculinity and making social media platforms more accountable for the content their algorithms amplify.

They also call for greater investment in research to monitor changing online communities and assess whether interventions are working. The authors stress that efforts must confront wider misogynistic attitudes and discrimination already present in society, rather than treating the manosphere as their sole source.

A day earlier, The Guardian highlighted the researchers' call for governments, schools, healthcare providers and community organisations to coordinate their response. It also reported Professor Hawkes's argument that boys need positive alternatives to these online spaces, rather than simply being told to avoid them.

The Lancet proposed investment in education, accessible mental health services, healthier representations of masculinity, platform accountability and research into the evolving online environment. Their central argument is that addressing online misogyny requires tackling the conditions that make such communities appealing, alongside the commercial systems that help them grow.

description: With fare negotiations and AI-powered safety, inDrive is advancing affordability, transparency and choice in Pakistan
article_text:
Pakistan’s ride-hailing market is evolving in 2026, with affordability, earning opportunities and safety shaping the experience for both passengers and drivers.

inDrive addresses these priorities through its peer-to-peer fare negotiation model, giving passengers and drivers greater control over pricing. The platform also uses AI-powered safety technologies designed to identify potential risks and support safer journeys.

Trusted by millions worldwide and ranked as the number-one ride-hailing app across app stores in Pakistan, inDrive combines pricing flexibility with technology-driven safety measures.

A Bidding Model That Gives Users More Control

Unlike platforms where fares are determined by automated pricing systems, inDrive allows passengers and drivers to negotiate directly. A recommended fare, calculated using live market data and updated every 30 minutes, provides a starting point.

Passengers can accept, adjust or decline the price, while drivers can accept, counter the offer or decline without penalties. Drivers can also view the destination before accepting a ride, helping them make informed decisions about the journeys they undertake.

The platform also focuses on driver earnings and flexibility. Its commission rate of 7% is the lowest in the country, allowing drivers to retain more of each fare. Flexible working hours accommodate both full-time drivers and those seeking supplementary income.

The driver loyalty programme offers additional perks, including discounts on electronics, laboratory tests and everyday products through partner businesses.

According to Oxford Economics data from January 2026, 59% of riders and 54% of drivers in Pakistan reported completing more rides because they could negotiate and agree on fares directly. These figures highlight the perceived value of fare negotiation for both sides.

AI-Powered Safety

Alongside pricing flexibility, inDrive is developing an AI-native safety ecosystem that combines identity verification, account activity, in-app communication and ride-related signals to help identify potential risks.

Driver onboarding includes document verification, facial comparison and vehicle inspection. Regular selfie verification and vehicle photo checks help confirm that the verified driver and registered vehicle are being used.

AI and machine learning also help detect duplicate accounts, suspicious account changes and prohibited content in chats. Potential violations can trigger additional checks or be referred to human specialists, who retain responsibility for critical decisions.

Practical safety features complement these systems. In-app calls and chat allow passengers and drivers to communicate without sharing personal phone numbers. An SOS button, trusted contacts, in-trip monitoring and live ride sharing provide additional ways to seek assistance and keep others informed.

According to inDrive’s internal analytics, 8.8 million users shared their rides with close contacts between April and September 2026, demonstrating the use of its ride-sharing safety feature.

Choice Reflects Local Needs

Passenger preferences further illustrate the importance of affordability in Pakistan. According to inDrive’s internal analytics, Moto accounts for almost half of riders nationwide, while Ride Mini is the second-most popular ride option. In Islamabad, more than 50% of riders use Ride Mini.

By combining negotiated fares, driver flexibility and AI-supported safety measures, inDrive is building a ride-hailing proposition centred on choice, transparency and safer journeys.

headline: Ray Nicholson reveals he was nearly in a coma after contracting dangerous infection
description: Ray Nicholson reveals how a near-fatal MRSA infection ended his football career and inspired him to pursue acting
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Ray Nicholson has revealed that a life-threatening infection nearly cost him his arm and brought his high school football career to an abrupt end before inspiring him to pursue acting.

The actor, 34, shared the experience during an interview with PEOPLE while discussing his latest film, The Mosquito Bowl, alongside co-star Tom Francis.

Nicholson recalled developing a staph infection that progressed into MRSA, a potentially serious bacterial infection, during his final football game in high school. The condition caused his arm to swell dramatically, leaving doctors concerned about the spread of the infection.

“My arm got so swollen up, they literally drew a line on my arm and were like, ‘If the infection gets past here, we have to cut off your arm,’” he said.

Nicholson also revealed that he lost approximately 50 pounds in a week and was nearly in a semi-coma during the ordeal. Following his recovery, the experience prompted him to reconsider his future and pursue a career in acting.

The son of actor Jack Nicholson and actress Rebecca Broussard had previously considered becoming a sports agent. Although football had given his life direction, he eventually realised that acting was what he had always wanted to do.

Nicholson made his screen debut in the 2006 comedy The Benchwarmers before pursuing acting more seriously in 2018. He later gained wider recognition through projects including Smile 2 in 2024.

His latest project, The Mosquito Bowl, sees him portray real-life American football player Tony Butkovich, who served as a US Marine during World War II. The film also stars Tom Francis, Bill Skarsgård and Nicholas Galitzine.

Nicholson described the opportunity to return to football through the role as a dream experience. The Mosquito Bowl arrives in theatres on October 30 and will begin streaming on Netflix on November 25.

headline: Tarek El Moussa defends $150K BMW gift for daughter Taylor’s 16th birthday
description: Tarek and ex-wife Christina Haack surprised their daughter with the BMW X5 in August ahead of her birthday
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Tarek El Moussa has defended his decision to buy his 16-year-old daughter, Taylor, a $150,000 BMW X5 for her birthday, saying the teenager earned the luxury gift through her academic and sporting achievements.

Speaking on Nicole Lapin’s Money Rehab podcast on October 28, the 45-year-old former Flip or Flop presenter explained that Taylor had achieved a 4.2 GPA and been named MVP of her freshman football team.

“She got a 4.2 GPA,” he said. “She was MVP of her freshman soccer team. She’s an absolutely fantastic kid and didn’t just get it; she actually earned it. And if you ask me, she deserved it because she worked really, really hard.”

Tarek, his wife Heather Rae El Moussa and his ex-wife Christina Haack surprised Taylor with the BMW in August, ahead of her September birthday.

He said the teenager had not requested an expensive vehicle and would have been happy with a “used Honda”.

Tarek added that safety was a major consideration behind the purchase. “That thing is built like a tank,” he said. “The biggest thing for me was safety. She’s in a safe car and she loves it.”

Addressing concerns that the gift could spoil his daughter, Tarek explained that Taylor had grown up around wealth but remained hardworking.

He also revealed that he had been teaching her financial literacy, including investing in stocks and real estate.

The surprise was organised by Tarek, Heather and Christina, who shared footage of Taylor's emotional reaction on Instagram.

Tarek El Moussa has defended his decision to buy his 16-year-old daughter, Taylor, a $150,000 BMW X5 for her birthday, saying the teenager earned the luxury gift through her academic and sporting achievements.

Speaking on Nicole Lapin’s Money Rehab podcast on October 28, the 45-year-old former Flip or Flop presenter explained that Taylor had achieved a 4.2 GPA and been named MVP of her freshman football team.

“She got a 4.2 GPA,” he said. “She was MVP of her freshman soccer team. She’s an absolutely fantastic kid and didn’t just get it; she actually earned it. And if you ask me, she deserved it because she worked really, really hard.”

Tarek, his wife Heather Rae El Moussa and his ex-wife Christina Haack surprised Taylor with the BMW in August, ahead of her September birthday.

He said the teenager had not requested an expensive vehicle and would have been happy with a “used Honda”.

Tarek added that safety was a major consideration behind the purchase. “That thing is built like a tank,” he said. “The biggest thing for me was safety. She’s in a safe car and she loves it.”

Addressing concerns that the gift could spoil his daughter, Tarek explained that Taylor had grown up around wealth but remained hardworking.

He also revealed that he had been teaching her financial literacy, including investing in stocks and real estate.

The surprise was organised by Tarek, Heather and Christina, who shared footage of Taylor's emotional reaction on Instagram.

headline: Pakistan set to feature in Youth Olympics
description: Four athletes to represent the country in athletics and swimming at Dakar Games
author: Sports Desk
article_text:
Pakistan is set to field a five-member contingent, including four athletes, in the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Senegal, with the competition scheduled to run from October 31 to November 13.

Pakistan Olympic Association (POA) announced the contingent on Friday after the International Olympic Committee (IOC) allocated Pakistan quota places in athletics and swimming.

Pakistan will be represented by Shahzain Safdar in athletics, while Hareem Malik and Syed Muhammad Daniyal Hatim will compete in swimming. Safdar will be accompanied by athletics coach Rehan Yousaf.

Lt Col (retd) Ahmed Ali Khan has been named Chef de Mission and will lead the national contingent at the Games.

According to the POA, Pakistan received one male quota place in athletics and two swimming places, one each for male and female athletes, through allocations made by the IOC.

The athletes' nominations were reviewed and vetted by the respective international federations in line with the age limits and eligibility requirements for participation in the event.

The Dakar Games, scheduled to take place in Senegal, will provide young athletes from across the world with an opportunity to compete on an international stage and gain experience in a multi-sport event.

The POA said Pakistan's participation reflected the IOC's commitment to providing athletes from all National Olympic Committees with opportunities to take part in events within the Olympic Movement.

The association expressed confidence that the contingent would uphold the values of sportsmanship, discipline and integrity while representing the country.

Contingent: Lt Col (retd) Ahmed Ali Khan (chef de mission), Hareem Malik (swimmer), Syed Muhammad Daniyal Hatim (swimmer), Shahzain Safdar (athlete), Rehan Yousaf (athlete)

headline: PTI K-P division dispels impression of internal discord
description: Demands access to Imran Khan and his ‘authentic’ medical records
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Parliamentary Party on Friday rejected reports of internal divisions, declaring that there was no grouping within the party.

The declaration came at a meeting of the provincial parliamentary party, attended by a majority of its members, with Barrister PTI Chairman Gohar Ali Khan, Provincial General Secretary Ali Asghar Khan and Acting Provincial President Noorul Haq Qadri participating on special invitation.

In a statement issued after the meeting, the parliamentary party said, “The parliamentary party expressed complete confidence in the leadership of Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and clarified that there is no grouping of any kind in Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf. All political and organisational matters of the party will be advanced in the light of the instructions of Founder Chairman Imran Khan, mutual consultation, and collective decisions.”

A day earlier, PTI central secretariat ruled out any change in the office of the K-P chief minister, reaffirming that Sohail Afridi would continue to hold the position with the support of party founder Imran Khan.

Emergency and governor’s rule were declared in K-P on October 11 after the talks between the government and opposition failed. On the same day, reports emerged that Afridi had been detained as the long march initiated on October 4 progressed and was on its way to Swabi. Since then, intraparty rifts have emerged, leading to PTI leaders exchanging barbs online.

Former K-P chief minister Ali Amin Gandapur and PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja tore each other apart on social media. Raja warned of attempts by “undemocratic decision-makers” to undermine internal consensus, while Gandapur demanded that the party secretary general substantiate his allegations or apologise.

The latest statement appears to aim at dispelling the perception of intraparty differences.

According to the statement issued by PTI K-P on X, the meeting also decided that the provincial parliamentary party would be given effective representation in any future protest movement, negotiations or political strategy.

It stressed that previous decisions reached through consensus by the provincial parliamentary party must be respected.

The participants discussed the prevailing political, constitutional and administrative situation in the province, as well as issues confronting the party leadership and workers.

The meeting strongly opposed the imposition of governor's rule and emergency in K-P, terming the measures contrary to the public mandate, democratic principles and constitutional requirements.

It vowed to challenge the move through constitutional, legal, judicial and political forums.

The parliamentary party also condemned what it described as political victimisation in the guise of counterterrorism measures, including raids on workers' homes, arrests, detentions under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) and the removal of PTI flags and signboards from development projects.

“These actions be immediately stopped and that political workers be provided with their constitutional and legal rights,” it demanded.

Expressing “grave concern” over Imran's health, the meeting demanded authentic information about his medical condition, immediate access to him and meetings for his family members and lawyers.

Imran and Bushra remain incarcerated in Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail. They were sentenced on December 20, 2025, to 17 years in prison in the Toshakhana-II case, while in January last year, an Islamabad accountability court sentenced Imran to 14 years and Bushra to seven years in prison in the £190 million case.

It also voiced “serious” concern over the detention of his wife and sisters, calling for the provision of medical facilities and legal rights, justice for his wife and the release of his sisters.

Two days earlier, Noreen Niazi, 70, was admitted to Lahore's Punjab Institute of Cardiology following a deterioration in her health while in custody, according to her legal counsel. He claimed that the patient's family was neither informed nor granted access to her during the treatment. Imran's sisters Noreen and Dr Uzma were detained on September 21, a day after their sister Aleema Khan was also held under Section 3 of the Punjab MPO Ordinance, 1960, ahead of the planned PTI long march towards Islamabad. The detention was later extended on October 7 for another 30 days.

The statement further condemned what it termed unconstitutional detention or arrest of Afridi, the provincial assembly speaker and other elected representatives, demanding their immediate release and restoration of their political activities.

The meeting also expressed reservations over the imposition of emergency and transfer of administrative powers in 12 districts, including the merged tribal districts.

It opposed any attempt to reverse the administrative integration of the former tribal areas and decided to convene a joint jirga (meeting) of tribal elders and representatives of other political parties to formulate a mutually agreed strategy against the move.

The parliamentary party also expressed resolve to hold its meetings regularly and continue its struggle for the protection of public rights, safeguarding development projects, respect for the public mandate, constitutional supremacy and restoration of the democratic system.

PPP urged to clarify position on governor’s rule, emergency in K-P

Separately, PTI lawmaker Asad Qaiser, while speaking in the National Assembly, questioned how Governor’s Rule and an emergency could operate simultaneously in different areas of the same province, arguing that both measures were governed by constitutional provisions and required clarity regarding their implementation.

The lawmaker also sought clarification on the legal authority under which a committee had been constituted following the imposition of the emergency, asking whether any specific law provided for its formation.

On October 17, the federal government formally notified the establishment of the 48-member Area Representative and Development Council (ARDC) across 12 districts of K-P as the governor consolidated his rule in the province.

The official notification named 48 members drawn from the tribal and adjacent districts, with Shaukatullah Khan of the Tarkani tribe from Bajaur district appointed as chairman and Malik Khan Marjan of the Wazir tribe from North Waziristan named vice chairman.

The federal government imposed emergency and governor's rule in K-P under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, which suspended the PTI-led provincial administration and transferred executive authority to Governor Faisal Karim Kundi. On October 15, a joint session of the Parliament adopted two separate resolutions ratifying the presidential proclamations imposing a state of emergency and governor's rule for two months in K-P amid opposition uproar.

Citing remarks by senior Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) leader and former chairman of the Senate Farooq Hamid Naek, the PTI lawmaker alleged that Naek had described the emergency and the committee formed under it as “unconstitutional”.

The MPA highlighted that the governor of K-P was affiliated with the PPP and had taken ownership of the action.

He called on the PPP to elaborate its position, saying: “They should clarify their policy. We believe this is against the spirit of democracy.”

Qaiser also questioned whether Parliament would adopt a resolution against what he termed an unconstitutional action.

The declaration came at a meeting of the provincial parliamentary party, attended by a majority of its members, with Barrister PTI Chairman Gohar Ali Khan, Provincial General Secretary Ali Asghar Khan and Acting Provincial President Noorul Haq Qadri participating on special invitation.

In a statement issued after the meeting, the parliamentary party said, “The parliamentary party expressed complete confidence in the leadership of Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and clarified that there is no grouping of any kind in Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf. All political and organisational matters of the party will be advanced in the light of the instructions of Founder Chairman Imran Khan, mutual consultation, and collective decisions.”

Read: PTI throws weight behind suspended K-P chief minister, says Afridi has Imran’s backing

A day earlier, PTI central secretariat ruled out any change in the office of the K-P chief minister, reaffirming that Sohail Afridi would continue to hold the position with the support of party founder Imran Khan.

Emergency and governor’s rule were declared in K-P on October 11 after the talks between the government and opposition failed. On the same day, reports emerged that Afridi had been detained as the long march initiated on October 4 progressed and was on its way to Swabi. Since then, intraparty rifts have emerged, leading to PTI leaders exchanging barbs online.

Former K-P chief minister Ali Amin Gandapur and PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja tore each other apart on social media. Raja warned of attempts by “undemocratic decision-makers” to undermine internal consensus, while Gandapur demanded that the party secretary general substantiate his allegations or apologise.

The latest statement appears to aim at dispelling the perception of intraparty differences.

According to the statement issued by PTI K-P on X, the meeting also decided that the provincial parliamentary party would be given effective representation in any future protest movement, negotiations or political strategy.

It stressed that previous decisions reached through consensus by the provincial parliamentary party must be respected.

The participants discussed the prevailing political, constitutional and administrative situation in the province, as well as issues confronting the party leadership and workers.

— PTI Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (@PTIKPOfficial) October 30, 2026

The meeting strongly opposed the imposition of governor's rule and emergency in K-P, terming the measures contrary to the public mandate, democratic principles and constitutional requirements.

It vowed to challenge the move through constitutional, legal, judicial and political forums.

The parliamentary party also condemned what it described as political victimisation in the guise of counterterrorism measures, including raids on workers' homes, arrests, detentions under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) and the removal of PTI flags and signboards from development projects.

“These actions be immediately stopped and that political workers be provided with their constitutional and legal rights,” it demanded.

Expressing “grave concern” over Imran's health, the meeting demanded authentic information about his medical condition, immediate access to him and meetings for his family members and lawyers.

Imran and Bushra remain incarcerated in Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail. They were sentenced on December 20, 2025, to 17 years in prison in the Toshakhana-II case, while in January last year, an Islamabad accountability court sentenced Imran to 14 years and Bushra to seven years in prison in the £190 million case.

It also voiced “serious” concern over the detention of his wife and sisters, calling for the provision of medical facilities and legal rights, justice for his wife and the release of his sisters.

Two days earlier, Noreen Niazi, 70, was admitted to Lahore's Punjab Institute of Cardiology following a deterioration in her health while in custody, according to her legal counsel. He claimed that the patient's family was neither informed nor granted access to her during the treatment. Imran's sisters Noreen and Dr Uzma were detained on September 21, a day after their sister Aleema Khan was also held under Section 3 of the Punjab MPO Ordinance, 1960, ahead of the planned PTI long march towards Islamabad. The detention was later extended on October 7 for another 30 days.

Read more: Govt will try to ensure Noreen’s relatives can visit her, Rana Sanaullah says

The statement further condemned what it termed unconstitutional detention or arrest of Afridi, the provincial assembly speaker and other elected representatives, demanding their immediate release and restoration of their political activities.

The meeting also expressed reservations over the imposition of emergency and transfer of administrative powers in 12 districts, including the merged tribal districts.

It opposed any attempt to reverse the administrative integration of the former tribal areas and decided to convene a joint jirga (meeting) of tribal elders and representatives of other political parties to formulate a mutually agreed strategy against the move.

The parliamentary party also expressed resolve to hold its meetings regularly and continue its struggle for the protection of public rights, safeguarding development projects, respect for the public mandate, constitutional supremacy and restoration of the democratic system.

PPP urged to clarify position on governor’s rule, emergency in K-P

Separately, PTI lawmaker Asad Qaiser, while speaking in the National Assembly, questioned how Governor’s Rule and an emergency could operate simultaneously in different areas of the same province, arguing that both measures were governed by constitutional provisions and required clarity regarding their implementation.

The lawmaker also sought clarification on the legal authority under which a committee had been constituted following the imposition of the emergency, asking whether any specific law provided for its formation.

On October 17, the federal government formally notified the establishment of the 48-member Area Representative and Development Council (ARDC) across 12 districts of K-P as the governor consolidated his rule in the province.

The official notification named 48 members drawn from the tribal and adjacent districts, with Shaukatullah Khan of the Tarkani tribe from Bajaur district appointed as chairman and Malik Khan Marjan of the Wazir tribe from North Waziristan named vice chairman.

The federal government imposed emergency and governor's rule in K-P under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, which suspended the PTI-led provincial administration and transferred executive authority to Governor Faisal Karim Kundi. On October 15, a joint session of the Parliament adopted two separate resolutions ratifying the presidential proclamations imposing a state of emergency and governor's rule for two months in K-P amid opposition uproar.

Citing remarks by senior Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) leader and former chairman of the Senate Farooq Hamid Naek, the PTI lawmaker alleged that Naek had described the emergency and the committee formed under it as “unconstitutional”.

headline: 'Ghosts' star Asher Grodman teases high-stakes Christmas special after Pete's return
description: Asher Grodman reacts to Pete's major memory-loss twist in 'Ghosts' season 6 and teases the upcoming Christmas special
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Ghosts star Asher Grodman has shared his reaction to the surprising return of Pete in the season 6 Halloween special, revealing how the character's unexpected memory loss could shape the show's upcoming episodes.

The Halloween special, which aired on CBS on October 30, marked the return of Richie Moriarty's Pete after his disappearance in the season 5 finale. However, his comeback came with an unexpected complication: Pete has lost his memories of the past 40 years as a ghost.

Speaking to PEOPLE, Grodman, who plays Trevor, said the development creates interesting possibilities for the series, particularly because of the relationships among the eight ghosts.

At the end of the special, Pete reappears at Woodstone Manor on the anniversary of his death but appears unaware of the experiences and friendships he has developed since becoming a ghost.

Grodman described the storyline as an opportunity to explore how the other characters respond to someone who is physically present but has lost his shared history with them. He also confirmed that Pete's memory loss will continue when the show returns with its Christmas special in December.

The upcoming one-hour episode will feature a storyline inspired by the action film Die Hard. Grodman revealed that Trevor will play an important role in both the trouble and its resolution, teasing a high-stakes instalment that will show some characters in unfamiliar situations.

Meanwhile, season 6 marks another milestone for the CBS comedy, which is expected to reach its 100th episode in 2027.

Grodman expressed gratitude for the show's continued success, describing the production as a collaborative and enjoyable experience.

Ghosts season 6 returns in December with its Christmas special on CBS. Seasons 1 through 5 and the Halloween special are currently available on Paramount+.

headline: FBI and US Secret Service working with Binance after $6.3 billion hack, source says
description: North Korean hackers targeted Binance wallets across 10 blockchains, stealing funds in 20 minutes
author: Reuters
article_text:
Binance is ‌working with law enforcement around the world, including the Federal ​Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and ​the United States Secret Service (USSS), ⁠after hackers stole a ​record $6.3 billion from the platform, ​a person familiar with the situation told Reuters.

The FBI said in ​a statement that it ​was "aware of the incident and is engaged ‌with ⁠relevant public and private partners to understand the scope of the activity, evaluate ​potential impacts, ​and ⁠coordinate appropriate investigative steps."

The USSS did not ​respond to a request ​for ⁠comment sent via email outside of US hours.

Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, in what analysts say is the biggest crypto hack ever, an attack that could prompt investors to rethink the risks of ​owning digital assets.

The hackers behind the raid were from North Korea, according to US blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis. The attackers targeted Binance wallets on 10 blockchains and shifted most ‌of the funds in about 20 minutes, TRM Labs said in a statement.

headline: Alison Hammond breaks silence on 22-year age gap with boyfriend David Putman
description: Alison Hammond tells critics to mind their business as she addresses her 22-year age gap with boyfriend David Putman.
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
The Great British Baking Show host Alison Hammond has addressed criticism of her relationship with boyfriend David Putman, telling people to stop worrying about their 22-year age difference.

The 51-year-old presenter discussed her relationship with Putman, 29, in a new interview with Attitude. When asked what she would say to people who question their age gap, Hammond had a straightforward response: “Mind your business!”

She explained that people should focus less on other people’s relationships, arguing that two consenting adults should be free to enjoy their lives together if they are happy and respect each other.

“If two consenting adults are happy, loved, respected and making each other laugh, what exactly is the problem?” she said.

Hammond also addressed the term “cougar”, pointing out what she sees as a double standard surrounding age-gap relationships. She noted that men who date younger women are often praised, while women in similar relationships receive different labels.

The presenter added that she sometimes finds the criticism amusing, joking that she is not a cougar but “a whole safari!”

Hammond encouraged women to enjoy their relationships without worrying about public opinion. She also said the differences between her and Putman make their relationship interesting, describing their dynamic as a combination of her life experience and his youth.

According to Hammond, one of the things she appreciates most about their relationship is their ability to make each other laugh.

The presenter has hosted The Great British Baking Show alongside Noel Fielding since 2023. The show's 14th collection premiered on Netflix on September 25, following its UK debut as The Great British Bake Off on September 22.

Hammond also presents ITV's This Morning.

headline: CDA gives Fazlur Rehman's residence 15 days to remove alleged encroachments
description: Notice lists security guards' posts, generator and additional kitchen among the violations at JUI-F chief's residence
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Friday issued an encroachment notice at the residence of Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, identifying illegal constructions and encroachments on its land and directing their removal within 15 days.

The notice came amid an escalating war of words between the government and Fazl, who had criticised what he described as the government's misuse of the Constitution. Federal ministers hit back a day earlier, accusing the JUI-F chief of overlooking his own role in forming and toppling governments.

Pasted at the residence, the notice directed the removal of security guards' cabins and a generator installed on CDA land. It also identified additional construction, including a kitchen built within the premises, as a violation of building regulations.

The authority gave 15 days for the identified violations to be removed, warning that failure to comply could result in the building being sealed or the unauthorised structures being demolished.

The notice was issued to Amanullah, son of Muhammad Younis, whom it identified as the building's owner. It also stated that the CDA had previously directed the removal of encroachments from the residence on March 18, 2019.

Meanwhile, Fazl's son and JUI-F leader Maulana Asjad Mahmood described the action as retaliatory, linking it to his father's political differences with the government.

In a statement, Mahmood said the retaliatory measures had begun after encroachments were pointed out to the Peshawar corps commander. "When no response was received to the issue being raised, opponents resorted to cheap tactics," he said.

He added that objections had also been raised over the removal of a security guard's cabin, the relocation of the generator and the construction of an additional kitchen.

Mahmood alleged that state institutions were being used to fulfil the personal desire for revenge of one individual. "Turning political differences into personal vendettas is a matter of concern," he said, urging the public and JUI-F workers to remain informed and vigilant about the situation.

Talal says CDA anti-encroachment drive under way for a year

Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry on Friday described the Capital Development Authority’s (CDA) action against alleged encroachments at JUI-F chief’s residence as routine, saying the campaign against illegal constructions had been under way for more than a year.

“Action against encroachments and illegal constructions in Islamabad has not started now, a few weeks ago or even a few months ago. It has been under way for more than a year, and the posh sectors of Islamabad were the first to be targeted,” he said while speaking to a private television channel.

He regretted that the matter was being used to secure political gains, saying the CDA had been taking action against encroachments and illegal constructions in Islamabad for over a year, beginning with the city's posh sectors.

Chaudhry said notices had been issued to all property owners whose premises had security cabins, generators or illegal constructions on green areas.

The minister added that the government had also removed unauthorised security deployments from public spaces, including green belts.

He said the authorities were taking action against illegal structures without discrimination, regardless of the individuals or organisations involved.

He cited the demolition of a wall belonging to a five-storey building constructed on government land on security grounds as another example of the campaign.

Chaudhry said the notice concerning Molana Fazl's residence had been issued in the name of Amanullah, adding that he did not know why the JUI-F chief was living there or what arrangement existed between the two.

“Defending illegal constructions is unbecoming of any political or religious leader,” he said, adding that the operation against encroachments would continue until all illegal structures were removed.

The latest exchange came amid growing tensions between the government and opposition leaders over the political and security situation in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa.

Following the imposition of governor’s rule in K-P, Fazl, who had been tasked by both the PTI and the government with mediating between the two sides, accused the government of backtracking on the negotiations, saying the PTI had agreed to the proposed terms while categorically opposing the imposition of governor's rule.

In return, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi took a swipe at the JUI-F chief over his opposition to the imposition of governor's rule in the province, suggesting that the religious-political leader was unhappy at not being offered a role in the new provincial setup.

Other government figures, including Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, also assailed his stance, with allegations that he was supporting people accused of backing terrorism.

Federal ministers once again took to task the JUI-F chief on October 18, accusing Fazl of politicising the security situation and opposing measures they said were intended to combat terrorism.

Responding to the allegations, Fazl described the remarks as character assassination and maintained that his criticism was directed at government policies rather than state institutions. He then called for parliament to hold an in-camera session to examine the country's counterterrorism strategy.

The tensions further escalated earlier this week when Fazl criticised Asif in the NA, questioning the government's role in discussions related to the Makkah defence pact in Tehran while the prime minister and defence minister remained in Pakistan.

A day later, Naqvi and Asif unleashed a barrage of criticism on the JUI-F chief for remarks about Asif's absence from talks in Tehran, saying no defence agreement was being negotiated there.

article_html:
The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Friday issued an encroachment notice at the residence of Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, identifying illegal constructions and encroachments on its land and directing their removal within 15 days.

The notice came amid an escalating war of words between the government and Fazl, who had criticised what he described as the government's misuse of the Constitution. Federal ministers hit back a day earlier, accusing the JUI-F chief of overlooking his own role in forming and toppling governments.

Pasted at the residence, the notice directed the removal of security guards' cabins and a generator installed on CDA land. It also identified additional construction, including a kitchen built within the premises, as a violation of building regulations.

The authority gave 15 days for the identified violations to be removed, warning that failure to comply could result in the building being sealed or the unauthorised structures being demolished.

The notice was issued to Amanullah, son of Muhammad Younis, whom it identified as the building's owner. It also stated that the CDA had previously directed the removal of encroachments from the residence on March 18, 2019.

Meanwhile, Fazl's son and JUI-F leader Maulana Asjad Mahmood described the action as retaliatory, linking it to his father's political differences with the government.

In a statement, Mahmood said the retaliatory measures had begun after encroachments were pointed out to the Peshawar corps commander. "When no response was received to the issue being raised, opponents resorted to cheap tactics," he said.

He added that objections had also been raised over the removal of a security guard's cabin, the relocation of the generator and the construction of an additional kitchen.

Mahmood alleged that state institutions were being used to fulfil the personal desire for revenge of one individual. "Turning political differences into personal vendettas is a matter of concern," he said, urging the public and JUI-F workers to remain informed and vigilant about the situation.

Talal says CDA anti-encroachment drive under way for a year

Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry on Friday described the Capital Development Authority’s (CDA) action against alleged encroachments at JUI-F chief’s residence as routine, saying the campaign against illegal constructions had been under way for more than a year.

“Action against encroachments and illegal constructions in Islamabad has not started now, a few weeks ago or even a few months ago. It has been under way for more than a year, and the posh sectors of Islamabad were the first to be targeted,” he said while speaking to a private television channel.

He regretted that the matter was being used to secure political gains, saying the CDA had been taking action against encroachments and illegal constructions in Islamabad for over a year, beginning with the city's posh sectors.

Chaudhry said notices had been issued to all property owners whose premises had security cabins, generators or illegal constructions on green areas.

The minister added that the government had also removed unauthorised security deployments from public spaces, including green belts.

He said the authorities were taking action against illegal structures without discrimination, regardless of the individuals or organisations involved.

He cited the demolition of a wall belonging to a five-storey building constructed on government land on security grounds as another example of the campaign.

Chaudhry said the notice concerning Molana Fazl's residence had been issued in the name of Amanullah, adding that he did not know why the JUI-F chief was living there or what arrangement existed between the two.

“Defending illegal constructions is unbecoming of any political or religious leader,” he said, adding that the operation against encroachments would continue until all illegal structures were removed.

The latest exchange came amid growing tensions between the government and opposition leaders over the political and security situation in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa.

Read More: Fazl calls for new Charter of Democracy

Following the imposition of governor’s rule in K-P, Fazl, who had been tasked by both the PTI and the government with mediating between the two sides, accused the government of backtracking on the negotiations, saying the PTI had agreed to the proposed terms while categorically opposing the imposition of governor's rule.

In return, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi took a swipe at the JUI-F chief over his opposition to the imposition of governor's rule in the province, suggesting that the religious-political leader was unhappy at not being offered a role in the new provincial setup.

Other government figures, including Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, also assailed his stance, with allegations that he was supporting people accused of backing terrorism.

Federal ministers once again took to task the JUI-F chief on October 18, accusing Fazl of politicising the security situation and opposing measures they said were intended to combat terrorism.

Also Read: PTI, TTAP affirm 'full support' for Fazl after govt hammering in Parliament

Responding to the allegations, Fazl described the remarks as character assassination and maintained that his criticism was directed at government policies rather than state institutions. He then called for parliament to hold an in-camera session to examine the country's counterterrorism strategy.

The tensions further escalated earlier this week when Fazl criticised Asif in the NA, questioning the government's role in discussions related to the Makkah defence pact in Tehran while the prime minister and defence minister remained in Pakistan.

A day later, Naqvi and Asif unleashed a barrage of criticism on the JUI-F chief for remarks about Asif's absence from talks in Tehran, saying no defence agreement was being negotiated there.

headline: Meta, TikTok, X lose legal challenge against UK watchdog over online safety data demands
description: 2023 law imposes tougher content standards on TikTok, X and Meta to protect children online
author: Reuters
article_text:
TikTok and X lost a legal challenge against British regulator Ofcom on ‌Friday over information requests made under the Online Safety Act, in one of the first tests of Britain's nascent online safety regime.

The case is one of several brought over parts of the 2023 act, which ​sets tougher standards for platforms such as TikTok, X and Meta's Facebook and Instagram ​with the aim of protecting particularly children from harmful and illegal content.

Friday's ⁠decision by London's High Court is a boost for Ofcom, though a potentially more significant ​ruling on Meta's separate case about how Ofcom calculates fees and potential fines is awaited.

Meta, which is ​also challenging Ofcom over the categorisation of WhatsApp in the new regime, was made the subject of Ofcom's first formal investigation under the Online Safety Act earlier this month.

X did not immediately respond to requests for comment. ​TikTok said it is considering the judgment, while a spokesperson for Meta said in a ​statement: "We're disappointed with the court's decision, but we and others across industry pursued this challenge because information-gathering of ‌this ⁠scale goes beyond what is necessary or proportionate."

Ofcom requested metrices from Meta, Tiktok, X

Ofcom has been gradually implementing the Online Safety Act regime, with its requirements backed up by the threat of fines of up to 10% of a company's global turnover for the most serious breaches.

The ​regulator issued information notices ​to Meta, TikTok ⁠and X in February, requesting detailed content moderation metrics including data on how many posts were removed or had visibility restricted, and how many ​users were exposed to harmful content.

Meta, TikTok and X argued the ​notices create ⁠unprecedented regulatory burdens, with X claiming that what it described as "the most burdensome information request X has received from any regulator" would cost it millions of pounds.

But their case was dismissed by the ⁠High ​Court, which in its ruling rejected their arguments that ​the information requests were disproportionate.

An Ofcom spokesperson welcomed the ruling, saying that "gathering information from companies is fundamental to our ability ​to do our job".

headline: Asia chip firms see strong AI demand; market jitters continue
description: Company forecasts 87% rise in operating profit to 1.17 trillion yen on strong chip equipment demand
author: Reuters
article_text:
Asian chip supply chain companies said on Friday ‌that AI-related demand remained strong, while investor concerns persisted over whether the massive investments in AI infrastructure would generate adequate returns.

Foxconn Chairman Young Liu told reporters at a company event that AI was not in a bubble and demand for AI products remained clear. ​The contract electronics maker is Nvidia's biggest AI server maker and Apple's top iPhone assembler.

Alphabet, Intel ​and Amazon all fell overnight due to market concerns over whether returns will justify continued ⁠high capital expenditure. The caution spread to Asia on Friday, with technology stocks, including South Korea's SK Hynix, ​Taiwan's TSMC and Japan's Advantest, coming under pressure.

"In the various conversations we are having with our customers, interest is very ​strong," Tokyo Electron Chief Financial Officer Hiroshi Kawamoto told reporters at a briefing about the company's half-yearly results.

The company, on Friday, forecast a stronger-than-expected 87% jump in operating profit to 1.17 trillion yen ($7.41 billion), underscoring robust demand for chipmaking equipment.

"At present, there are ​no signs that this is slowing down," he said.

Despite concerns about AI-related spending, Asian suppliers of chips and chipmaking ​equipment continue to report strong results. SK Hynix said this week it would return about $75 billion to shareholders as higher memory ‌prices boost ⁠profits.

On Friday Japanese memory chip maker Kioxia announced an interim dividend of 90 yen per share with excess cash to be used for shareholder returns from the second half of the fiscal year onwards.

The chipmaker forecasts non-GAAP operating profit of 2 trillion yen for the third quarter. Its shares have slide heavily from a peak in June.

Demand ​growth for AI will certainly ​continue although the rate ⁠may vary, said Rick Tsai, CEO of Taiwan chip designer MediaTek .

"Doubts over the Anthropic IPO, AI financing and wider AI adoption are holding back investors," said David Gibson ​of MST Financial.

"It will take time to fix this week's selloff."

Tokyo Electron, a major ​supplier of equipment ⁠for processes such as deposition and etching to chipmakers, said it would spend up to 150 billion yen to buy back some 25 million shares. Its shares closed down 5% ahead of earnings.

In China, CXMT said it swung to a ⁠net profit ​for the quarter due to higher memory prices. The chipmaker became ​China's most valuable listed company in July after its shares surged by more than five times in their Shanghai debut.

headline: K-P govt says evidence being gathered against Sohail Afridi over alleged corruption
description: Samar Bilour briefs media on corruption probe, school repairs, and law and order
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Adviser to the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa government on Information and Public Relations, Samar Haroon Bilour, has said that the dysfunctional Chief Minister Sohail Afridi remains in protective custody, while evidence is being collected in connection with allegations of corruption involving billions of rupees.

Speaking at a press conference at the Information Cell in the Civil Secretariat on Friday, she said the government was pursuing institutional reforms, transparency and improved public service delivery.

Responding to questions about Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, she described him as a senior and respected politician but said his recent statements appeared to reflect political frustration and resentment over being excluded from decision-making.

She suggested that the absence of the political role he expected in the current technocratic setup might also be contributing to his dissatisfaction. However, she said the government would welcome his constructive suggestions and guidance.

Regarding the Dir Colony tragedy in Peshawar, Bilour said investigations into the incident had been completed and a detailed report would soon be shared with the media. Inspections of government and private schools and seminaries across the province had identified 4,049 educational institutions requiring repairs and rehabilitation.

A comprehensive plan was being prepared to improve these institutions. Students from affected schools would be shifted to nearby government schools, with arrangements for class-wise adjustments and second shifts wherever necessary to ensure continuity of education.

She said a subcommittee was also examining the responsibilities of relevant departments and tehsil municipal administrations to determine whether negligence had occurred in building approvals, inspections and supervision.

On law and order, she said eight modern armoured vehicles had been handed over to the provincial police. A comprehensive plan to improve police infrastructure and operational capacity would be prepared within the next five to six weeks. Paying tribute to police personnel who had sacrificed their lives in the war against terrorism, she said providing modern equipment and resources to the force was the government's responsibility.

The adviser said internal irregularities in the Sehat Card programme were being examined, but there was no intention to discontinue or abolish it. The performance and administrative affairs of Medical Teaching Institutions (MTIs), along with the professional competence of their governing boards, would also be reviewed.

On the anti-encroachment campaign, she said illegal occupation of government land, green belts and drainage channels had to be eliminated to address Peshawar’s traffic and sewage problems. The operation was continuing without discrimination, and no one was being granted concessions on political or personal recommendations. Cleared areas would subsequently be rehabilitated and beautified for public use.

The advisor further added that sanitation services in Peshawar were improving, with cleaning staff working late into the night to remove accumulated waste. A comprehensive waste collection plan was also being developed, alongside measures to address shortages of manhole covers and dustbins.

Concluding, Bilour said the government’s vision was not merely a slogan but a commitment to good governance, institutional reforms, accountability, transparency and public service. She said the government would continue pursuing these priorities while protecting the province’s interests through responsible conduct and institutional procedures.
