headline: Punjab eyes exports, jobs boom
description: Punjab eyes exports, jobs boom
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif on Friday launched the first Punjab Innovation for Value, Opportunity and Transformation (PIVOT) programme, along with a portal as part of a three-year economic transformation plan aimed at boosting investment, exports and employment.

The programme envisages government investment of around Rs1.089 trillion and private sector Rs906 billion, with an expected increase of $6.8b in exports and the creation of 162,000 jobs.

The government estimates that the initiative will improve the quality of life of one million people over the next three years.

Addressing the launch ceremony, attended by State Bank Governor Jameel Ahmad, members of the Pakistan Business Council and prominent industrialists and investors, the CM said PIVOT would drive economic transformation across the industry, agriculture, tourism, skills development and technology sectors.

She said the plan, covering 2026-29, was designed to expand economic opportunities, industrial capacity, investment and export-led growth.

Under the initiative, Rs753.7b has been allocated to strengthen Punjab's industrial sector, while a target has been set to train 402,060 people.

The programme also envisages concessional loans worth Rs300b for industrial projects at interest rates ranging up to five per cent.

The chief minister said the plan would address challenges facing businesses, including limited access to finance, industrial infrastructure and skills, regulatory hurdles and high energy costs.

The planned measures include machinery duty refunds and support for solar and battery energy storage systems.

Four agro-processing parks will be established in Sargodha, Khanewal, Okara and Bhakkar to promote fruit processing, cold storage, grading and other value-added activities. The initiative is expected to improve farmers' access to markets and strengthen agricultural value chains.

Modern farm mechanisation, storage facilities, meat and dairy processing, disease prevention and financial support for farmers are also part of the plan.

It will also focus on manufacturing sectors such as garments, sports goods, leather and footwear, pharmaceuticals, fans and ceramics.

The chief minister said aquaculture projects would promote shrimp farming, fisheries infrastructure and export-oriented production.

Tourism development is another component with investment opportunities planned around historical and religious sites, Lahore's night-time economy, the Potohar region, Cholistan and other attractions.

The skills and technology component aims to equip youth with expertise matching domestic and international demands. It includes digital skills training, information technology internships, internationally recognised certifications, start-up incubation and entrepreneurship support.

The chief minister said economic reforms under the programme would cover public-private partnerships, industrial land policy and business-friendly labour regulations.

She stressed that investor facilitation and transparent monitoring would be central to ensuring effective implementation.

Addressing the launch ceremony of the innovation, entrepreneurship and technology initiative, the chief minister said more than 1,200 start'ups were operating in Punjab, while 50 common facilities had been brought together to develop industrial clusters. The government had also consolidated skill development, she added.

headline: Woman shot dead over divorce dispute
description: Woman shot dead over divorce dispute
author: Sarfaraz Akram
article_text:
A man allegedly shot dead his former mother-in-law over a divorce dispute, while another man was seriously injured in a firing incident in Mailsi, police said on Friday.

According to police, the incident occurred at night in Chak No 204/WB, near Danish School, within the limits of Tibba Sultanpur police station.

Police said the suspects, identified as Naveed Iqbal and his accomplice Muhammad Shahid, along with an unidentified man, allegedly broke into the house and opened fire.

As a result, Amina Bibi died on the spot, while Ghulam Shabbir sustained serious bullet wounds.

The injured man was shifted to Nishtar Hospital in Multan in critical condition, where he is receiving treatment.

In his statement to police, Muhammad Rafiqat, the deceased woman's son and complainant in the case, alleged that his sister was formerly married to Naveed Iqbal but had obtained a divorce.

He claimed that the suspect, harbouring a grudge over the separation, entered the house with his accomplices and shot his mother dead.

Police reached the scene after receiving information about the incident, took custody of the body and began legal proceedings.

headline: Lahore's winter fish feast gets costlier
description: Lahore's winter fish feast gets costlier
author: BILAL GHAURI
article_text:
A sharp increase in fish prices amid rising inflation has made the popular winter delicacy increasingly unaffordable for ordinary consumers, with rates of traditional and river fish climbing substantially as the cold season begins.

Despite the high prices, families have started visiting Lahore's fish market to buy freshwater, farm-raised and marine fish according to their budgets. Parents are particularly interested in varieties with fewer bones, including Sewal, Pari and Bangash, for their children.

With the onset of winter, activity at the fish market has picked up, attracting customers from different walks of life. However, many shoppers have described the latest price increases as an additional burden on household budgets.

A full-sized Sewal fish is selling for Rs2,500 per kg, while the smaller variety costs Rs1,500 per kg.

Khagga is priced at Rs1,400 per kg, while large-sized local Khagga sells for Rs1,300 per kg and the smaller variety for Rs500.

Bangash fish is available for Rs500 per kilogram, while full-sized Chira costs Rs450 per kilogram. Pari fish, commonly used to prepare minced fish meat, is selling for Rs650 per kg.

Farm-raised black Rohu is priced between Rs300 and Rs1,000 per kg, depending on its size. Sewal and Fauji Khagga are also used to prepare fish fingers and fish chips because they contain fewer small bones.

Families often prefer Sewal, Pari and Fauji Khagga for children, as these varieties have a single prominent bone that can be removed during cleaning.

The fish market also supplies prepared fish to shops across the city.

Workers clean the fish, remove the heads and other unwanted parts, cut the flesh into portions, apply spices and freeze it for delivery to shopkeepers according to their requirements.

These preparations are used by vendors selling fried and gram-flour-coated fish in local markets.

Fish heads are also purchased by small and large restaurants for preparing fish soup. They are sold separately to ordinary customers for Rs80 per kilogram.

The market operates throughout the day, serving both retail customers and wholesale traders.

Retail buyers generally visit between 11am and 9pm, while commission agents and wholesale traders conduct their business from 11pm until around 3am.

headline: UAF mobilises 32,000 students for wheat drive
description: UAF mobilises 32,000 students for wheat drive
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
.

The University of Agriculture Faisalabad (UAF), in collaboration with the Punjab Agriculture Extension Department, has mobilised around 32,000 students for a 10-day wheat awareness campaign from October 30 to November 8 across six divisions of Punjab.

Addressing the inaugural ceremony at Iqbal Auditorium, Punjab Parliamentary Secretary for Agriculture Usama Khan Leghari urged students to help farmers adopt modern technologies, saying young graduates could play a key role in improving agricultural productivity, mechanisation and entrepreneurship.

He said the government was supporting farmers through the Kisan Card, mechanised equipment, including super seeders, and a wheat support price of Rs4,500 per maund.

He added that more than Rs350 billion had been disbursed in agricultural microfinance loans through the Bank of Punjab, with a recovery rate of 99 per cent.

headline: LHC orders end to 'parchi' system in Punjab hospitals
description: LHC orders end to 'parchi' system in Punjab hospitals
author: Rana Yasif
article_text:
The Lahore High Court has directed the Punjab government to abolish the existing 'parchi' (registration slip) system in all public-sector hospitals across the province within four weeks, requiring patients to receive medical attention without having to obtain slips or wait in long queues at registration counters.

Justice Malik Javid Iqbal Wains issued the directions while hearing a public interest petition seeking enforcement of the fundamental rights to life and healthcare, as well as implementation of superior courts' judgments regarding the provision of basic medical facilities in government hospitals.

The court was informed that the Punjab Health Department would introduce a modern, technology-based patient management system to ensure prompt treatment for emergency cases and outpatients, while eliminating unnecessary delays.

The judge directed the authorities concerned to implement an undertaking given by Special Secretary (Health) Nabila Irfan and submit a detailed compliance report at the next hearing, supported by documentary evidence outlining the steps taken to replace the existing system with a patient-friendly mechanism.

The court also sought comprehensive reports from all respondents addressing the grievances raised in the petition and detailing measures taken to ensure the availability of essential healthcare facilities.

The order noted that the public interest petition had remained pending since 2020, highlighting persistent shortages of essential medical facilities and difficulties faced by patients seeking treatment at public hospitals.

headline: Polio virus resurfaces in Rawalpindi
description: Polio virus resurfaces in Rawalpindi
author: Qaiser Shirazi
article_text:
The health department and district administration have approved another anti-polio campaign from November 2 after the United Nations Children's Fund (Unicef) confirmed a substantial presence of poliovirus in Rawalpindi's sewage.

The last anti-polio campaign of the year will also be held in December.

Earlier this year, the district administration and health department had made strong claims that Rawalpindi's sewage had been completely cleared of poliovirus.

However, a third-party survey detected a significant quantity of the virus in the city's sewage, particularly in Nullah Lai, prompting authorities to launch another vaccination campaign.

The district administration had previously described families refusing polio drops as Afghan refugees. However, the number of refusal cases has continued to rise despite the deportation of all Afghan families from Rawalpindi district.

From January 1 to October 30 this year, the health department has remained unable to effectively cover families refusing vaccination.

Authorities have once again claimed that such families will be a particular focus of the campaign beginning on November 2. These include a large number of Kashmiri and local Rawalpindi families living in affluent areas as well as Pindora, Satellite Town, Saddar, Dhok Hassu, Pirwadhai, Fauji Colony, Dhok Mangtal, Adiala Road, Gulistan Colony and Rehmatabad.

Meanwhile, a meeting of the District Polio Eradication Committee, chaired by Deputy Commissioner Nadeem Nasir, was held on Thursday to review arrangements for the November 2 campaign, the performance of the previous drive and preparations for the upcoming campaign.

A presentation on the previous campaign reviewed the performance of union councils, vaccination coverage, missed children and cases involving parents who refused vaccination.

According to the presentation, a target of 989,924 children had been set in Rawalpindi district during the previous campaign. Of the children missed during the drive, 84 per cent were covered on the same day.

The deputy commissioner directed officials to pay special attention during the upcoming campaign to union councils where vaccination coverage had remained low.

He called for identifying missed children and ensuring effective follow-up to administer polio drops.

He also issued special instructions for Lab Thatho union council in Taxila, saying the complete eradication of polio was a national responsibility.

The health department, World Health Organisation and other relevant institutions should work in coordination and adopt a joint strategy, he said.

He directed officials to continuously monitor the performance of field teams and ensure there was no negligence during the campaign.

Later, the deputy commissioner formally inaugurated the campaign by administering polio drops to children.

headline: China, Pakistan push poverty reduction
description: China, Pakistan push poverty reduction
author: News Desk
article_text:
.

Government officials, diplomats and development experts from China and Pakistan have called for stronger regional cooperation, economic connectivity and inclusive development to tackle poverty across South Asia.

The call was made at the 2026 China South Asia Forum on Poverty Reduction and Development Cooperation, held in Islamabad under the theme 'Creating Development Opportunities for Common Prosperity'.

The event was organised by the China International Communications Group (CICG) in collaboration with the Understanding China Forum.

Chinese Ambassador Jiang Zaidong said CPEC had attracted approximately $25.9 billion in direct investment, added more than 8,000 megawatts of electricity generation capacity and created over 260,000 jobs.

headline: Five honour killers sentenced to death
description: Five honour killers sentenced to death
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
.

A local court sentenced five accused to death in a triple murder case. The honour killing case which had cost the life of a woman and two others was registered at the Kallar Syedan police station in July 2023.

The convicts had killed the woman because they did not approve of her marrying a man of her own choice. The court found the five accused guilty of murder, conspiring to murder and trespassing, and sentenced each of them to death, a collective compensation of Rs1 million, 35 years of imprisonment and fines amounting to Rs125,000 rupees.

The court cited available evidence, post-mortem reports, and the recovery of the murder weapons before announcing the verdict. The convicts, Kashif, Ahsan, Asif, Ismail and Yasir, were each ordered to pay Rs200,000 compensation.

headline: Traders oppose quarterly garbage tax
description: Traders oppose quarterly garbage tax
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Shopkeepers across Rawalpindi have been issued bills demanding Rs6,000 in garbage tax for three months, with notices directing them to pay the amount within seven days. The notices warn that shops will be sealed in case of non-payment.

The tax has triggered strong protests from traders' organisations across the city. Former president of the District Bar Association, Advocate Syed Tanvir Sohail, has announced that he will challenge the Rs6,000 bills before the Lahore High Court's Rawalpindi Bench on Monday, November 2.

Traders have decided not to pay the tax, raising the possibility of a confrontation between the district administration and business community.

Central Traders Association leaders, including Commercial Market Vice Chairman Hammad Qureshi and Sabzi Mandi Traders Association President Ghulam Qadir Mir, said no sanitation worker from the Suthra Punjab Company visited shops or plazas to provide cleaning services.

They said every market and commercial plaza had its own sanitation workers, who were paid salaries.

They said traders would not pay the Rs6,000 garbage tax under any circumstances.

The leaders said the city's sanitation system had virtually collapsed and cleaning activities existed only in official statements and documents. In practice, they said, every street and neighbourhood in Rawalpindi had turned into a dumping ground.

They questioned why shopkeepers should pay the tax when Suthra Punjab Company's sanitation workers had never visited any market or commercial plaza in the city to clean the premises.

They also pointed out that each plaza housed between 100 and 300 shops, asking why every shop should separately pay Rs6,000.

The traders said the government had placed the burden of 10 departments on shopkeepers, with two or three departments visiting shops daily to impose fines and collect money. They said sealing shops for refusing to pay had become routine.

Traders' organisations from markets and commercial plazas across the city would devise a joint strategy and launch a strong protest, they added.

Meanwhile, households in residential areas have also started receiving garbage tax bills, demanding Rs3,000 per house for three months.

headline: Teenage girl alleges repeated assault
description: Teenage girl alleges repeated assault
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
A married man was arrested for allegedly raping a 14-year-old girl in Qazian, within the jurisdiction of Gujar Khan Police Station.

According to police, the suspect, who lived in the same neighbourhood as the victim, allegedly subjected her to sexual assault on multiple occasions while threatening her.

In his complaint, the girl's uncle stated that he belonged to Toba Tek Singh and worked as a labourer in the Habib Canal area of Qazian, where he also resided. He said his 14-year-old niece had come to stay with the family around two to two-and-a-half months ago.

The complainant said the girl recently felt dizzy and was about to be taken to a doctor when she initially refused. She later disclosed, while visibly frightened, that a local resident, identified as Fayyaz, had allegedly sexually assaulted her around two-and-a-half months earlier after finding her alone at home.

He further alleged that the suspect, who was married and had two children, continued to threaten the girl and sexually assault her. The most recent alleged incident took place around 10 days ago, which reportedly contributed to her present condition.

Police said a case had been registered and the suspect taken into custody. Further investigation is under way.

headline: Jobs of 2,000 dengue workers restored
description: Jobs of 2,000 dengue workers restored
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
The jobs of nearly 2,000 male and female dengue workers in Rawalpindi district, who were dismissed last week following the expiry of their contracts, have been restored on the orders of the director general of health, Punjab, Lahore.

The contracts of all the workers have been extended for another 90 days.

On Friday, the Rawalpindi health department telephoned the dismissed male and female workers to inform them about the restoration of their contracts and asked them to rejoin duty on Saturday, October 31, for another three-month period.

The contract extension has brought relief and happiness among the female dengue workers, who had been dismissed after their previous contracts expired.

However, the health department has refused to regularise the services of these workers.

Meanwhile, dengue infections continue to spread in the twin cities of Rawalpindi and Islamabad, taking the combined number of patients to 134, with two of them reportedly in critical condition. Of the total cases, 85 have been reported in Rawalpindi and 49 in Islamabad.

The number of patients may increase if heavy rainfall does not occur over the next two weeks. Rainfall, however, followed by severe cold could bring the dengue season to an end.

According to the health department, the peak dengue season and associated threat will persist until November 15. After that, dengue larvae are expected to die naturally due to the severe cold during the evenings, nights and early mornings.

Health officials have reportedly started hoping for immediate heavy rainfall to help bring the season to an end.

Anti-dengue activities in open areas along the boundary between Rawalpindi and Islamabad have not been properly updated due to jurisdictional disputes. As a result, dengue larvae have multiplied in these areas.

The health department said dengue larvae and mosquito populations had remained under control in Rawalpindi district this year.

The district's 1,400 anti-dengue teams have so far inspected 7,902,099 houses, open spaces, tyre shops, junkyards and buildings under construction. They detected dengue larvae at 241,942 locations.

A total of 2,798 FIRs were registered after the detection of larvae, while 690 properties were sealed. The authorities also issued 2,335 challans and imposed fines amounting to Rs3,156,000.

The health department said the drop in temperatures had reduced the presence of dengue mosquitoes in open areas, graveyards, tyre shops and junkyards.

headline: IHC seeks answers on passenger offloading
description: IHC seeks answers on passenger offloading
author: Fiaz Mahmood
article_text:
The Islamabad High Court (IHC) has sought responses from the interior secretary, the director of immigration and the director general of the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) in a case challenging allegedly unnecessary travel restrictions imposed on citizens.

Justice Arbab Muhammad Tahir issued the order while hearing a petition filed by the Judicial Activism Panel, which challenges travel restrictions, passport rules and the placement of citizens' names on the Passport Control List (PCL) and the Provisional National Identification List (PNIL).

The court also issued a notice to the Attorney General of Pakistan, seeking assistance on important legal questions, and directed that the case be fixed for hearing in the first week of December.

According to the petition, citizens' names are placed on the relevant travel control lists merely on the recommendations of government departments or agencies. It further alleges that travellers holding valid passports, visas and confirmed tickets are offloaded without prior notice or an explanation of the reasons.

The petitioner contended that such restrictions caused irreparable harm to citizens by disrupting their employment, education and medical treatment.

headline: 'The Great Gatsby' gets a gender-swapped crime drama adaptation at NBC
description: NBC develops Gatsby, a modern police procedural inspired by 'The Great Gatsby', with a gender-swapped Nick Carraway
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
NBC is developing Gatsby, a modern-day police procedural inspired by F. Scott Fitzgerald’s classic novel The Great Gatsby, with a gender-swapped twist on one of its central characters.

The series comes from writers and executive producers Jake Coburn and Jason Tracey, with Universal Television, a division of Universal Studio Group, attached to the project, Deadline reported on October 30.

The upcoming drama will centre on Det. Jay Gatsby, a charming investigator with a con artist’s ability to read human behaviour, and New York State Police Det. Nicole “Nicky” Carraway, a decorated officer who has always wanted to become a writer.

Nicky is a gender-swapped version of Nick Carraway, the narrator of Fitzgerald’s 1925 novel. In the original story, Nick moves to the fictional Long Island neighbourhood of West Egg, where he becomes acquainted with the mysterious millionaire Jay Gatsby and his attempts to rekindle his romance with Daisy Buchanan.

The new adaptation will reimagine the literary characters in a contemporary crime-solving setting, shifting the focus towards a police procedural format.

The Great Gatsby is widely regarded as one of the great American novels and has inspired several screen adaptations. Among the best-known are the 1974 film starring Robert Redford and Mia Farrow, and Baz Luhrmann’s 2013 version featuring Leonardo DiCaprio, Tobey Maguire and Carey Mulligan.

Coburn previously worked on NBC’s The Hunting Party, serving as co-showrunner and executive producer. His other credits include The Endgame, Quantico and Gossip Girl.

Tracey most recently served as an executive producer on ABC’s RJ Decker. He also created and showran CSI: Vegas and worked on Elementary, Burn Notice and Cold Case.

No casting details or premiere date have been announced.

The Great Gatsby is widely regarded as one of the great American novels and has inspired several screen adaptations. Among the best-known are the 1974 film starring Robert Redford and Mia Farrow, and Baz Luhrmann’s 2013 version featuring Leonardo DiCaprio, Tobey Maguire and Carey Mulligan.
Coburn previously worked on NBC’s The Hunting Party, serving as co-showrunner and executive producer. His other credits include The Endgame, Quantico and Gossip Girl.
Tracey most recently served as an executive producer on ABC’s RJ Decker. He also created and showran CSI: Vegas and worked on Elementary, Burn Notice and Cold Case.
No casting details or premiere date have been announced.

headline: Balochistan sacks 102 absent employees
description: Balochistan sacks 102 absent employees
author: SHOAIB RAISANI
article_text:
The Balochistan government has dismissed 72 medical officers in Grades 17 and 18 for prolonged unauthorised absence from duty under the Balochistan Employees Efficiency and Discipline Act (BEEDA) 2011.

Provincial Health Minister Bakht Muhammad Kakar said the action was taken as part of efforts to improve the functioning of the provincial health department on the directives of Chief Minister Mir Sarfraz Bugti.

He said the government would not tolerate absenteeism or negligence on the part of medical staff, adding that reforms were being introduced in the health sector under the chief minister's leadership.

The minister said the government had pledged from the outset to provide healthcare facilities to people at their doorsteps and would not tolerate any lapse in public service delivery.

He warned that action would continue against officials demonstrating negligence or an unserious attitude towards their responsibilities.

Meanwhile, the Balochistan Prisons Department has dismissed 30 employees, including 20 wardens, over prolonged absence from duty and negligence in the performance of their responsibilities.

headline: K-P gathers evidence against Sohail Afridi
description: K-P gathers evidence against Sohail Afridi
author: Shahida Parveen
article_text:
Adviser to the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa government on Information and Public Relations Samar Haroon Bilour has said that former chief minister Sohail Afridi remains in protective custody, while evidence is being collected in connection with allegations of corruption involving billions of rupees.

Speaking at a press conference at the Information Cell in the Civil Secretariat on Friday, she said the government was pursuing institutional reforms, transparency and improved public service delivery.

Responding to questions about Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, she described him as a senior and respected politician but said his recent statements appeared to reflect political frustration and resentment over being excluded from decision-making.

She suggested that the absence of the political role he expected in the current technocratic setup might also be contributing to his dissatisfaction. However, she said the government would welcome his constructive suggestions and guidance.

Regarding the Dir Colony tragedy in Peshawar, Samar Bilour said investigations into the incident had been completed and a detailed report would soon be shared with the media. Inspections of government and private schools and seminaries across the province had identified 4,049 educational institutions requiring repairs and rehabilitation.

A comprehensive plan was being prepared to improve these institutions. Students from affected schools would be shifted to nearby government schools, with arrangements for class-wise adjustments and second shifts wherever necessary to ensure continuity of education.

She said a subcommittee was also examining the responsibilities of relevant departments and tehsil municipal administrations to determine whether negligence had occurred in building approvals, inspections and supervision.

On law and order, she said eight modern armoured vehicles had been handed over to the provincial police. A comprehensive plan to improve police infrastructure and operational capacity would be prepared within the next five to six weeks. Paying tribute to police personnel who had sacrificed their lives in the war against terrorism, she said providing modern equipment and resources to the force was the government's responsibility.

The adviser said internal irregularities in the Sehat Card programme were being examined, but there was no intention to discontinue or abolish it. The performance and administrative affairs of Medical Teaching Institutions (MTIs), along with the professional competence of their governing boards, would also be reviewed.

headline: Three cops martyred in K-P attacks
description: Three cops martyred in K-P attacks
author: Ghulam Akbar Marwat
article_text:
Three policemen were martyred in separate incidents in Bannu, Lakki Marwat and Bajaur on Friday, while unidentified armed men abducted a head constable in Bannu. In a retaliatory operation in Lakki Marwat, police and Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) personnel killed two suspected target killers allegedly involved in the murder of a police constable.

In Bajaur, unidentified armed men launched a late-night attack on the Salai Pati Police Post, falling within the jurisdiction of Barang Police Station, martyring Constable Khaista Main Syed. According to police, the policeman bravely confronted the attackers but succumbed to his injuries.

The funeral prayers of the martyred constable were offered at Police Lines, where the District Police Officer (DPO), Deputy Commissioner, SP Investigation and other senior officials attended.

In Bannu, unidentified gunmen opened fire on CTD Constable Sadiq Zaman, a resident of Taji Killi, at Barmashil Chowk, killing him on the spot. He was serving as a driver with the CTD in North Waziristan and was visiting his native area on leave when he was attacked.

In another incident, armed men abducted Head Constable Ziaullah from the Karam Garhi area near Baran Dam. He was posted at Bannu Police Lines and was reportedly associated with the Wazir Police Sub-Division.

Meanwhile, in Lakki Marwat, unidentified armed men opened fire on Constable Mumtaz near a bank within the jurisdiction of Shahbazkhel Police Station, martyring him.

Following the attack, police and the local peace committee launched an immediate response.

headline: Raj Kapoor, Dilip homes set for facelift
description: Raj Kapoor, Dilip homes set for facelift
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi has called for comprehensive measures to preserve and restore Peshawar's historical heritage and promote its cultural and tourism potential, while directing authorities to ensure representation of all languages spoken in the province in the proposed Khyber Star Talent Hunt Programme.

At a meeting chaired by him to review the development and restoration of Peshawar's historical heritage and tourist attractions, the governor was briefed on the city's historical and cultural significance, the preservation of heritage sites, and ongoing and proposed development projects. Adviser for Development and Planning Usman Saifullah, Secretary Tourism Saadat Hassan and other relevant officials attended the meeting.

The briefing also covered plans for night tourism and heritage tourism.

Kundi said Peshawar was a living embodiment of centuries-old history, civilisation and culture and stressed the need to highlight its historical identity to attract domestic and foreign tourists.

He directed the authorities to display the vintage ambulance and old fire engines preserved at Gor Khatri at a suitable location where visitors could see them. He also called for introducing special tourist buses to facilitate visits to the city's historical landmarks.

The governor further directed the installation of large information boards near the Peshawar Motorway Toll Plaza, highlighting the city's historical sites and cultural heritage to familiarise visitors with its rich past.

Emphasising the importance of cultural activities, he said efforts should be made to preserve Peshawar's traditions, arts and literary heritage. He also directed that restoration work on the ancestral homes of legendary actors Dilip Kumar and Raj Kapoor be initiated at the earliest.

He welcomed practical steps towards protecting the city's heritage, saying restoration of historical sites and provision of better tourist facilities would help promote Peshawar's cultural identity.

Separately, chairing a meeting on the proposed Khyber Star Talent Hunt and Cultural Promotion Programme, Kundi directed that all languages spoken in the province, including Urdu and Saraiki, be included to ensure equal representation and promote cultural diversity.

Officials briefed the participants on the programme's objectives, implementation mechanism and selection process. They said the initiative aimed to identify and promote young talent while showcasing the province's culture, traditions and linguistic diversity.

They informed the meeting that audition camps would be established in different districts, while a committee comprising representatives of relevant departments would oversee the selection process to ensure transparency and maintain standards.

Kundi stressed that no regional language should be excluded from the auditions. He specifically highlighted the importance of Saraiki, which is widely spoken in Dera Ismail Khan, Sindh and parts of Punjab.

He said the youth of K-P possessed immense talent and potential that deserved recognition at national and international levels.

Providing young people with constructive opportunities and an effective platform to showcase their abilities was essential, he added, expressing hope that the programme would encourage emerging talent and contribute to the promotion of the province's rich cultural heritage.

article_html:
PESHAWAR:

Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi has called for comprehensive measures to preserve and restore Peshawar's historical heritage and promote its cultural and tourism potential, while directing authorities to ensure representation of all languages spoken in the province in the proposed Khyber Star Talent Hunt Programme.

At a meeting chaired by him to review the development and restoration of Peshawar's historical heritage and tourist attractions, the governor was briefed on the city's historical and cultural significance, the preservation of heritage sites, and ongoing and proposed development projects. Adviser for Development and Planning Usman Saifullah, Secretary Tourism Saadat Hassan and other relevant officials attended the meeting.

The briefing also covered plans for night tourism and heritage tourism.

Kundi said Peshawar was a living embodiment of centuries-old history, civilisation and culture and stressed the need to highlight its historical identity to attract domestic and foreign tourists.

He directed the authorities to display the vintage ambulance and old fire engines preserved at Gor Khatri at a suitable location where visitors could see them. He also called for introducing special tourist buses to facilitate visits to the city's historical landmarks.

The governor further directed the installation of large information boards near the Peshawar Motorway Toll Plaza, highlighting the city's historical sites and cultural heritage to familiarise visitors with its rich past.

Emphasising the importance of cultural activities, he said efforts should be made to preserve Peshawar's traditions, arts and literary heritage. He also directed that restoration work on the ancestral homes of legendary actors Dilip Kumar and Raj Kapoor be initiated at the earliest.

He welcomed practical steps towards protecting the city's heritage, saying restoration of historical sites and provision of better tourist facilities would help promote Peshawar's cultural identity.

Separately, chairing a meeting on the proposed Khyber Star Talent Hunt and Cultural Promotion Programme, Kundi directed that all languages spoken in the province, including Urdu and Saraiki, be included to ensure equal representation and promote cultural diversity.

Officials briefed the participants on the programme's objectives, implementation mechanism and selection process. They said the initiative aimed to identify and promote young talent while showcasing the province's culture, traditions and linguistic diversity.

They informed the meeting that audition camps would be established in different districts, while a committee comprising representatives of relevant departments would oversee the selection process to ensure transparency and maintain standards.

Kundi stressed that no regional language should be excluded from the auditions. He specifically highlighted the importance of Saraiki, which is widely spoken in Dera Ismail Khan, Sindh and parts of Punjab.

He said the youth of K-P possessed immense talent and potential that deserved recognition at national and international levels.

Providing young people with constructive opportunities and an effective platform to showcase their abilities was essential, he added, expressing hope that the programme would encourage emerging talent and contribute to the promotion of the province's rich cultural heritage.

headline: Special audit targets JUI-F chief's lands
description: Special audit targets JUI-F chief's lands
author: Ramzan Seemab
article_text:
Land transfers involving properties registered in the names of Maulana Fazlur Rehman, Maulana Lutafur Rehman, Attaur Rehman and Ziaur Rehman have come under scrutiny after the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Board of Revenue ordered a special audit and verification of land records in Dera Ismail Khan and Paharpur over alleged irregularities.

According to an official letter dated back October 29, 2025, the Deputy Commissioner/District Collector DI Khan has been directed to conduct a detailed examination of property transfers, ownership documents and mutation registers relating to several properties in Abdul Khel, Shorikot and urban areas of the district.

The properties under scrutiny include a residential compound, a hujra and around 64 kanals of land in Abdul Khel; approximately 88 kanals and 24 kanals of commercial and agricultural land in Shorikot; and a residential and commercial property measuring 18 kanals and 12 marlas in urban DI Khan.

The audit observations have raised questions about land classification, oral mutations, declared property valuations and payment of government dues. The document also highlights discrepancies between declared and estimated property values, potentially resulting in short payments of stamp duty and Capital Value Tax (CVT).

The Board of Revenue has directed the district administration to take original land records and cadastral maps covering the period from 2002 to 2025 into safe custody. A precautionary entry is also to be recorded to prevent further transfers of the properties under investigation.

The authorities have further been asked to issue notices for recovery of any outstanding government dues and initiate departmental inquiries into the conduct of the revenue officials concerned.

Copies of the letter were also sent to the principal secretary to the chief minister, the director general of NAB Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, the chief commissioner of the Federal Board of Revenue's Regional Tax Office in DI Khan, the divisional commissioner, the director of land records and the tehsildars of DI Khan and Paharpur.

However, the allegations and audit observations have not been independently verified. No response from the individuals concerned or details of a final inquiry or judicial determination were available.

headline: ML-I phase one to cost $2.1b
description: ML-I phase one to cost $2.1b
author: Shahbaz Rana
article_text:
The government has informed the Senate that the first phase of the Mainline-I (ML-I) project would cost $2.1 billion, as Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif constituted a new committee to finalise funding plans for the second phase of the much-delayed scheme.

The project faces delay even though 67% of the railways' track is unsafe, causing 300 accidents in just three years, the official response to the upper house of Parliament revealed on Friday.

The 1,872-kilometre ML-I from Karachi to Peshawar faces serious funding constraints, compelling the government to look for sources other than China, pledge land with local banks and seek loans from multilateral creditors.

The Minister for Railways Hanif Abbasi informed the Senate on Friday that the estimated cost of the 480-kilometre Karachi-Rohri section is $2.1 billion. He said the final project cost will be determined upon completion of the detailed engineering design, currently under review for finalisation.

The minister said construction is expected to commence during the current fiscal year, subject to completion of all requisite approvals, financing arrangements and procurement processes, with an estimated implementation period of two and a half years.

Pakistan could not secure $8 billion in funding from China out of a total cost of $10 billion, despite the project having been declared the only strategically important initiative under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC).

In response to another question, the minister said accidents faced by Pakistan Railways had risen to 300 over a three-year period. As many as 299 accidents were reported from 2023 to 2025, including 241 incidents of derailment of goods and passenger trains. About 84 accidents were reported in 2023, a maximum of 118 in 2024 and 97 in 2025, including 37 head-on collisions.

The ministry of railways admitted that 67% of the track and 60% of the rolling stock has outlived its life, but said that "despite the fact that 67% of the railway track and 60% of the rolling stock is over-aged, there have not been significant investments in railway infrastructure, as required, for more than seven decades of our history".

Due to funding constraints, the government has not been able to fill vacant posts. There were 22,546 vacant positions in Pakistan Railways against pay scales 1 to 22, of which 12,165 are in Punjab, 7,245 in Sindh, 1,840 in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and 1,296 in Balochistan.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has also constituted a committee under the chairmanship of the governor of the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) to formalise a financing plan for the second phase, the Multan-Rohri section. The committee met this week to find ways to securitise Pakistan Railways' land to finance the project's second phase.

"Trillions of rupees of land is lying vacant and the government is now looking for ways to give the land as collateral to domestic commercial banks for raising funds for the second phase," Federal Minister for Planning Ahsan Iqbal told The Express Tribune.

The Frontier Works Organisation (FWO), which was eager to construct the Multan-Rohri section, had estimated the second phase cost at Rs470 billion under a build-and-lease model. However, there were issues over who would repay the debt and the quantum of sovereign guarantees the ministry of finance may have to issue, and Pakistan Railways was reluctant to take full responsibility for debt repayments that FWO would raise from local banks.

Out of the Rs470 billion estimated cost, the debt requirement was around Rs365 billion and the remaining money had been sought from the government as a grant.

Sources said that over a 25-year lease, total payments had been estimated at Rs1.1 trillion, but the ministry of railways showed willingness to pay only Rs29 billion. It had projected operational profits of Rs485 billion over 25 years, and the ministry of finance was of the view that at least this amount should be pledged by the railways.

But the railways ministry was unwilling to provide the entire funds, and the ministry of finance was unwilling to provide guarantees against 25-year repayment obligations.

Under the FWO construction model, FWO will complete the rail link in three years by borrowing a maximum 80% of the cost from local banks and securing at least 20% financing from the federal government as viability gap funding. FWO will then hand over the track to Pakistan Railways on a 25-year lease and transfer the title after expiry of the lease period. The total project cost is Rs470 billion.

article_html:
ISLAMABAD:

The government has informed the Senate that the first phase of the Mainline-I (ML-I) project would cost $2.1 billion, as Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif constituted a new committee to finalise funding plans for the second phase of the much-delayed scheme.

The project faces delay even though 67% of the railways' track is unsafe, causing 300 accidents in just three years, the official response to the upper house of Parliament revealed on Friday.

The 1,872-kilometre ML-I from Karachi to Peshawar faces serious funding constraints, compelling the government to look for sources other than China, pledge land with local banks and seek loans from multilateral creditors.

The Minister for Railways Hanif Abbasi informed the Senate on Friday that the estimated cost of the 480-kilometre Karachi-Rohri section is $2.1 billion. He said the final project cost will be determined upon completion of the detailed engineering design, currently under review for finalisation.

The minister said construction is expected to commence during the current fiscal year, subject to completion of all requisite approvals, financing arrangements and procurement processes, with an estimated implementation period of two and a half years.

Pakistan could not secure $8 billion in funding from China out of a total cost of $10 billion, despite the project having been declared the only strategically important initiative under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC).

In response to another question, the minister said accidents faced by Pakistan Railways had risen to 300 over a three-year period. As many as 299 accidents were reported from 2023 to 2025, including 241 incidents of derailment of goods and passenger trains. About 84 accidents were reported in 2023, a maximum of 118 in 2024 and 97 in 2025, including 37 head-on collisions.

The ministry of railways admitted that 67% of the track and 60% of the rolling stock has outlived its life, but said that "despite the fact that 67% of the railway track and 60% of the rolling stock is over-aged, there have not been significant investments in railway infrastructure, as required, for more than seven decades of our history".

Due to funding constraints, the government has not been able to fill vacant posts. There were 22,546 vacant positions in Pakistan Railways against pay scales 1 to 22, of which 12,165 are in Punjab, 7,245 in Sindh, 1,840 in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and 1,296 in Balochistan.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has also constituted a committee under the chairmanship of the governor of the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) to formalise a financing plan for the second phase, the Multan-Rohri section. The committee met this week to find ways to securitise Pakistan Railways' land to finance the project's second phase.

"Trillions of rupees of land is lying vacant and the government is now looking for ways to give the land as collateral to domestic commercial banks for raising funds for the second phase," Federal Minister for Planning Ahsan Iqbal told The Express Tribune.

The Frontier Works Organisation (FWO), which was eager to construct the Multan-Rohri section, had estimated the second phase cost at Rs470 billion under a build-and-lease model. However, there were issues over who would repay the debt and the quantum of sovereign guarantees the ministry of finance may have to issue, and Pakistan Railways was reluctant to take full responsibility for debt repayments that FWO would raise from local banks.

Out of the Rs470 billion estimated cost, the debt requirement was around Rs365 billion and the remaining money had been sought from the government as a grant.

Sources said that over a 25-year lease, total payments had been estimated at Rs1.1 trillion, but the ministry of railways showed willingness to pay only Rs29 billion. It had projected operational profits of Rs485 billion over 25 years, and the ministry of finance was of the view that at least this amount should be pledged by the railways.

But the railways ministry was unwilling to provide the entire funds, and the ministry of finance was unwilling to provide guarantees against 25-year repayment obligations.

Under the FWO construction model, FWO will complete the rail link in three years by borrowing a maximum 80% of the cost from local banks and securing at least 20% financing from the federal government as viability gap funding. FWO will then hand over the track to Pakistan Railways on a 25-year lease and transfer the title after expiry of the lease period. The total project cost is Rs470 billion.

headline: Energy, food keep SPI in double digits
description: Energy, food keep SPI in double digits
author: Usman Hanif
article_text:
Pakistan's Sensitive Price Indicator (SPI) remained elevated at 11.32% year-on-year for the week ended October 29, 2026, underscoring sticky short-term inflation even as the index slipped 0.35% week-on-week.

The year-on-year reading reflects sustained cost pressures on energy and selected food items, with global supply concerns linked to the US-Israel conflict with Iran and ongoing Houthi confrontation with Saudi Arabia continuing to influence fuel and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices.

Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS) data showed the combined SPI stood at 373.51, down from 374.84 in the previous week but well above 335.53 recorded a year earlier. On a weekly basis, electricity charges for Q1 fell 3.92%, chicken prices declined 2.95%, eggs dropped 2.81%, wheat flour eased 0.83% and LPG retreated 0.73%. Petrol, sugar and powdered milk also posted modest declines.

In contrast, tomatoes surged 34.91%, potatoes rose 3.27%, diesel increased 2.53% and gram pulse advanced 2.11%. Bread, onions, fresh milk and curd registered smaller gains. Of the 51 essential items tracked across 50 markets in 17 cities, prices of 15 items (29.41%) rose, 12 items (23.53%) fell and 24 items (47.06%) remained unchanged.

Year-on-year, LPG prices climbed 106.86%, electricity charges for the lowest quintile jumped 52.38%, diesel rose 45.13% and petrol increased 43.61%. Wheat flour was up 34.87% and chicken 31.72%. Declines were recorded in potatoes (down 38.67%), tomatoes (27.99%), eggs (26.70%) and sugar (25.21%).

The highest-income quintile (Q5) faced the steepest annual increase of 12.13%, while the lowest-income group (Q1) recorded a rise of 8.07%. Week-on-week, Q5 saw the largest decline of 0.41%. The persistence of double-digit SPI growth, particularly in energy, points to limited near-term relief for households despite the modest weekly dip.

The monthly Consumer Price Index (CPI)-based inflation slowed down to 10.3% in September but it remained higher than the official forecast due to increasing prices of electricity and fuel, which offset the positive impact of a significant slowdown in prices of food commodities.

According to the PBS, energy group prices further increased compared to a year ago. This kept the overall inflation at 10.3%, which was slightly higher than the projection of the Planning Commission.

headline: Gold hits one-year low globally
description: Gold hits one-year low globally
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Gold prices in Pakistan declined on Friday, tracking losses in the international market where the metal fell to its lowest level in a year. Local rates came under pressure as white precious metals also weakened sharply amid a broader sell-off in technology shares.

In the domestic market, the price of gold per tola fell by Rs5,100 to reach Rs420,536, according to rates shared by the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association (APGJSA). The price of 10-gram gold dropped by Rs4,373 to Rs360,541. On Thursday, the per-tola rate had remained unchanged at Rs425,636.

The decline mirrored movements overseas. Spot gold fell 3.1 per cent to $3,897.09 an ounce by 11:47 am ET, marking its lowest level since October 2025 and slipping below the key $4,000 level, as per Reuters. Silver dropped 6 per cent to $49 an ounce, breaking below $50 for the first time in 11 months. Palladium also weakened, sliding below $1,000 an ounce. Platinum moved in the same direction as the other white metals.

Market participants noted that silver, platinum and palladium had entered technically oversold territory based on their relative strength index (RSI) readings. The sell-off in precious metals coincided with a sharp drop in technology shares. Investors expressed concern that heavy spending on artificial intelligence may not generate sufficient returns in the near term, prompting a broader risk-off move across markets.

In the local silver market, the price declined by Rs238 to Rs5,530 per tola. The simultaneous weakness in both gold and silver reflected the influence of international benchmarks on domestic pricing.

The drop in gold prices follows a period of relative stability earlier in the week. Thursday's unchanged rates had provided a brief pause, but Friday's international decline quickly fed through to local quotes. Jewellers and traders typically adjust rates in line with global moves, adjusted for the rupee-dollar exchange rate and local premiums.

The current international levels place gold well below the $4,000 mark that had served as a psychological support in recent sessions. Silver's break below $50 ends an 11-month stretch above that level. For palladium, the move under $1,000 adds to pressure on the metal, which has already faced weaker industrial demand signals in some sectors.

Meanwhile, the Pakistani rupee closed the day at 276.75 against the US dollar, posting a marginal gain of Re0.01. On Thursday, the local currency had settled at 276.76.

headline: Local businessmen demand level playing field
description: Local businessmen demand level playing field
author: SHAHRAM HAQ
article_text:
As Punjab courts Chinese, Austrian and other foreign investors with long-term land leases and tax breaks, local businessmen are asking a simple question: will they get the same facilitation?

The question arose after Austrian ambassador called for faster action on economic ties. "The time has come to take more effective steps to increase bilateral economic cooperation," Ambassador Wolfgang Oliver Kutschera said in a meeting with Punjab Minister for Industries and Commerce Chaudhry Shafay Hussain on Friday.

He said the Punjab government had done remarkable work on promoting economic activity and Austria would examine the potential of setting up small hydroelectric power projects in the province.

"Austria has expertise in hydropower and we want to benefit from its technology," the provincial minister said, adding that small dams could be completed in two to three years. He told the ambassador that the infrastructure in Punjab's Special Economic Zones (SEZs) had been built according to international standards at a cost of billions of rupees and the new federal industrial policy allowed land to be taken on 30 to 50-year lease. He invited Austrian firms to consider agro-based value addition, seed development, dairy joint ventures and wastewater treatment.

Local industrialists welcome the foreign interest but say the offer should not stop at the border. "We are happy to see Austrian, Chinese and other investors coming, but a local manufacturer who has paid taxes for 20 years should not be forced to run between five offices while the foreign company gets the red carpet treatment," said a Lahore-based industrialist.

He added that facilitation should depend on the project and the jobs it created, not on the passport of the investor. Local and foreign investors should get the same incentives, the same speed in approvals and the same certainty that the policy will not change," he said.

Punjab is not the only province that prefers foreign investors, all other provinces, including Islamabad, also want foreign investment as it brings dollars, transfer of technology and much more. However, the hue and cry is not new. Earlier, in consultative sessions on investment policy at the Lahore Chamber of Commerce and Industry, the chamber office-bearers said foreign investment could not be encouraged without promoting local investment and the confidence of local investors must be restored first. The Board of Investment says the government treats both local and foreign investors equally.

The government has offered investors in Punjab SEZs a 10-year income tax holiday and one-time duty-free import of machinery, and has described these as open to both domestic and international investors. Businessmen say the real test is whether those benefits reach a small or medium-sized local firm as easily as a large foreign company.

The need for fresh capital is clear. UN Comtrade data shows Austria bought about $428.52 million of Pakistani goods in 2025, mostly clothing and textile, a growth of 20%, while Pakistan imported goods worth $115.73 million from Austria. Austrian investment in energy, dairy and agriculture is still small compared with textile trade.

Punjab is not the only province competing for capital. Sindh, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan also have SEZs, with many linked to the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor. Punjab's advantages include its large domestic market and industrial clusters in Faisalabad, Sialkot, Gujranwala and Gujrat. Businessmen say these advantages will matter more if investors see the same rules for everyone.

The meeting produced agreements in areas of cooperation, including hydroelectric power, technical education, tourism, garments, leather, footwear and livestock. However, it did not announce any specific projects, investment figures or timelines. Whether the talks lead to investment may depend on how Punjab treats investors who are already there.

He added that facilitation should depend on the project and the jobs it created, not on the passport of the investor. Local and foreign investors should get the same incentives, the same speed in approvals and the same certainty that the policy will not change," he said.

Punjab is not the only province that prefers foreign investors, all other provinces, including Islamabad, also want foreign investment as it brings dollars, transfer of technology and much more. However, the hue and cry is not new. Earlier, in consultative sessions on investment policy at the Lahore Chamber of Commerce and Industry, the chamber office-bearers said foreign investment could not be encouraged without promoting local investment and the confidence of local investors must be restored first. The Board of Investment says the government treats both local and foreign investors equally.

The government has offered investors in Punjab SEZs a 10-year income tax holiday and one-time duty-free import of machinery, and has described these as open to both domestic and international investors. Businessmen say the real test is whether those benefits reach a small or medium-sized local firm as easily as a large foreign company.

The need for fresh capital is clear. UN Comtrade data shows Austria bought about $428.52 million of Pakistani goods in 2025, mostly clothing and textile, a growth of 20%, while Pakistan imported goods worth $115.73 million from Austria. Austrian investment in energy, dairy and agriculture is still small compared with textile trade.

Punjab is not the only province competing for capital. Sindh, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan also have SEZs, with many linked to the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor. Punjab's advantages include its large domestic market and industrial clusters in Faisalabad, Sialkot, Gujranwala and Gujrat. Businessmen say these advantages will matter more if investors see the same rules for everyone.

The meeting produced agreements in areas of cooperation, including hydroelectric power, technical education, tourism, garments, leather, footwear and livestock. However, it did not announce any specific projects, investment figures or timelines. Whether the talks lead to investment may depend on how Punjab treats investors who are already there.

headline: Oil set for 4th straight monthly gains
description: Oil set for 4th straight monthly gains
author: Reuters
article_text:
Oil prices rose on Friday to their highest levels since the end of April, putting them on track for a fourth straight month of gains, as traders braced for a potential escalation in the US-Iran war after the US midterm elections, with an attack on a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz highlighting supply risks.

Brent crude futures for December, which expired on Friday, were up $2.28, or 2.5%, at $117.75 a barrel as of 1707 GMT, after touching a high of $118. The more active January contract gained $3.23 to $114.03. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures climbed $2.74, or 2.7%, to $104.79. For the month, Brent was on course to finish 13% higher, while WTI was heading for a 15% jump.

"Traders will remain focused on oil flows out of the Middle East and the likely escalation by the US and allied forces," said Dennis Kissler, Senior Vice President of Trading at BOK Financial.

On Friday, a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz – the key sea outlet for Gulf crude and fuel supplies – was hit by explosive devices attached by a small boat, said the UKMTO, the British maritime security service. It was not immediately clear who was behind the attack. It was the first known successful strike using limpet mines, explosives that are attached to a ship's hull from a small boat, in the waterway since the US-Israel war with Iran began in February, maritime sources said.

headline: Profit-taking snaps four-day rally at PSX
description: Profit-taking snaps four-day rally at PSX
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
The KSE-100 index of the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) closed lower on Friday, shedding around 785 points and ending October down by 2.09% month-on-month. Rising oil prices, driven by fears of heightened US-Iran tensions after midterm elections, and reports of tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz weighed on sentiment. Profit-taking after the recent rally on September-quarter results added to the pressure.

At the close of trading, the benchmark KSE-100 index posted a loss of 784.19 points, or 0.47%, and settled at 166,409.25.

Arif Habib Limited (AHL) reported that the KSE-100 slipped 0.47% to close the month around 166,400, with UBL, LUCK and HBL among the major drags. OGDC's strong first-quarter results (EPS up 53% year-on-year to Rs13.60 and a dividend of Rs5 per share), driven by higher oil and gas output plus other income, provided some relief amid elevated oil prices, while support was reported near 160k.

Topline's daily market review noted that the market remained largely in negative territory during the last trading session of the week, when the index declined 0.47% to close at 166,409. The bearish sentiment was primarily driven by rising crude oil prices amid expectations of heightened US-Iran tensions following the US midterm elections, coupled with reported attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, raising concerns over potential supply disruptions.

Additionally, investors resorted to profit-taking following the recent market rally driven by September-quarter financial results. Top negative contributors to the index were UBL, LUCK, HBL, FATIMA and ATRL, as they cumulatively wiped off 359 points. Traded value-wise, CNERGY (Rs1.57 billion), OGDC (Rs953 million), THCCL (Rs794 million), SAZEW (Rs530 million) and PSO (Rs510 billion) dominated the activity.

Topline reported in its monthly review that the KSE-100 dipped 2.09% on a month-on-month basis during October, primarily due to geopolitical uncertainty, foreign portfolio outflows, profit-taking in heavyweight stocks and cautious investor sentiment over global financial market volatility and domestic macroeconomic concerns.

Major developments during the month included a moderation in Pakistan's CPI inflation to 10.26% in September 2026, compared to 11.15% in August 2026, while remaining above 5.76% recorded in September 2025. Automobile sales declined 12% YoY and 3% MoM to 15,104 units, as reported by the auto manufacturers association.

Overall trading volumes were recorded at 825.47 million shares compared with the previous session's tally of 816.83 million. The value of shares traded during the day was Rs23.12 billion. Shares of 501 companies were traded. Of these, 173 stocks closed higher, 300 fell, and 28 remained unchanged.

Pervez Ahmed Consultancy was the volume leader with trading in 165.86 million shares, losing Rs0.44 to close at Rs3.96. It was followed by Cnergyico PK with 111.99 million shares, losing Rs0.44 to close at Rs13.64, and First National Equities with 40.46 million shares, gaining Rs0.01 to close at Rs1.13. Foreign investors sold shares worth Rs6.2 billion, the National Clearing Company reported.

headline: Bank profits slip 1%to Rs505b
description: Bank profits slip 1% to Rs505b
author: Shazia Tasneem Farooqi
article_text:
The banking sector recorded a marginal decline in profitability in the first nine months of calendar year 2026 as higher interest expenses and operating costs offset growth in non-interest income and lower taxation, an Arif Habib Limited (AHL) report showed.

Banks posted a consolidated profit after tax of Rs505 billion, down 1% year-on-year. Total interest earned rose 6% while interest expenses climbed 9%, leaving net interest income flat at Rs1.6 trillion compared with the same period last year.

The average policy rate stood at approximately 11.1% against 11.4% a year earlier, though earnings shifted as banks realigned balance sheets ahead of expected rate volatility from the US-Iran conflict.

Average interest yield fell to about 11% from 13%, while average cost of funds declined to around 6% from 8%, taking the sector-wide net interest margin to approximately 4%.

Non-interest income grew about 18% to Rs504 billion, driven by fee income up 11%, foreign exchange income up 36% and capital gains up 30%.

The sector recorded a net provisioning reversal of about Rs21 billion against Rs8 billion a year earlier, with National Bank of Pakistan posting the largest at Rs6 billion, followed by United Bank Limited at Rs4.4 billion and Bank Alfalah Limited at Rs3.2 billion, on improving recoveries from specific lending portfolios.

Operating expenses reached Rs1.1 trillion, up about 15%. Meezan Bank Limited recorded the lowest cost-to-income ratio at 32%, followed by Standard Chartered Bank Pakistan Limited at 33% and UBL at 38%.

Effective taxation declined to 53%, partly offsetting a 5% fall in pre-tax profit and leaving the bottom line down 1%.

On a quarterly basis, listed banks recorded a combined profit of Rs164 billion, down 3% year-on-year and 2% quarter-on-quarter.

Following a 100-basis-point policy rate hike in the second quarter of calendar year 2026, average yields on assets expanded to about 11% in the third quarter from 10.7% in the preceding quarter. Average cost of funds rose to around 6.4% from 6.1%.

Quarterly interest earned stood at about Rs1.6 trillion while interest expenses amounted to Rs1.1 trillion, increases of 13% and 18% year-on-year respectively.

Non-interest income declined 4.6% sequentially, primarily due to normalisation in capital gains, reported at Rs154 billion during the quarter.

Average interest yield fell to about 11% from 13%, while average cost of funds declined to around 6% from 8%, taking the sector-wide net interest margin to approximately 4%.

headline: SME financing doublesto Rs1.1tr
description: SME financing doubles to Rs1.1tr
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Outstanding financing to small and medium enterprises (SMEs) rose to approximately Rs1,110 billion in June 2026 from Rs491 billion in June 2024, with borrowers climbing to 325,000 from 177,000, State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) Governor Jameel Ahmad said, announcing that the collateral-free limit for SME loans had been raised from Rs10 million to Rs50 million.

He was addressing the Lahore Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI), according to a statement issued on Friday.

The definition of SMEs has also been revised, with the annual turnover limit for small enterprises raised from Rs150 million to Rs400 million and for medium enterprises from Rs800 million to Rs2 billion, so that businesses with turnover of up to Rs2 billion can now access SME financing.

Financing stood at Rs691 billion in June 2025 with 275,000 borrowers, he said.

Ahmad said the SBP, with the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Authority (SMEDA) and commercial banks, had cut the SME loan application form to a single page, and that the SME Connect Portal would become operational on November 1, 2026, allowing entrepreneurs to apply online from their homes and track progress.

He said the limit under the Export Refinance Scheme had been raised from Rs1 trillion to Rs1.5 trillion, of which Rs300 billion is allocated for SME exporters, and that the cabinet had approved a 10-year long-term export financing scheme to support export-oriented investment.

Under the government's revised housing finance scheme, banks approved Rs521 billion for about 80,000 applicants in six to seven months, against outstanding housing finance of Rs251 billion before the March 2026 revision. Loans under the Prime Minister's Youth Business and Agriculture Scheme carry mark-up rates of zero to 7%.

LCCI President Ali Hussam Asghar proposed a joint financing mechanism involving industry, government, EXIM Bank and commercial banks, selecting 1,000 SMEs on available data, identifying their obstacles and developing a replicable facilitation model. He urged the SBP to link its complaint centre with the LCCI's to help importers and exporters facing delays in opening letters of credit, and said a clear timeline should be set for resolving complaints.

Senior Vice President Sardar Usman Ghani said Islamic banking accounted for 39.1% of total financing but only 15.9% of SME financing, proposing a minimum 5.9% target that could add Rs204 billion, in line with the sector average. He said the bad-debt ratio in Islamic banks' SME portfolio was 2.2% against 5.5% for the overall banking sector.

The definition of SMEs has also been revised, with the annual turnover limit for small enterprises raised from Rs150 million to Rs400 million and for medium enterprises from Rs800 million to Rs2 billion, so that businesses with turnover of up to Rs2 billion can now access SME financing.
Financing stood at Rs691 billion in June 2025 with 275,000 borrowers, he said.

Ahmad said the SBP, with the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Authority (SMEDA) and commercial banks, had cut the SME loan application form to a single page, and that the SME Connect Portal would become operational on November 1, 2026, allowing entrepreneurs to apply online from their homes and track progress.

He said the limit under the Export Refinance Scheme had been raised from Rs1 trillion to Rs1.5 trillion, of which Rs300 billion is allocated for SME exporters, and that the cabinet had approved a 10-year long-term export financing scheme to support export-oriented investment.

Under the government's revised housing finance scheme, banks approved Rs521 billion for about 80,000 applicants in six to seven months, against outstanding housing finance of Rs251 billion before the March 2026 revision. Loans under the Prime Minister's Youth Business and Agriculture Scheme carry mark-up rates of zero to 7%.

LCCI President Ali Hussam Asghar proposed a joint financing mechanism involving industry, government, EXIM Bank and commercial banks, selecting 1,000 SMEs on available data, identifying their obstacles and developing a replicable facilitation model. He urged the SBP to link its complaint centre with the LCCI's to help importers and exporters facing delays in opening letters of credit, and said a clear timeline should be set for resolving complaints.

Senior Vice President Sardar Usman Ghani said Islamic banking accounted for 39.1% of total financing but only 15.9% of SME financing, proposing a minimum 5.9% target that could add Rs204 billion, in line with the sector average. He said the bad-debt ratio in Islamic banks' SME portfolio was 2.2% against 5.5% for the overall banking sector.

headline: FBR faces first tax shortfall of FY27
description: FBR faces first tax shortfall of FY27
author: Shahbaz Rana
article_text:
The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) collected Rs4.06 trillion in taxes during the first four months of the current fiscal year, facing a shortfall of Rs124 billion but clinging to hopes that it would receive a few more billions along with tax returns on Saturday.

The July-October collection results have been closely watched that came on the heels of two unusual developments – the government's proposal to establish a new tax agency, which it later shelved, and adverse action against office-bearers of the Inland Revenue Service Officers Association for threatening to observe a pen-down strike.

By the last official working day of the month, Friday, the FBR could bag Rs4.06 trillion for the July-October period of the current fiscal year despite setting a relatively low target, according to provisional figures compiled till late in the evening.

The collection was a mere Rs220 billion, or nearly 6%, higher than the last fiscal year but was far lower than the 17% pace needed to achieve the annual target.

For October, tax receipts remained at Rs974 billion, falling short of the target of Rs1.132 trillion by Rs158 billion. The increase in the monthly collection was only Rs23 billion, or 2.5%, compared to a year ago.

However, the tax authorities were hopeful that they could receive Rs20 billion to Rs25 billion along with income tax returns on October 31, the last day of the twice extended deadline for filing returns. The taxes paid along with returns were not portraying a healthy trend, although the number of returns was higher.

As of October 28, compared to the Rs88.5 billion income tax paid along with returns last year, the tax department received Rs85.2 billion this year. Authorities were hopeful that the figure would cross Rs100 billion by late Saturday evening. This will lower the tax shortfall but will not eliminate it.

A few days ago, the government had discussed the idea of either establishing a new tax agency or outsourcing the functions of the FBR. After coming to know about the government's plans, the IRS Officers Association threatened to stage a pen-down strike. The association withdrew from its threat following assurance from the FBR member operations that no adverse action would be taken against them.

However, the FBR suspended two officers and posted another seven in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan on suspicion that they were behind the pen-down strike move. The association president escaped suspension or being deputed in a province.

Tax collection

The FBR got Rs4.06 trillion in taxes during July-October of the current fiscal year, missing the target by Rs124 billion. There was a slim growth of 6%, or Rs220 billion, over the same period of last fiscal year. The numbers will improve after more payments are received along with tax returns in the next 24 hours, in addition to import taxes.

For the current fiscal year, the government and the IMF have given a Rs15.263 trillion annual tax target to the FBR. This requires a 17.4% growth over last year's collection. Unlike in the past, the IMF has made it binding to meet tax goals and the approval of the sixth loan tranche would be contingent upon achieving the first-half target.

However, sources said that the FBR's internal assessment indicated that it would be able to hit Rs14.3 to Rs14.6 trillion by the end of the current fiscal year in June 2027, thus there would be a shortfall.

According to the provisional figures, the revenue board received Rs1.85 trillion in income tax, missing the four-month target by Rs165 billion. For the fourth consecutive month, sales tax collection remained higher than the target. The FBR got Rs1.515 trillion worth of sales tax, exceeding the target by Rs67 billion. Four-month sales tax receipts were higher by Rs155 billion, or 11.3%.

Federal excise duty collection stood at Rs277 billion, almost equal to the target as it grew only 6.5%. Customs duty payments reached Rs424 billion, which was Rs25 billion lower than the target and almost at last year's level with no growth.

headline: National Grid Co plans to issue Rs100b Sukuk
description: National Grid Co plans to issue Rs100b Sukuk
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
National Grid Company of Pakistan Limited is planning to issue Sukuk worth up to Rs100 billion, of which the inaugural Shariah-compliant bonds will have an issue size of Rs20 billion with a 10-year maturity.

The proposed Sukuk offer came up for discussion at the fourth meeting of the Capital Market Development Council on Friday, chaired by Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb. It reviewed progress on capital market reforms, with particular emphasis on deepening Pakistan's corporate debt market, expanding the issuer and investor base, improving market infrastructure and facilitating access to long-term financing.

The Sukuk is intended to be floated in tranches through public offerings on the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX), subject to requisite approvals and market conditions. The finance minister saw the initiative as an important opportunity to demonstrate the potential of listed corporate debt instruments and encourage similar issuances by other entities.

The council was informed that corporate debt issuances reached Rs291 billion during January-September 2026, following Rs326 billion raised in 2025, representing a 30% increase over 2024. The market also witnessed 12 new listed corporate debt issuances worth Rs45.4 billion between February 2025 and September 2026, reflecting growing activity in Sukuk and other debt instruments. The council underscored the importance of encouraging more public offerings and enabling a wider range of businesses to access capital market financing.
