description: Hackers steal $6.3b from Binance
author: Reuters
article_text:
Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a theft that analysts blamed on North Korea and said could be the largest financial heist of all time.

Cryptocurrency prices fell on the news, while Binance halted withdrawals and said it would use company funds to cover the losses. Stablecoin issuers including El Salvador-based Tether and the Trump-backed World Liberty Financial froze about half of the stolen assets.

The exchange said customer funds were safe and it was working with partners to freeze some of the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It said earlier on Friday it expected to resume withdrawal services in the next 48 hours. It did not mention the status of the remaining $3.3 billion, but Binance co-CEO Yi He said in a post on X that $3 billion represented only about 2% of the company's total user assets and public reserves.

Binance said it had set aside around $6.34 billion of company funds internally to cover the losses. The company has a $1 billion bitcoin reserve fund designed to protect customer assets in the event of security breaches, according to its website. Binance founder Changpeng Zhao said on X that the company owned SpaceX shares worth more than $1 billion.

Binance other co-CEO, Richard Teng, said in a post on X that the breach as a "complex attack" that was not carried out by one person and included a compromised laptop as well as malicious software designed to delete evidence of its activity as it went along, "making it more difficult for us to trace and investigate."

The hackers were able to manipulate a system used to approve transactions to move money out of a Binance-controlled, internet-connected so-called "hot" wallet in a way that did not pass through normal approval controls, Teng said.

"Rest assured that we are working non-stop to resolve this, to make

the users whole, and live up to your trust," Teng wrote.

headline: First Parkinson's patient receives stem-cell therapy
description: First Parkinson's patient receives stem-cell therapy
author: AFP
article_text:
A patient has undergone pioneering stem-cell therapy to treat Parkinson's disease, the Japanese drugmaker behind the treatment said on Friday, in a world-first following its conditional approval in the country.

Sumitomo Pharma's treatment involves transplanting millions of induced Pluripotent Stem (iPS) cells, which have the potential to develop into any cell in the body, into a patient's brain.

Japanese regulators approved the groundbreaking therapy in March, following a successful clinical trial.

"The first transplant was performed at Kyoto University Hospital in October," the company said on Friday in an earnings press release, without giving further details.

Parkinson's disease is a chronic, degenerative neurological disorder that affects the body's motor system, often causing shaking and other difficulties with movement.

Worldwide, more than 10 million people are estimated to have the illness, according to the Parkinson's Foundation.

Currently available therapies "improve symptoms without slowing or halting the disease progression", it says.

iPS cells are created by inducing mature, already specialised cells to return to a juvenile state.

Under Sumitomo Pharma's treatment, iPS cells from healthy donors are developed into the precursors of dopamine-producing brain cells, which are no longer present in people with Parkinson's.

During a clinical trial, seven patients aged between 50 and 69 each received implants of either five million or 10 million cells on both sides of the brain.

headline: Six killed in India helicopter crash
description: Six killed in India helicopter crash
author: Reuters
article_text:
.

Six people were killed in a helicopter crash in the Indian Himalayan state of Uttarakhand on Friday, news agency ANI reported, citing an official from the state's civil aviation authority.

The helicopter was flying from Badrinath, a prominent pilgrimage destination for Hindus located in the mountains, to Dehradun city, the Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority (UCADA) said in a statement.

All six people on board the chopper, including five passengers and the pilot, were killed, ANI reported, citing UCADA's Chief Executive Officer Prateek Jain. "The helicopter lost communication while it was flying over Joshimath valley.

headline: Rifts mar G20 summit in Atlanta
description: Rifts mar G20 summit in Atlanta
author: Reuters
article_text:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged fellow G20 foreign ministers on Friday to work together for greater geopolitical stability and economic prosperity, warning that a series of crises posed serious threats to the global economic order.

But Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov's participation in the two-day gathering in Atlanta has roiled many G20 ministers, aggravating deep rifts over the wars in Ukraine and the Middle Eastthat experts and diplomats say could thwart real progress at the meeting.

Canada's foreign minister, Anita Anand, who has been critical of Lavrov's participation, missed the opening plenary session. Her spokeswoman said she was arriving late from a Canada-EU summit in Montreal.

South Africa's minister was also absent, not invited by the US, which holds this year's rotating presidency.

A traditional G20 family photo was left off Rubio's official schedule after some European officials said they would not be photographed with Lavrov. A third of the participants objected, including Australia and Canada, a Western diplomat said.

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul told reporters that he expected the family photo to be scrapped entirely, adding, "In no case will there be a family photo with European partners and Mr. Lavrov together because, as I said yesterday, there is no normalcy with Russia."

The US has sought to focus its allies on trade imbalances while building a coalition to counter China's control of critical minerals, but the wars and their economic impact remain the top concern for many G20 members.

In his opening remarks, Rubio said the world faced various crises that threatened global energy and food supply, trade, and the freedom of navigation.

"We are tasked, on behalf of the nations that we serve, to work together with one another to coordinate responses to emerging crises and to protect our shared interests," he said. "We can help set the context for expanded geopolitical stability and the broader economic prosperity agenda that our leaders will tackle."

With G20 members Russia, China and middle powers such as Brazil and India trying to navigate US-China strategic competition, you have "much more of a split than we've ever had," said Heidi Crebo-Rediker, who was chief economist at the State Department during the Obama administration.

Over the past decade or so, G7 countries would at least "have agreed a coordinated platform before they came to the G20, but now we don't even really have that," she added.

But Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov's participation in the two-day gathering in Atlanta has roiled many G20 ministers, aggravating deep rifts over the wars in Ukraine and the Middle Eastthat experts and diplomats say could thwart real progress at the meeting.

Canada's foreign minister, Anita Anand, who has been critical of Lavrov's participation, missed the opening plenary session. Her spokeswoman said she was arriving late from a Canada-EU summit in Montreal.

South Africa's minister was also absent, not invited by the US, which holds this year's rotating presidency.

A traditional G20 family photo was left off Rubio's official schedule after some European officials said they would not be photographed with Lavrov. A third of the participants objected, including Australia and Canada, a Western diplomat said.

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul told reporters that he expected the family photo to be scrapped entirely, adding, "In no case will there be a family photo with European partners and Mr. Lavrov together because, as I said yesterday, there is no normalcy with Russia."

The US has sought to focus its allies on trade imbalances while building a coalition to counter China's control of critical minerals, but the wars and their economic impact remain the top concern for many G20 members.

In his opening remarks, Rubio said the world faced various crises that threatened global energy and food supply, trade, and the freedom of navigation.

"We are tasked, on behalf of the nations that we serve, to work together with one another to coordinate responses to emerging crises and to protect our shared interests," he said. "We can help set the context for expanded geopolitical stability and the broader economic prosperity agenda that our leaders will tackle."

With G20 members Russia, China and middle powers such as Brazil and India trying to navigate US-China strategic competition, you have "much more of a split than we've ever had," said Heidi Crebo-Rediker, who was chief economist at the State Department during the Obama administration.

Over the past decade or so, G7 countries would at least "have agreed a coordinated platform before they came to the G20, but now we don't even really have that," she added.

headline: Pope Leo first pontiff to cast US ballot
description: Pope Leo first pontiff to cast US ballot
author: Reuters
article_text:
.

Oct 30 (Reuters) - Pope Leo XIV cast a ballot by mail in the US midterm elections, the Vatican press office said on Friday, a historic first for the American-born pontiff.

"In keeping with this long-standing practice of civic participation, he has submitted his mail-in ballot in Chicago," the Vatican said. "The Holy Father expresses his belief in the right and the duty of citizens to participate in democratic processes."

The Vatican did not say which candidates Leo had voted for.

Leo, 71, was born in Chicago and is the first American-born pope. The pope voted by mail under his birth name, Robert Francis Prevost, according to the Will County Clerk's website.

President Donald Trump's sagging popularity is hurting his fellow Republicans' chances of holding onto their majorities in both chambers of Congress in the November 3 election, with the public unhappy about the high cost of living and the Iran war.

Trump repeatedly criticized Leo early in the new pope's tenure, calling him "weak" and "terrible" on crime.

headline: US plans to ban Chinese telecom firms
description: US plans to ban Chinese telecom firms
author: Reuters
article_text:
The United States plans to soon ban Chinese telecom firms from direct access to US phone numbers on national security grounds - a measure designed to prevent scam-related robocalls.

The US Federal Communications Commission said on Thursday that it will vote on November 19 on a proposal to ban China Mobile 600941.SS, China Telecom 601728.SS and China Unicom 0762.HK and other IP-enabled service providers from direct access.

For telecom firms providing Voice over Internet Protocol - technology that converts voice into digital data and transmits it over broadband connections - direct access is a much cheaper option and makes it easier to offer advanced features.

"With this decision, the FCC will be strengthening our first line of defense against bad actors and illegal robocallers," FCC Chair Brendan Carr said in a statement.

The Chinese Embassy in Washington criticized the action, saying it "severely hinders normal economic and trade cooperation between Chinese and American businesses and is not in the interest of any party including US companies and consumers."

The FCC also said on Thursday that it plans to bar IP-enabled service providers that use equipment from companies on the FCC's list that pose national security risks, including Huawei or ZTE 000063.SZ.

The agency added that it would ban all Chinese labs from testing US electronics in December 2028 and may also revoke direct number authorizations for Chinese companies that it deems to pose national security risks.

The FCC has previously barred China Mobile, China Telecom and China Unicom from providing international telecommunications services to the United States.

headline: Residents leave Russian-held town by bus
description: Residents leave Russian-held town by bus
author: Reuters
article_text:
Starving and exhausted residents of a Russian-held town in southern Ukraine were evacuated by bus on Friday as part of a joint relief operation by the opposing sides, the first of its kind in four years and eight months of war.

Under a local ceasefire brokered by US first lady Melania Trump, an aid convoy arrived in the town of Oleshky to distribute food and medicine.

Those wishing to leave - some for Russia, some for Ukraine - were taken initially to Russian-annexed Crimea in 25 buses and nine ambulances, Russian human rights commissioner Yana Lantratova said, before splitting into separate convoys.

Senior Ukrainian lawmaker David Arakhamia said those heading for Ukraine would be taken from there to Anapa in southern Russia before flying to Belarus and finally crossing back into Ukraine by bus - a route of more than 1,000 miles.

Although it was a striking example of cooperation between the warring sides, a spokesman for Russian President Vladimir Putin described it as "difficult to extrapolate" to the wider search for peace.

Attacks continued elsewhere, with Russian strikes overnight targeting seven regions of Ukraine, the capital Kyiv and the southeastern city of Dnipro, officials said. On Thursday, a Russian drone killed at least 15 people on a rail platform in Dnipro.

Russia said Ukraine had resumed strikes on its oil refineries despite a request from US President Donald Trump to stop such attacks, which Trump has blamed for raising the cost of diesel before midterm legislative elections next week. There was no comment from Ukraine.

It was not clear how many people had chosen to stay behind in Oleshky, which has suffered extensive war damage and was badly flooded after the destruction of the Kakhovka dam upstream from the town in 2023.

headline: Margaret Qualley and Jack Antonoff reportedly file for divorce three months after split
description: Margaret Qualley and Jack Antonoff reportedly file for divorce three months after confirming the split in July 2026
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Actress Margaret Qualley and musician Jack Antonoff have reportedly filed for divorce, three months after news of their separation became public.

According to a source cited by People, the former couple have jointly submitted divorce papers and are pursuing an uncontested divorce. The insider described the decision as mutual, saying both remain deeply fond of one another despite ending their romantic relationship.

“They share a deep affinity and love for one another, and though their romantic partnership is ending, they will absolutely be lifelong friends,” the source said.

Reports of Qualley and Antonoff’s separation first emerged in July, after the couple had been married for three years.

At the time, Qualley’s representative addressed speculation surrounding the breakup, rejecting claims of trust issues or infidelity. The representative stressed that the relationship had been built on mutual respect and partnership, adding that the pair continued to care deeply for one another.

The representative also urged the public to respect their privacy, saying people commenting on the marriage were not necessarily close to the couple.

Meanwhile, Antonoff recently discussed performing songs inspired by his relationship with Qualley following their split. In an interview with The Guardian, the musician said he had considered changing his setlist but ultimately decided to continue performing the songs as written.

He explained that being honest with his audience about his feelings was part of his relationship with them. Antonoff also described the experience of sharing the music with listeners as beautiful, despite the sadness surrounding the songs.

The musician said he did not want to rewrite the past, adding that he would rather experience something publicly than escape it privately.

Neither Qualley nor Antonoff has publicly commented on the reported divorce filing.

Actress Margaret Qualley and musician Jack Antonoff have reportedly filed for divorce, three months after news of their separation became public.

According to a source cited by People, the former couple have jointly submitted divorce papers and are pursuing an uncontested divorce. The insider described the decision as mutual, saying both remain deeply fond of one another despite ending their romantic relationship.

“They share a deep affinity and love for one another, and though their romantic partnership is ending, they will absolutely be lifelong friends,” the source said.

Reports of Qualley and Antonoff’s separation first emerged in July, after the couple had been married for three years.

At the time, Qualley’s representative addressed speculation surrounding the breakup, rejecting claims of trust issues or infidelity. The representative stressed that the relationship had been built on mutual respect and partnership, adding that the pair continued to care deeply for one another.

The representative also urged the public to respect their privacy, saying people commenting on the marriage were not necessarily close to the couple.

Meanwhile, Antonoff recently discussed performing songs inspired by his relationship with Qualley following their split. In an interview with The Guardian, the musician said he had considered changing his setlist but ultimately decided to continue performing the songs as written.

He explained that being honest with his audience about his feelings was part of his relationship with them. Antonoff also described the experience of sharing the music with listeners as beautiful, despite the sadness surrounding the songs.

The musician said he did not want to rewrite the past, adding that he would rather experience something publicly than escape it privately.

Neither Qualley nor Antonoff has publicly commented on the reported divorce filing.

headline: Dam project costs surge by Rs1.9tr
description: Dam project costs surge by Rs1.9tr
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
The depreciation of the Pakistani rupee against the US dollar in recent years has significantly driven up the cost of two major hydropower projects, adding a combined Rs1.896 trillion to their estimated expenses.

According to details presented by the Ministry of Water Resources in the National Assembly, the cost of the Diamer-Bhasha Dam increased by Rs642 billion, with its project cost rising from Rs479 billion to Rs1.121 trillion.

The ministry attributed the increase to changes in foreign exchange rates and said a revised PC-I had been submitted to the Ministry of Water Resources.

The estimated cost of the Dasu Hydropower Project also surged from Rs486 billion to Rs1.740 trillion, representing an increase of Rs1.254 trillion, or around 260%.

The government also acknowledged a sharp increase in the prices of petroleum products and construction materials, further adding to the financial burden of infrastructure projects.

According to the figures presented, the price of a cement bag rose by 204% from Rs530 to Rs1,610 while the price of high-speed diesel climbed from Rs72 to Rs414 per litre, marking an increase of 472%.

Steel and iron bars became significantly more expensive, with their price rising by 268%, from Rs72,000 to Rs265,000 per metric tonne.

The National Assembly was informed that after the dissolution of Pakistan Agricultural Storage and Services Corporation (PASSCO), letters have been sent to relevant institutions and provinces for distribution of available wheat stocks, while wheat is also being supplied to Balochistan, Azad Kashmir and other concerned areas.

Parliamentary Secretary for National Food Security and Research Shaista Khan gave the information during Question Hour in response to questions by Shahida Rehmani and Aliya Kamran.

She said wheat imports have also been made to meet requirements and imported stocks have reached warehouses. To make wheat transportation and supply to provinces transparent, a digital system has been introduced with a dashboard to monitor movement, the concerned province and complete delivery details.

In reply to a supplementary question, the Parliamentary Secretary said PASSCO had declined due to financial and administrative issues, as some provinces were not paying its dues and bills on time.

She explained that the government intends to properly involve the private sector and for this purpose relevant companies will be linked with the Ministry of National Food Security and Research.

A system is also being devised to monitor and hold private companies accountable to make wheat supply and distribution process effective.

The National Assembly on Friday passed four government bills by majority vote after clause-by-clause consideration. The bills included the Higher Education Commission (Amendment) Bill, 2026; the NFC Institute of Engineering and Technology Multan (Amendment) Bill, 2026 and the National Textile University (Amendment) Bill, 2026.

headline: Imran's sister receiving necessary medical care, Senate told
description: Imran's sister receiving necessary medical care, Senate told
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry informed the Senate on Friday that Noreen Niazi was being provided all necessary medical care and had been shifted to hospital on the recommendation of doctors.

Responding to a point raised by Senator Mohsin Aziz regarding her health condition, he said the government was particularly sensitive to the health and welfare of individuals in detention and would ensure that their rights and medical needs were fully protected.

He said Noreen Niazi was shifted to hospital on the advice of doctors, adding that decisions regarding her treatment, hospitalisation and any further medical intervention would be taken by the medical professionals concerned.

"The decision about whether a person is ill and what treatment is required rests with doctors," he said, stressing that medical care would be provided in accordance with professional advice and established procedures.

He added that her family was present at the hospital and the government had fulfilled its responsibility by arranging the necessary medical facilities.

Meanwhile, Senator Azam Swati referred to a recent telephone conversation with Hafeez Ullah Niazi, who appreciated the government for facilitating Noreen Niazi's transfer to hospital and arranging a meeting with her elder daughter.

Azam Swati described the arrangements as a positive humanitarian step and urged the government to also allow her younger daughter to meet her, saying family visits should be facilitated on humanitarian grounds.

He said the matter should be viewed from a humanitarian perspective, beyond political differences. He also called for consideration of similar relief for other family members.

headline: Karachi-Lahore private train starts chugging
description: Karachi-Lahore private train starts chugging
author: ​ Our Correspondents
article_text:
Pakistan Railways has launched the operation of the Karakoram Express under the private sector as part of its efforts to improve train services and provide passengers with modern travel facilities.

The 41-Up Karakoram Express departed from Karachi Cantt Railway Station for Lahore on Friday, marking the beginning of its operations under private management by Prime Rail. The train will also operate as the 42-Down service from Lahore to Karachi.

The 20-coach train comprises 10 economy-class coaches, two AC business-class coaches, two AC standard coaches, one AC sleeper coach, a power van, a premium lounge, a brake van and two luggage vans.

Passengers are offered facilities including mineral water, fresh meals, bedding, mobile charging points, Wi-Fi and an infotainment system. Complimentary services are also available to passengers travelling in AC sleeper and AC business classes.

Pakistan Railways has announced a 25% discount on fares across all classes until November 6. During the promotional period, it has set the AC sleeper fare at Rs12,600, AC business at Rs9,550, AC standard at Rs7,550 and economy at Rs4,150.

The train will operate on the Main Line-I (ML-1), departing simultaneously from Karachi and Lahore at 3pm. It will stop at Drigh Road, Landhi, Hyderabad, Nawabshah, Rohri, Bahawalpur, Khanewal, Sahiwal and Raiwind before reaching its destination. The journey between the two cities is expected to take around 19 hours.

Speaking on the occasion, Pakistan Railways CEO Muhammad Hafizullah said the department was working with private companies to provide passengers with modern facilities and a more comfortable travelling experience.

He said railway coaches were being upgraded while infrastructure development projects worth billions of rupees were also under way. "More trains will be outsourced to the private sector to improve services and bring them closer to international standards," he added.

The CEO said Pakistan Railways was also adopting modern technology, including improvements in its ticketing system and operational infrastructure. Under the agreement, the commercial management of the Karakoram Express has been outsourced to Prime Rail for an annual amount of Rs3.9015 billion.

Passengers can purchase tickets at reservation counters at relevant railway stations, through the Prime Rail website (primerail.pk) or its mobile application.

article_html:
KARACHI/LAHORE:

Pakistan Railways has launched the operation of the Karakoram Express under the private sector as part of its efforts to improve train services and provide passengers with modern travel facilities.

The 41-Up Karakoram Express departed from Karachi Cantt Railway Station for Lahore on Friday, marking the beginning of its operations under private management by Prime Rail. The train will also operate as the 42-Down service from Lahore to Karachi.

The 20-coach train comprises 10 economy-class coaches, two AC business-class coaches, two AC standard coaches, one AC sleeper coach, a power van, a premium lounge, a brake van and two luggage vans.

Passengers are offered facilities including mineral water, fresh meals, bedding, mobile charging points, Wi-Fi and an infotainment system. Complimentary services are also available to passengers travelling in AC sleeper and AC business classes.

Pakistan Railways has announced a 25% discount on fares across all classes until November 6. During the promotional period, it has set the AC sleeper fare at Rs12,600, AC business at Rs9,550, AC standard at Rs7,550 and economy at Rs4,150.

The train will operate on the Main Line-I (ML-1), departing simultaneously from Karachi and Lahore at 3pm. It will stop at Drigh Road, Landhi, Hyderabad, Nawabshah, Rohri, Bahawalpur, Khanewal, Sahiwal and Raiwind before reaching its destination. The journey between the two cities is expected to take around 19 hours.

Speaking on the occasion, Pakistan Railways CEO Muhammad Hafizullah said the department was working with private companies to provide passengers with modern facilities and a more comfortable travelling experience.

He said railway coaches were being upgraded while infrastructure development projects worth billions of rupees were also under way. "More trains will be outsourced to the private sector to improve services and bring them closer to international standards," he added.

The CEO said Pakistan Railways was also adopting modern technology, including improvements in its ticketing system and operational infrastructure. Under the agreement, the commercial management of the Karakoram Express has been outsourced to Prime Rail for an annual amount of Rs3.9015 billion.

Passengers can purchase tickets at reservation counters at relevant railway stations, through the Prime Rail website (primerail.pk) or its mobile application.

headline: Family found stabbed to death in Skardu house
description: Family found stabbed to death in Skardu house
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
.

A married couple and their two young children were stabbed to death by unidentified assailants at their home in Skardu.

The bodies of all four family members were found at a house behind Madania Colony.

According to police sources, the victims were attacked with repeated knife blows during the night while they were asleep. The deceased man belonged to Talu Broq, while his wife was from Parachinar.

The couple had contracted a court marriage some time ago. Their two children, a five-year-old daughter and a two-and-a-half-year-old son, were also killed in the attack.

headline: 24m children to get polio drops in upcoming drive
description: 24m children to get polio drops in upcoming drive
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
.

The government on Friday launched a nationwide sub-national polio vaccination campaign targeting approximately 24 million children in 97 high-risk districts from November 2 to 8.

The campaign was launched at the National Emergency Operations Centre (NEOC) for Polio Eradication.

The drive will mobilize more than 200,000 frontline polio workers to administer oral polio vaccine to children under five. It will run simultaneously in Pakistan and Afghanistan, the last two countries where wild poliovirus remains endemic, with coordinated cross-border efforts to prevent its spread.

24m children to get polio drops in upcoming drive

.

Our Correspondent October 31, 2026 Less than a minute read
facebook twitter whatsup linkded email
ISLAMABAD:

The government on Friday launched a nationwide sub-national polio vaccination campaign targeting approximately 24 million children in 97 high-risk districts from November 2 to 8.

The campaign was launched at the National Emergency Operations Centre (NEOC) for Polio Eradication.

The drive will mobilize more than 200,000 frontline polio workers to administer oral polio vaccine to children under five. It will run simultaneously in Pakistan and Afghanistan, the last two countries where wild poliovirus remains endemic, with coordinated cross-border efforts to prevent its spread.

headline: SC rules almonds, cashews not smuggled goods
description: SC rules almonds, cashews not smuggled goods
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
The Supreme Court has ruled that shelled almonds and cashews do not fall within the specific categories of smuggled goods listed under the Customs Act, observing that a violation of import restrictions alone does not automatically render goods legally smuggled.

The court dismissed appeals filed by customs authorities against Balochistan High Court judgments, holding that the phrase "all kinds of food grains and food items" used in the relevant notification could not be interpreted so broadly as to include distinct categories of goods such as almonds and cashews.

According to the detailed judgment authored by Justice Muhammad Shafi Siddiqui, a three-member bench comprising Chief Justice of Pakistan Justice Yahya Afridi, Justice Muhammad Shafi Siddiqui and Justice Mian Gul Hassan Aurangzeb heard the customs authorities' appeals on October 8, 2026.

According to the case record, customs officials intercepted vehicles transporting foreign-origin almonds and cashews in Nokkundi on October 20, 2024, following a tip-off. The goods declarations presented by the drivers did not match the customs record, as the relevant declarations pertained to Iranian raisins and contained different vehicle details.

The customs authorities ordered the seizure of the goods and the vehicles used for their transportation. However, the Customs Appellate Tribunal allowed the release of the goods subject to payment of applicable duties and taxes and a penalty equivalent to 20 per cent of their customs value. It also set aside the seizure of the vehicles.

The Balochistan High Court subsequently dismissed the customs authorities' challenges to the tribunal's decisions.

headline: NAB law tweaks benefitted politicians, bureaucrats
description: NAB law tweaks benefitted politicians, bureaucrats
author: RAZZAk ABRO
article_text:
Accountability proceedings against some of the country's most prominent political figures have taken a turn in their favour following amendments to the National Accountability Act in 2022, with several high-profile investigations either closed or transferred to provincial anti-corruption authorities and regular courts.

The list of beneficiaries includes former prime ministers, sitting chief ministers, federal and provincial ministers, former senators and influential businessmen, raising questions about the impact of the legislative changes on accountability, particularly in cases involving public office-holders.

In March this year, an accountability court in Lahore approved the closure of NAB investigations against Punjab CM Maryam Nawaz and her father, former PM Nawaz Sharif, in the Chaudhry Sugar Mills money laundering case.

The same month, a Sindh anti-corruption court acquitted provincial minister Sharjeel Inam Memon in two cases transferred from NAB to the provincial Anti-Corruption Establishment (ACE) following the amendments. The cases related to alleged abuse of authority and misappropriation of government advertisements.

Earlier, in October 2024, Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah was acquitted in the Noriabad Power Plant case after NAB withdrew its reference in the wake of the changes to the accountability law.

Former prime ministers Nawaz Sharif and Yousaf Raza Gilani were among the first prominent beneficiaries of the amendments when an Islamabad accountability court halted proceedings in the high-profile Toshakhana case after taking into account the revised NAB law.

Other politicians and public figures who have benefited from the changes include former prime ministers Shaukat Aziz and Raja Pervez Ashraf, former finance minister Shaukat Tarin, former Balochistan chief minister Nawab Aslam Raisani, former senator Lashkari Raisani and businessman Anwar Majeed, among others.

The 2022 amendments significantly narrowed NAB's jurisdiction by excluding certain matters relating to decisions, policies, advice, development projects and official functions of public office-holders. The bureau's jurisdiction was also restricted by removing offences involving amounts below Rs500 million from its ambit.

More than 500 cases involving politicians and government officials were affected by the legislative changes. Subsequently, NAB closed investigations in several matters, while others were transferred to provincial anti-corruption departments and regular courts.

The amendments have also triggered criticism over their implications for governance and bureaucratic accountability, particularly in Sindh. Critics argue that the threat of NAB proceedings had previously made government officials cautious about approving files and signing official decisions, with some allegedly reluctant to exercise their authority for fear of prosecution.

They contend that the revised law has eased this pressure, potentially weakening the deterrent against misuse of authority and irregularities in public administration.

However, the closure or transfer of an investigation does not automatically establish the innocence or guilt of those named in a case. Each matter remains subject to its own legal proceedings, evidence and judicial findings.

Meanwhile, in the latest development, at least 19 corruption references previously transferred from NAB to provincial anti-corruption authorities have returned to accountability courts following a Sindh High Court ruling, with proceedings now being restored.

Different accountability courts have issued notices to individuals nominated in the references, directing them to appear as hearings resume in cases involving alleged illegal allotment of government land in Karachi and other corruption charges.

The development follows a June 29, 2026 order by an SHC division bench comprising Justice Muhammad Saleem Jessar and Justice Nisar Ahmed Banbhro.

The court ruled that the 2022 amendments to the NAB law did not automatically remove all pending corruption references from accountability courts' jurisdiction.

article_html:
KARACHI:

Accountability proceedings against some of the country's most prominent political figures have taken a turn in their favour following amendments to the National Accountability Act in 2022, with several high-profile investigations either closed or transferred to provincial anti-corruption authorities and regular courts.

The list of beneficiaries includes former prime ministers, sitting chief ministers, federal and provincial ministers, former senators and influential businessmen, raising questions about the impact of the legislative changes on accountability, particularly in cases involving public office-holders.

In March this year, an accountability court in Lahore approved the closure of NAB investigations against Punjab CM Maryam Nawaz and her father, former PM Nawaz Sharif, in the Chaudhry Sugar Mills money laundering case.

The same month, a Sindh anti-corruption court acquitted provincial minister Sharjeel Inam Memon in two cases transferred from NAB to the provincial Anti-Corruption Establishment (ACE) following the amendments. The cases related to alleged abuse of authority and misappropriation of government advertisements.

Earlier, in October 2024, Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah was acquitted in the Noriabad Power Plant case after NAB withdrew its reference in the wake of the changes to the accountability law.

Former prime ministers Nawaz Sharif and Yousaf Raza Gilani were among the first prominent beneficiaries of the amendments when an Islamabad accountability court halted proceedings in the high-profile Toshakhana case after taking into account the revised NAB law.

Other politicians and public figures who have benefited from the changes include former prime ministers Shaukat Aziz and Raja Pervez Ashraf, former finance minister Shaukat Tarin, former Balochistan chief minister Nawab Aslam Raisani, former senator Lashkari Raisani and businessman Anwar Majeed, among others.

The 2022 amendments significantly narrowed NAB's jurisdiction by excluding certain matters relating to decisions, policies, advice, development projects and official functions of public office-holders. The bureau's jurisdiction was also restricted by removing offences involving amounts below Rs500 million from its ambit.

More than 500 cases involving politicians and government officials were affected by the legislative changes. Subsequently, NAB closed investigations in several matters, while others were transferred to provincial anti-corruption departments and regular courts.

The amendments have also triggered criticism over their implications for governance and bureaucratic accountability, particularly in Sindh. Critics argue that the threat of NAB proceedings had previously made government officials cautious about approving files and signing official decisions, with some allegedly reluctant to exercise their authority for fear of prosecution.

They contend that the revised law has eased this pressure, potentially weakening the deterrent against misuse of authority and irregularities in public administration.

However, the closure or transfer of an investigation does not automatically establish the innocence or guilt of those named in a case. Each matter remains subject to its own legal proceedings, evidence and judicial findings.

Meanwhile, in the latest development, at least 19 corruption references previously transferred from NAB to provincial anti-corruption authorities have returned to accountability courts following a Sindh High Court ruling, with proceedings now being restored.

Different accountability courts have issued notices to individuals nominated in the references, directing them to appear as hearings resume in cases involving alleged illegal allotment of government land in Karachi and other corruption charges.

The development follows a June 29, 2026 order by an SHC division bench comprising Justice Muhammad Saleem Jessar and Justice Nisar Ahmed Banbhro.

The court ruled that the 2022 amendments to the NAB law did not automatically remove all pending corruption references from accountability courts' jurisdiction.

headline: NA resolution on workplace harassment
description: NA resolution on workplace harassment
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
The National Assembly on Friday unanimously passed a resolution reaffirming parliament's commitment to protecting the dignity, equality and rights of every individual against all forms of workplace harassment and gender-based discrimination.

Member of the National Assembly and Secretary of the Women's Parliamentary Caucus (WPC), Dr Shahida Rehmani, moved the resolution in the House.

The resolution underscores that workplace harassment is not limited to conduct of a sexual nature but may also manifest itself through gender-based discrimination, intimidation, humiliation, degrading treatment, hostile behaviour and misuse of authority, whether sexual or non-sexual in nature.

It reaffirms the legislative intent and protections enshrined in the Protection against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010, as amended in 2022, which expressly recognises discrimination on the basis of gender, whether sexual or non-sexual, within the statutory framework of harassment.

The resolution further emphasises that the absence of a sexual advance or demand does not diminish the seriousness of gender-based harassment or discrimination. It states that the dignity of individuals cannot be subjected to narrow distinctions between different forms of harassment and that all conduct falling within the scope of the law must be addressed with equal seriousness, fairness and accountability.

Through this resolution, the National Assembly has called upon the Federal Government and all concerned institutions to ensure the effective implementation of existing legislation in its entirety, ensuring that no individual is deprived of statutory protection merely because the reported harassment or gender-based discrimination is non-sexual in nature.

The initiative also reinforces the broader commitment of the Women's Parliamentary Caucus to ensuring that workplaces across Pakistan remain free from harassment, intimidation, humiliation and discrimination.

The resolution reaffirmed that a workplace free from harassment, humiliation and gender-based discrimination is not a privilege but a fundamental requirement of human dignity, equality and justice.

The 2010 Act describes harassment as "any unwelcome sexual advance, request for sexual favours or other verbal or written communication or physical conduct of a sexual nature or sexually demeaning attitudes, causing interference with work performance or creating an intimidating, hostile or offensive work environment, or the attempt to punish the complainant for refusal to comply to such a request or is made a condition for employment".

headline: Envoys briefed on minerals forum
description: Envoys briefed on minerals forum
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Friday held a pre-event briefing for ambassadors and diplomats based here to familiarise them with the upcoming Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum 2026 (PMIF26).

The session provided an overview of PMIF26, including its concept, major thematic sessions, programme outline, venue, registration process and participation opportunities for ministers, diplomats, international investors and industry leaders.

The participants were also briefed on the planned exhibition and opportunities for government-to-government (G2G) and government-to-business (G2B) engagements.

headline: PM to visit Moscow in 1st week of December
description: PM to visit Moscow in 1st week of December
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif is going to visit Russia in the first week of December along with a big trade delegation.

According to sources, PM Shehbaz chaired a meeting to review preparations for his upcoming Moscow visit. They said Shehbaz will be accompanied on this visit by a large delegation of businessmen and that he will also address a joint business forum in the Russian capital

During the visit, the prime minister will also hold bilateral talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Shehbaz will be the second Pakistani prime minister to visit the Russian capital in recent years.

headline: CDA targets JUI-F chief's properties
description: CDA targets JUI-F chief's properties
author: Naeem Asghar
article_text:
Just days after JUIF-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman's scathing criticism of the PML-N led federal government, the Capital Development Authority (CDA) issued notices to the properties and seminaries associated with the JUI-F chief in Islamabad for alleged violation of CDA by-laws.

The CDA has pasted a notice at the Islamabad residence of Fazl. The authority has ordered the removal of a security guards' cabin and generator outside the house. The CDA has declared an additional kitchen built inside the residence a violation of building regulations.

The notice directs that the encroachments be removed within 15 days, warning that the CDA will take action itself if the order is not followed. The CDA has issued the notice to Amanullah, son of Muhammad Younis, identifying him as the owner of the building.

The CDA had also ordered the removal of encroachments from Fazl's residence on March 18, 2019. It has also issued a notice to Madrassa Akhtarul Uloom in Bilal Town, near Korang Nullah in Khanna Dak, for carrying out construction without an approved building plan.

It has directed the seminary to submit its building plans within 15 days, failing which the authority may seal the building. The CDA has also identified Illegal construction at Idara Maarif-e-Islamia, Sharia Rabbaniyah and Tafseerul Quran, located at House No 3, Street No 6, Sector F-8/3.

According to the CDA, unauthorised structures have been built in the mandatory setbacks and on the rooftop of the seminary. The authority has also objected to the use of the building as a seminary instead of for residential purposes.

It has directed the seminary's administration to remove all violations within 15 days.

The CDA has warned that failure to comply may result in the building being sealed, fines being imposed and the allotment being cancelled. The CDA has launched action against seminaries and other buildings in Islamabad to enforce building control regulations.

Meanwhile, after the notice was issued, Maulana Asjad Mahmood, the son of the JUI-F chief, claimed it was retaliation for pointing out alleged encroachments by a senior military official.

In a statement, Mahmood said that instead of responding to the alleged encroachments, the authorities resorted to what he described as underhanded tactics.

He expressed concern over the "transformation of political differences into personal revenge". He said such actions were a matter of serious concern and urged the nation and JUI-F workers to remain informed and vigilant about the evolving situation.

The JUI-F chief had faced ministers wrath, who accused him of exploiting religion for political and financial gains after his criticism of the government in the National Assembly a day earlier.

Fazl had accused the government of misusing the Constitution and resorting to unconstitutional measures in imposing governor's rule and an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

Speaking on the floor of the National Assembly on Wednesday, Fazl noted the Centre's stance was that it took the measures according to the Constitution.

He alleged, "The government has misused the Constitution [ ] Here, just as the law is misused, the Constitution was misused."

headline: Costly winter ahead for electricity consumers
description: Costly winter ahead for electricity consumers
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
The Power Division on Friday warned that December, January and February were potentially the most difficult months for electricity consumers as higher fuel costs and seasonal constraints on power generation could bring an additional financial burden during the winter.

Fuel price adjustments (FPAs) could increase two to threefold between December and February as the rising international prices of liquefied natural gas (LNG), coal and other fuels push up the cost of electricity generation, Power Division sources said.

Consumers may consequently have to bear higher FPAs during the three-month period, while an increase in power load management is also expected.

The sources said global market prices of LNG and other fuels had climbed to high levels, adding to the cost of electricity production.

Hydropower generation is expected to decline during winter, potentially increasing the country's reliance on more expensive fuels to meet electricity demand. Limited availability of domestic gas is also likely to pose a major challenge in supplying gas to power plants, the sources added.

They warned that restricted domestic gas supplies during the winter could further affect electricity generation.

The Power Division has also indicated that power load management could increase from December to February.

Sources said two hours of load management had been carried out during previous months to keep the burden of higher electricity prices on consumers in check.

The country faces an energy crisis, aggravated since the start of a war between United States and Iran in February this year.

The conflict in the Persian Gulf has resulted in the closure of the Strait of Hormuz which is one of the major fuel supply route of the world. Pakistan generates hydro-electricity while it also relies on fuel-based energy solutions.

headline: Pakistan tops world in hepatitis C
description: Pakistan tops world in hepatitis C
author: Waqas Ahmed
article_text:
More than 45 million people in Pakistan are affected by mental health disorders, hepatitis B and C, and HIV, according to figures presented by the Ministry of National Health Services to the National Assembly.

The figures show that more than 32.4 million people suffer from mental health disorders, while 12.9 million are affected by hepatitis B or C.

The number of people living with HIV has also exceeded 417,000, while nearly 3,900 HIV-positive children were registered between January 2025 and June 2026, according to the ministry's data.

According to the report, the number of people suffering from mental health disorders increased from 30 million in 2019 to 32.4 million in 2023, marking a rise of 2.4 million during the period.

More than 300,000 people in the federal capital alone are affected by mental health disorders.

The report also highlighted a severe shortage of psychiatrists in the country, with only 1,050 specialists registered nationwide. This translates into just one psychiatrist for every 245,000 people.

Provincial figures show that Punjab has 406 registered psychiatrists, followed by Sindh with 228, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa with 122 and Balochistan with 44, according to the document.

Pakistan also ranks first globally in the number of hepatitis C patients and is among the 10 countries with the highest number of deaths from the disease, the report said.

Citing World Health Organisation (WHO) figures, the Ministry of National Health Services informed the house that the number of hepatitis C patients in Pakistan had reached nine million, while more than 3.86 million people were suffering from hepatitis B.

The combined number of people affected by hepatitis B and C stands at 12.9 million.

The country records around 48,000 deaths annually due to hepatitis, while more than 88,000 new hepatitis C infections were reported in 2024, according to the report.

The ministry also presented details of people affected by HIV/AIDS, stating that, according to the WHO, more than 417,000 people in Pakistan were living with HIV.

Of these, 92,148 were registered with the relevant authorities, while 67,878 people were receiving antiretroviral therapy (ART).

The report further revealed that the annual number of HIV cases had increased from 16,000 in 2010 to 48,000 in 2024.

It also recorded a significant increase in HIV screening, which rose from 37,944 tests in 2020 to 374,000 in 2025.

ISLAMABAD:

More than 45 million people in Pakistan are affected by mental health disorders, hepatitis B and C, and HIV, according to figures presented by the Ministry of National Health Services to the National Assembly.

The figures show that more than 32.4 million people suffer from mental health disorders, while 12.9 million are affected by hepatitis B or C.

The number of people living with HIV has also exceeded 417,000, while nearly 3,900 HIV-positive children were registered between January 2025 and June 2026, according to the ministry's data.

According to the report, the number of people suffering from mental health disorders increased from 30 million in 2019 to 32.4 million in 2023, marking a rise of 2.4 million during the period.

More than 300,000 people in the federal capital alone are affected by mental health disorders.

The report also highlighted a severe shortage of psychiatrists in the country, with only 1,050 specialists registered nationwide. This translates into just one psychiatrist for every 245,000 people.

Provincial figures show that Punjab has 406 registered psychiatrists, followed by Sindh with 228, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa with 122 and Balochistan with 44, according to the document.

Pakistan also ranks first globally in the number of hepatitis C patients and is among the 10 countries with the highest number of deaths from the disease, the report said.

Citing World Health Organisation (WHO) figures, the Ministry of National Health Services informed the house that the number of hepatitis C patients in Pakistan had reached nine million, while more than 3.86 million people were suffering from hepatitis B.

The combined number of people affected by hepatitis B and C stands at 12.9 million.

The country records around 48,000 deaths annually due to hepatitis, while more than 88,000 new hepatitis C infections were reported in 2024, according to the report.

The ministry also presented details of people affected by HIV/AIDS, stating that, according to the WHO, more than 417,000 people in Pakistan were living with HIV.

Of these, 92,148 were registered with the relevant authorities, while 67,878 people were receiving antiretroviral therapy (ART).

The report further revealed that the annual number of HIV cases had increased from 16,000 in 2010 to 48,000 in 2024.

It also recorded a significant increase in HIV screening, which rose from 37,944 tests in 2020 to 374,000 in 2025.

headline: CJ recuses himself from IHC judges transfer case
description: CJ recuses himself from IHC judges transfer case
author: Fiaz Mahmood
article_text:
An Islamabad High Court (IHC) bench hearing a plea against a Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) order regarding filling vacant IHC seats by transfer of judges from other high courts dissolved after a bench member recused himself.

IHC Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar on Friday took up a petition filed by Islamabad High Court Bar Association (IHCBA) former president Syed Nayab Hassan Gardezi, challenging the JCP's April order along with the IHC registrar's objections to the plea.

In its April 28 meeting, the JCP decided to fill the seatsvacated by transfer of some IHC judges to other high courtsby bringing in judges from other high courts. Gardezi challenged the decision in the IHC, whose registrar raised objections to his plea.

During the hearing, CJ Dogar observed that he was part of the JCP and it was unsuitable for him to hear a case challenging its decision. "I am recusing myself from hearing this plea. Your petition will be listed for hearing before some other bench in a few days," Justice Dogar told the petitioner.

When Gardezi urged him to remove the registrar's objections, the CJ observed that this matter would also be addressed by the new bench. Justice Dogar is also one of the three judges who were transferred to the IHC in February last year from provincial high courts.

headline: Iran-Iraq land border closed for pilgrims
description: Iran-Iraq land border closed for pilgrims
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Ministry advises zaireen to take direct flights

The Ministry of Religious Affairs has issued an alert for pilgrims intending to enter Iraq via a land route to visit religious sites, informing them that the border crossing between Iran and Iraq has been closed for over a week.

According to a ministry spokesperson, the only land route through which pilgrims enter Iraq from IranAl-Sheeb Borderis closed since October 21 for all vehicles.

The spokesperson said Pakistani pilgrims in Iran can only go to Iraq via flights to Najaf and Baghdad airports. He advised pilgrims to read the latest travel advisory before embarking on a journey from Iran to Iraq.

The ministry spokesperson also advised Ziyarrah Group Organisers (ZGOs) to inform pilgrims about the land route closure and not to use it to reach Iraq.

Pilgrims from all over the world visit holy sites in Iraq and Iran including the Shrine of Imam Hussain (AS) in Karbala and the Shrine of Imam Reza (AS) in Mashhad.

headline: PPP courts opposition for electoral reforms
description: PPP courts opposition for electoral reforms
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
The Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) on Friday intensified its efforts to secure opposition participation in the proposed parliamentary committee on electoral reforms as a party delegation met Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas to urge him to join the initiative.

The outreach came as the National Assembly approved the formation of a 30-member parliamentary committee to oversee electoral reforms.

Senator Sherry Rehman said Abbas had sought time to consult before conveying his response, adding that the party was hopeful of a positive outcome.

The delegation comprised PPP Secretary General Nayyar Bokhari, Senator Waqar Mehdi, Nadeem Afzal Chan and Rehman.

"Every political party should ensure its participation in the committee. We all know that the PTI has boycotted parliamentary committees. So we asked them to join this committee, play an active role in it, express their reservations and suggest reforms," Rehman said in a video statement.

She said parliamentary committees were the "heart of parliamentary work", adding that the PTI should also participate in other parliamentary committees to "strengthen Parliament's role".

Rehman added that Abbas had warmly received the PPP delegation, thanked party Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari for the initiative and said he would respond after consultation.

"He told us that he will respond [to the proposal] after consultation. We are hopeful that their response will be positive," Rehman said.

30-member parliamentary panel approved

Meanwhile, the National Assembly approved the formation of a 30-member parliamentary committee to oversee electoral reforms. The proposed body will comprise 20 members from the lower house and 10 from the Senate.

Speaking to the media, Federal Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said the NA speaker would soon issue a formal notification constituting the committee, while the process of finalising the names of its members was still under way.

He added that the PTI had not opposed the motion when it was presented in the National Assembly.

Seats on the proposed committee will be allocated to parliamentary parties in proportion to their numerical strength in the respective houses, he said.

Chaudhry said the committee was being formed to promote parliamentary consultation and consensus on improving the electoral system, ensuring transparency and introducing reforms.

He said the government would seek to give due consideration to constructive, positive and practical proposals from all parliamentary parties, including those in the opposition, as part of the electoral reform process.

He said the objective was to develop an electoral system that further strengthened transparency, public confidence and democratic values.

The minister stressed that electoral reforms were not the concern of any single political party but a shared national responsibility aimed at strengthening the democratic system.

He said all political parties should play an effective role in the process through mutual consultation, keeping the national interest in mind.

The delegation comprised PPP Secretary General Nayyar Bokhari, Senator Waqar Mehdi, Nadeem Afzal Chan and Rehman.

"Every political party should ensure its participation in the committee. We all know that the PTI has boycotted parliamentary committees. So we asked them to join this committee, play an active role in it, express their reservations and suggest reforms," Rehman said in a video statement.

She said parliamentary committees were the "heart of parliamentary work", adding that the PTI should also participate in other parliamentary committees to "strengthen Parliament's role".

Rehman added that Abbas had warmly received the PPP delegation, thanked party Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari for the initiative and said he would respond after consultation.

"He told us that he will respond [to the proposal] after consultation. We are hopeful that their response will be positive," Rehman said.

He added that the PTI had not opposed the motion when it was presented in the National Assembly.

Seats on the proposed committee will be allocated to parliamentary parties in proportion to their numerical strength in the respective houses, he said.

Chaudhry said the committee was being formed to promote parliamentary consultation and consensus on improving the electoral system, ensuring transparency and introducing reforms.

He said the government would seek to give due consideration to constructive, positive and practical proposals from all parliamentary parties, including those in the opposition, as part of the electoral reform process.

He said the objective was to develop an electoral system that further strengthened transparency, public confidence and democratic values.

The minister stressed that electoral reforms were not the concern of any single political party but a shared national responsibility aimed at strengthening the democratic system.

He said all political parties should play an effective role in the process through mutual consultation, keeping the national interest in mind.

headline: Pakistan seeks Saudi energy crisis support
description: Pakistan seeks Saudi energy crisis support
author: ZAFAR BHUTTA
article_text:
Pakistan has sought Saudi Arabia's support for liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) supplies and invited investment in oil storage facilities and refinery upgrades as it grapples with supply disruptions linked to the Iran-US conflict and instability along key regional shipping routes.

Pakistan has relied heavily on LPG imports from Iran through the land border, and the closure of the crossing has raised concerns about supplies ahead of the winter season, when domestic gas demand typically increases.

Islamabad has approached Riyadh for dedicated LPG shipments to help meet the anticipated rise in demand, as disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz and security risks in the Red Sea have added to concerns over regional energy supplies.

The crisis has also highlighted Pakistan's limited strategic petroleum storage capacity. The government is now seeking investment from Middle Eastern countries, including Saudi Arabia and Kuwait, to develop oil storage infrastructure.

The proposals were discussed at a meeting between Federal Minister for Petroleum Ali Pervez Malik and Saudi Arabia's Ambassador to Pakistan Dr Rajeh Tami Albugamy, according to a statement issued by the ministry.

The discussions covered strategic oil storage, refinery upgrades, LPG supplies and commercial cooperation in the mining, petroleum and energy sectors.

Malik told the ambassador that Pakistan had approved a tax-neutral bonded policy modelled on international energy hubs such as Fujairah and Singapore. Under the framework, Saudi companies could establish commercial oil reserves in Pakistan without incurring local tax liabilities.

The minister said the arrangement could help diversify maritime transit risks associated with the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait while providing access to Asian markets.

He said strategic oil storage facilities in Pakistan would give Saudi Arabia greater flexibility in managing supply routes and reaching regional markets.

Malik also outlined plans to develop a large petroleum storage and refining complex at Hub in Balochistan, with guidance from Technip Energies UK. The proposed facility would be capable of accommodating very large crude carriers (VLCCs) and could strengthen Pakistan's role as a regional energy corridor serving Central Asian and Chinese markets, the statement said.

The minister also highlighted investment opportunities under Pakistan's refinery upgrade programme, which aims to modernise domestic refining infrastructure, improve efficiency and transition to Euro 5 fuel standards.

He thanked Saudi authorities at Yanbu port for prioritising crude oil shipments to Pakistan during recent disruptions in global energy markets. He also discussed with the ambassador coordination with Saudi Aramco to increase crude oil procurement and arrange dedicated LPG shipments.

Pakistan is also seeking Saudi investment in the multibillion-dollar Reko Diq copper and gold mining project in Balochistan. Saudi Arabia has previously expressed interest in acquiring a 15% stake in the project.

Malik said Pakistan valued its longstanding strategic relationship with Saudi Arabia and had conveyed its solidarity with the Saudi leadership and people during a recent visit to Riyadh.

Both sides said their defence and strategic partnership provided a foundation for broader economic cooperation and regional stability.

The Saudi ambassador reiterated Riyadh's commitment to its relationship with Islamabad and said the two countries stood together in all circumstances, according to the statement.

He also announced that the Saudi embassy in Islamabad had introduced same-day processing of visa applications for Pakistani citizens to facilitate travel and promote business, cultural and people-to-people exchanges.

Malik invited Saudi Vice Minister of Mining Khalid Al-Mudaifer to attend the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum, scheduled to take place in Islamabad on November 12-13.

headline: OGRA raises Oct RLNG prices by up to 15.27%
description: OGRA raises Oct RLNG prices by up to 15.27%
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
OGRA on Friday notified the increase in RLNG rates across the transmission and distribution networks of the two Sui gas companies, reversing a 20% reduction granted for September.

OGRA notified an increase of 13.89% to 15.27% in RLNG prices for October 2026 for sales by Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited (SNGPL) and Sui Southern Gas Company Limited (SSGCL).

The increase follows a 20% reduction in RLNG prices for September and has been attributed mainly to higher crude oil prices. The revised rates took effect from October 1 under the federal government's policy guidelines and were determined on the basis of two LNG cargoes imported by Pakistan State Oil (PSO).

The average delivered ex-ship price of LNG for the two cargoes in October stood at $10.75 per million British thermal units (MMBtu), compared with $10.06 per MMBtu in September, $12.12 per MMBtu in August and $18.96 per MMBtu in July.

The increase is expected to have a significant impact on fuel costs for power generation in December. RLNG-based power generation cost Rs40 per unit in September, when the average RLNG import price stood at $10.06 per MMBtu, compared with $10.75 per MMBtu in October.

According to OGRA's notification, the RLNG sale price for SNGPL's transmission network increased by 13.89% to $15.9357 per MMBtu in October, from $13.99 per MMBtu in September.

For the company's distribution network, the price rose by 14.01% to $17.3259 per MMBtu, compared with $15.196 per MMBtu in the preceding month.

For SSGCL, the RLNG sale price at the transmission stage increased by 15.25% to $14.5339 per MMBtu, against $12.611 per MMBtu in September. Its distribution-stage price rose by 15.27% to $16.3959 per MMBtu, from $14.22 per MMBtu.

SSGCL, based in Karachi, supplies gas to consumers in Sindh and Balochistan. Its distribution-stage system losses stand at 12.55%, compared with around 10.6% last year.

Meanwhile, Lahore-based SNGPL supplies gas to consumers in Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Its distribution-stage system losses have also reached nearly 9%, compared with 7.47% in October last year.

The revised RLNG prices will remain applicable from October 1, 2026, according to OGRA.

ISLAMABAD:

OGRA on Friday notified the increase in RLNG rates across the transmission and distribution networks of the two Sui gas companies, reversing a 20% reduction granted for September.

OGRA notified an increase of 13.89% to 15.27% in RLNG prices for October 2026 for sales by Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited (SNGPL) and Sui Southern Gas Company Limited (SSGCL).

The increase follows a 20% reduction in RLNG prices for September and has been attributed mainly to higher crude oil prices. The revised rates took effect from October 1 under the federal government's policy guidelines and were determined on the basis of two LNG cargoes imported by Pakistan State Oil (PSO).

The average delivered ex-ship price of LNG for the two cargoes in October stood at $10.75 per million British thermal units (MMBtu), compared with $10.06 per MMBtu in September, $12.12 per MMBtu in August and $18.96 per MMBtu in July.

The increase is expected to have a significant impact on fuel costs for power generation in December. RLNG-based power generation cost Rs40 per unit in September, when the average RLNG import price stood at $10.06 per MMBtu, compared with $10.75 per MMBtu in October.

According to OGRA's notification, the RLNG sale price for SNGPL's transmission network increased by 13.89% to $15.9357 per MMBtu in October, from $13.99 per MMBtu in September.

For the company's distribution network, the price rose by 14.01% to $17.3259 per MMBtu, compared with $15.196 per MMBtu in the preceding month.

For SSGCL, the RLNG sale price at the transmission stage increased by 15.25% to $14.5339 per MMBtu, against $12.611 per MMBtu in September. Its distribution-stage price rose by 15.27% to $16.3959 per MMBtu, from $14.22 per MMBtu.

SSGCL, based in Karachi, supplies gas to consumers in Sindh and Balochistan. Its distribution-stage system losses stand at 12.55%, compared with around 10.6% last year.

Meanwhile, Lahore-based SNGPL supplies gas to consumers in Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Its distribution-stage system losses have also reached nearly 9%, compared with 7.47% in October last year.

The revised RLNG prices will remain applicable from October 1, 2026, according to OGRA.

headline: Army destroys Afghan Taliban posts
description: Army destroys Afghan Taliban posts
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Army destroys Afghan Taliban posts

Pakistan Army successfully targeted and destroyed several posts and military positions of the Afghan Taliban in the areas adjacent to South Waziristan and Parachinar, state-run Radio Pakistan said on Friday, citing security sources.

It added that the army gave a befitting reply to unprovoked firing by the Afghan Taliban along the Pak-Afghan border in the Angoor Adda area on Thursday using heavy weaponry and forcing the Taliban personnel to abandon their posts and flee.

The report indicated that several personnel of the Afghan Taliban regime were killed during the operation. It added that security forces remain committed to the defence of the country and the protection of its people, and there will be no compromise on national security.

The latest escalation followed an incident on October 27 when Afghan Taliban forces opened fire on Pakistani border posts and civilian areas in Angoor Adda, Lower South Waziristan.

headline: Singapore pushes deeper Pak trade ties
description: Singapore pushes deeper Pak trade ties
author: Kamran Yousaf
article_text:
Singapore's Foreign Minister Dr Vivian Balakrishnan on Friday called for translating its strong political relationship with Pakistan into a much broader economic partnership, acknowledging that trade and investment between the two countries remained well below their potential despite six decades of diplomatic ties.

Balakrishnan pushed for greater economic ties during his visit to Islamabad where he held talks with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, called on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and later met Chief of Defence Forces and Army Chief Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir.

The visit, the first by a Singaporean foreign minister since 2005, coincided with the 60th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries and came months before Singapore assumes the chairmanship of ASEAN in 2027.

Speaking at a joint news conference with Dar after their talks, Balakrishnan was candid about the gap between the two countries' close diplomatic relationship and their limited economic engagement.

"To be very candid, at a diplomatic level, we've got excellent ties," the Singaporean foreign minister said. "In fact, they are so good that it makes it even more obvious that our trade relations - looking at the numbers and the data - ought to be much higher."

He described greater trade and investment flows as the "first order of business", calling for stronger links between businesses, particularly small and medium enterprises, in the two countries.

Dar said the two sides had agreed to encourage business delegations and closer interaction between their chambers of commerce. Pakistan has also reopened its Trade and Investment Office at its High Commission in Singapore to facilitate greater business-to-business engagement.

The two foreign ministers also discussed the possible resumption of direct air links between Pakistan and Singapore to facilitate business travel and people-to-people contacts.

Prime Minister Shehbaz, meanwhile, accepted in principle an invitation from Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong to visit Singapore, providing another potential opening for high-level engagement between the two countries.

During his meeting with Balakrishnan, the prime minister identified the digital economy, fintech, infrastructure development, logistics, SMEs and the services sector among areas where the two countries could expand cooperation.

Balakrishnan said Shehbaz's acceptance of the invitation had injected "an additional sense of urgency" into efforts to identify practical areas of cooperation.

One such area is the carbon market, which the Singaporean minister said could provide a new avenue for attracting investment into Pakistani projects aimed at reducing emissions while supporting sustainable development.

The two countries also exchanged a memorandum of understanding between Pakistan's National Disaster Management Authority and the Singapore Civil Defence Force.

The agreement envisages cooperation in disaster preparedness and response, including early-warning systems, search and rescue capabilities, sharing of best practices and possible joint training and exercises.

Balakrishnan said Singapore could learn from Pakistan's experience in dealing with large-scale natural disasters, particularly floods and extreme weather events.

Education, artificial intelligence and skills development also featured prominently in the discussions. The two sides are exploring stronger links between Nanyang Technological University and the National University of Singapore and Pakistan's National University of Sciences and Technology.

The Singaporean foreign minister also visited the National Center of Artificial Intelligence at NUST during his one-day visit.

Beyond bilateral relations, the two sides discussed the rapidly changing regional security environment, including the crisis in the Gulf and its implications for maritime trade and energy supplies.

In a significant endorsement of Islamabad's recent diplomatic efforts, Balakrishnan praised what he described as Pakistan's "unique, but very constructive and valuable role" in dealing with the Gulf crisis.

He noted that much of the energy passing through the Gulf was destined for South Asia, Southeast Asia and Northeast Asia, making stability in the region important well beyond the Middle East.

"We commend you for, and we wish you every success because if you succeed, it's good for all of us," he told Dar.

Dar said Pakistan remained engaged with key regional and international partners and believed dialogue and diplomacy were the only viable means of addressing outstanding disputes.

He also raised the situations in Palestine and Kashmir, reiterating Pakistan's support for an independent Palestinian state based on the pre-1967 borders with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital and calling for a settlement of the Jammu and Kashmir dispute in accordance with UN Security Council resolutions.

Maritime security was another area where Islamabad and Singapore appeared to find common ground. Balakrishnan stressed the importance of international law and the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea, given Singapore's dependence on maritime trade.

The two ministers also discussed closer engagement between Pakistan and ASEAN. Pakistan is one of ASEAN's earliest sectoral dialogue partners, while Singapore is due to take over the grouping's chairmanship next year.

Later, Balakrishnan met Field Marshal Asim Munir at the General Headquarters in Rawalpindi, where discussions focused on evolving regional and global security dynamics, regional peace and stability and avenues for strengthening bilateral cooperation.

According to an official statement, Field Marshal Munir reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to stronger ties with Singapore and stressed greater institutional linkages and constructive engagement.

The Singaporean foreign minister appreciated the professionalism of Pakistan's armed forces and acknowledged Pakistan's contribution to regional peace and stability.

Balakrishnan's visit marked an effort by both sides to give fresh momentum to a relationship that has remained politically cordial but economically modest despite six decades of diplomatic ties.

As the Singaporean foreign minister put it at the end of his visit, "60 years is an important milestone, but what matters more is what we do in the next 60 years."

The Singaporean foreign minister also visited the National Center of Artificial Intelligence at NUST during his one-day visit.
