headline: Pak Army 'cautiously optimistic' on Iran-US mediation
description: Pak Army 'cautiously optimistic' on Iran-US mediation
author: Reuters
article_text:
Pakistan Army is "cautiously optimistic" about its mediation between Iran and the United States, its spokesman said on Friday in his first interview since a high-level delegation visited Tehran this week.

Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir has been to Tehran twice this month, most recently on Monday alongside Saudi and Turkish officials.

"Why would the Field Marshal be going twice if it is not for some positivity? So yes, of course," spokesman Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said when asked whether the trips were a positive sign.

"The word that we would use is always cautiously optimistic," added Chaudhry, director general of Inter-Services Public Relations.

There were still "powerful spoilers and detractors," who believed conflict serves them, he added without naming them.

Speaking in Rawalpindi, Chaudhry declined to say what was discussed or whether the US had backed the trip.

"Anyone who has a shared vision of collective deterrence and regional peace, why not? Everyone is most welcome," he said, adding that it was for the political leadership of the three principal parties to decide.

Asked whether more Pakistani troops were being sent to Saudi Arabia under the agreement, Chaudhry said that would depend on the situation and the decision of both countries' political leadership.

He said Pakistan was committed to defending Saudi Arabia and the holy sites of Mecca and Medina. "We are not part of the Yemeni conflict, which is an intra-Yemen conflict," he added.

"Our counter-terrorism operations are based on what we call IBOs, intelligence-based operations... The tempo of the freedom of action of (those) IBOs will further increase," he said.

headline: Three tankers catch fire in Hormuz
description: Three tankers catch fire in Hormuz
author: Reuters
article_text:
Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said on Friday that three oil tankers had caught fire and exploded in the Strait of Hormuz, while attempting to use what it described as unauthorised routes, Iranian state media reported.

An IRGC Navy statement said one of the tankers, which was carrying 2 million barrels of crude oil, had hit a mine.

Reuters was unable to immediately verify the statement.

Separately, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency said it had received a report that a vessel was hit by an unknown projectile on its port side about 40 nautical miles (74 km) south of Iran's Lavan Island, causing a fire onboard. The crew were reported safe and there was no reported environmental impact, it said.

Lavan Island lies in the Gulf, off Iran's southern coast. It was not immediately clear whether the vessel cited by the agency was one of the three tankers referred to by the IRGC Navy.

Tensions have persisted in the Strait of Hormuz, a strategic waterway through which around one-fifth of global oil supplies pass, since the US-Israeli strikes on Iran at the end of February.

State media said Iranian forces also downed and captured an MQM-170 US drone over Iran's Qeshm island near the Strait of Hormuz. There was no immediate reaction from the US military and Reuters could not independently verify the report.

Iran also said it had destroyed an unmanned US vessel in the eastern Strait of Hormuz.

But the US military's Central Command denied this and said in a statement on X: "All US military unmanned surface vessels in the Middle East are accounted for, including a squadron of advanced sea drones on patrol in the Strait of Hormuz."

headline: FCC warns executive over ignored orders
description: FCC warns executive over ignored orders
author: Hasnaat Malik
article_text:
Amid an ongoing challenge regarding the non-implementation of superior courts' orders, the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) has reminded the executive that compliance with a judicial decision is a constitutional requirement, not a matter of courtesy.

"To disregard or to delay in implementation of [a court] verdict amounts to challenging the very framework of the legal system," said 10-page judgement authored by Justice Ali Baqar Najafi.

Justice Najafi was part of a three-member bench led by Chief Justice Amin-Ud-Din Khan which heard a case regarding the implementation of a Supreme Court judgement in a sacked employees' case.

The order stated that non-compliance not only disturbs the delicate equilibrium between the court's prestige and the enforcement of the rights but also sets a dangerous precedent that could lead to an executive overreach.

The court said implementing judicial orders is crucial for maintaining public confidence in the judicial system. If their decisions can be easily ignored or set aside by the individuals or entities, public trust in the efficacy of the judiciary and the entire government is seriously undermined.

"Consequently, the erosion of trust in the judicial system may undermine the democratic system," the order added.

The FCC noted that in a constitutional democracy, the rule of law is not just a principle but the foundation upon which the legitimacy and good governance of any system of government rests.

"The Supreme Court of Pakistan and, after the 27th amendment, this [FCC] being the apex court of the country is entrusted with performing the responsibility of interpreting the law, ensuring justice and upholding the Constitution of Islamic Republic of Pakistan."

It said the orders of the Supreme Court, as the then apex court, are not merely recommendations or advisories but a legal mandate that must be followed. Such decisions are the culmination of vigorous legal scrutiny and deliberation intended to reflect the values and laws of the land.

In December 2021, the Supreme Court while exercising suo motu jurisdiction restored thousands of government workers, sacked through its earlier August 17 judgement, which struck down the Sacked Employees (Reinstatement) Ordinance Act 2010.

The FCC asked whether the December 17, 2021 order was implemented in letter and spirit. It also questioned whether the non-implementation of the order amounted to the contempt of court.

The court disposing of the listed cases directed the government authorities to comply with the detailed judgement in the sacked employees' case in letter and spirit and consider the petitioners as unconditionally and regularly appointed beneficiary employees.

The court held that the conditions so imposed by the SC on the beneficiary employees were waived/diluted by the respondent-department due to the passage of time and their lethargy, not due to any fault of the petitioner employees.

"Such conduct cannot be awarded with any sentence of appreciation by this court. In this context the inaction on the pact of the employers is marked with caution, persuading us to show our concern to a sorry state of affair.

"However, at this stage we would exercise a restraint rather than acting pro-actively keeping in view the overall circumstances," stated the order.

Some legal experts believe that after 27th Constitutional Amendment, the biggest challenge for the superior courts is to establish their judicial authority. It is an open secret that the executive has a dominant role now in the appointment of judges.

In May last year, the SC ordered the federal government to carry out legislation for giving right of appeal to the civilians who convicted by the military courts in May 9, 2023 cases. However, the order is yet to implement so far.

Interestingly, both the SC and the FCC are silent on the non-implementation of the judicial order in the military courts case. On the other hand, dozens of PTI activists, convicted by military courts are behind the bar and waiting for a legislation so they can appeal against their convictions.

headline: Araghchi calls US bid to open dialogue a ‘positive step’
description: Qatari mediators hold 12-hour talks in Tehran to revive US-Iran negotiations as Washington weighs military options
author: Reuters
article_text:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Saturday described Washington’s attempt to open dialogue with Tehran as a “positive step”, saying an Iranian delegation is in Qatar to continue consultations with mediators amid renewed concerns over the possibility of another conflict.

In an interview with Al Jazeera, Araghchi said Tehran had studied a letter sent by US Vice President JD Vance last week, while declining to rule out the possibility of another military confrontation.

“We do not rule out any possibility regarding the outbreak of war, and we are prepared for all scenarios,” he said, adding that Iran had upgraded its weaponry, addressed vulnerabilities and tested new arms.

“Our forces are at the highest level of readiness,” he said.

Araghchi acknowledged the impact of US-imposed economic pressure on Iran but insisted that Tehran would not surrender.

“We will continue to stand firm and resist and we will overcome this difficult phase through our own capabilities,” he said.

The foreign minister also confirmed that an Iranian delegation had travelled to Qatar to continue consultations with mediators, including Qatar and Pakistan, over Tehran’s conditions.

“My aide is currently in Qatar to continue consultations. Qatari and Pakistani mediators are continuing consultations regarding our conditions,” he said.

However, Araghchi ruled out any immediate meeting with US officials, describing reports suggesting otherwise as media speculation.

“We see no need to meet with the Americans at present. Our conditions are clear, and mediators are continuing their consultations regarding them,” he said.

Khamenei orders unrestricted military response

Earlier, Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has ordered the armed forces to respond immediately and without "geographic limits to any enemy threat", according to a statement published on his official Telegram account on Saturday.

Khamenei said Iran would determine the timing and conditions for ending any renewed military or "terrorist attacks by its enemies," and ordered an update of the military target list to bring US and Israeli "physical and non-physical" assets within the reach of Iranian forces.

Iran provincial official says US attacked fishing boats off Qeshm Island, state media

Iranian state broadcaster IRIB, citing a Hormozgan province official, said on Saturday that the US attacked two fishing boats near Qeshm Island, leaving two fishermen missing and one wounded.

There was no immediate US confirmation of the attack.

The attack comes as spokesperson for the Iranian army Brigadier General Mohammad Akraminia said on Saturday that renewed war would “engulf a much wider area” if US President Donald Trump “resorts to another adventure in the region” alongside Israel.

“If the US president once again embarks on another military adventure in the region under pressure from and inducement by the Zionists, the flames of war will undoubtedly engulf a much wider geographical area,” Akraminia wrote on US social media company X.

“And the end of the conflict will not be in his (Trump’s) hands,” he warned.

Citing “the US President’s track record of betraying diplomacy,” Akraminia said the Iranian army is “continuously” enhancing its combat readiness and “closely monitoring” US movements in the region.

Iranian delegation arrives in Qatar for talks: report

An Iranian delegation, including a deputy to Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, is in Qatar for talks following a reported breakthrough in indirect negotiations between Tehran and Washington, a Qatari newspaper reported Saturday.

Citing an Iranian source, Al-Araby Al-Jadeed said the delegation was in the Qatari capital, Doha, "to facilitate engagement with the Qatari mediator."

The visit followed "intensive discussions held by a Qatari negotiating delegation in Tehran, which resulted in a breakthrough in indirect negotiations between Tehran and Washington," the newspaper reported, citing the source.

The discussions also paved the way for the Iranian negotiating team to accompany the Qatari delegation on its return trip to Doha, according to the report.

"Negotiations with the US side are taking place indirectly through the mediator, not directly," the Iranian source told the newspaper.

Sources close to Qatar- and Pakistan-led mediation efforts also told Al-Araby Al-Jadeed that an American delegation was expected to join the diplomatic process in Doha.

The sources said the US delegation could hold direct talks with Iranian negotiators in the Qatari capital.

Trump may order major Iran strike if Republicans suffer losses in midterm election: Axios

US President Donald Trump may be more inclined to approve a large-scale military operation against Iran if Republicans fare badly in the midterm elections next week, according to a report on Friday.

"If he feels embarrassed or disenfranchised, he will do something bold," a US official told Axios, adding that it is the message being passed to Iranian officials, who are being told their best chance for a deal is now.

A White House official rejected the idea, telling the outlet that election results will not factor into Trump's decisions on Iran.

The report said Qatari mediators spent more than 12 hours on Friday in Tehran, staying in regular contact with the White House, to restart direct talks between Washington and Tehran. A diplomatic source described "positive progress," and discussions are due to continue on Saturday in Doha.

Talks have stalled over competing demands, according to one US official. Washington wants nuclear concessions as part of any return to negotiations, while Tehran insists the US first lift its naval blockade, release frozen funds and allow oil sales.

The report said Doha is urging Iran to allow UN inspectors into its bombed nuclear sites in exchange for limited sanctions relief.

Pointing to divisions within Trump's circle, the report said Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio are sceptical of any deal and favour further weakening of Iran’s leadership. Vice President JD Vance and envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner back resuming talks.

The report comes amid heightened tensions between Iran and the US over the Strait of Hormuz, a strategic waterway for global energy shipments.

'Red lines are a thing of the past', says Iranian FM

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in a response to German Chancellor Friedrich Merz that "Red lines" were "a thing of the past" , and the 100 billion euro cost of the Iran war for Europe was "nothing compared to the Earth-shattering blow Iran's Powerful Armed Forces will deal against those who dare harm our people."

According to Clash Report, Merz said that this cost increase over the last eight months came "solely because of the increase in energy prices caused by this conflict."

Merz is reported as saying that they "have an economic interest in bringing this conflict to an end as quickly as possible."

Araghchi said Merz had hailed the US-Israel bombings of Iran since they began last year, saying that they were "Doing Europe's dirty work."

Tanker struck by unidentified projectile in Strait of Hormuz: UK maritime agency

A crude oil tanker was struck by an unidentified projectile while completing an outbound transit through the Strait of Hormuz, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO).

The agency said it had received information about the incident from a verified source.

The report did not disclose the vessel's name, the location of the strike, or the condition of the crew.

Authorities are investigating, while the agency advised vessels transiting the area to exercise caution and report any suspicious activity to the UKMTO.

Iran says 4th oil tanker hit mine, caught fire in Strait of Hormuz

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy said Friday that a fourth oil tanker had struck a mine and caught fire while attempting to pass through an unauthorised route in the Strait of Hormuz.

The navy’s public relations office said the supertanker, carrying more than 2 million barrels of crude oil, ignored repeated radio warnings against using the southern passage through the strategic waterway.

The vessel was struck by a mine, triggering a powerful explosion and leaving it burning, according to the statement.

The IRGC said the tanker was attempting to exit the strait through what it described as an unauthorised southern route.

It claimed the incident marked the fourth time a tanker had caught fire in the strait since early Friday.

Oman evacuates injured crew from Indian boat targeted in Strait of Hormuz

Oman announced on Friday that it had medically evacuated an injured crew member from an Indian boat targeted in the Strait of Hormuz.

The military’s Directorate of Moral Guidance said the Royal Air Force of Oman, in coordination with relevant authorities, carried out the evacuation from an Indian boat that had come under attack in the strategic waterway.

The injured crew member was airlifted from Khasab Hospital in the northern governorate of Musandam to Khawla Hospital in the capital, Muscat, for specialized medical treatment, it said in a statement on X.

The Royal Navy of Oman announced earlier that it had evacuated 25 crew members from a commercial vessel that caught fire after coming under attack 1.6 nautical miles off the coast of Musandam.

article_html:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Saturday described Washington’s attempt to open dialogue with Tehran as a “positive step”, saying an Iranian delegation is in Qatar to continue consultations with mediators amid renewed concerns over the possibility of another conflict.

In an interview with Al Jazeera, Araghchi said Tehran had studied a letter sent by US Vice President JD Vance last week, while declining to rule out the possibility of another military confrontation.

“We do not rule out any possibility regarding the outbreak of war, and we are prepared for all scenarios,” he said, adding that Iran had upgraded its weaponry, addressed vulnerabilities and tested new arms.

“Our forces are at the highest level of readiness,” he said.

Araghchi acknowledged the impact of US-imposed economic pressure on Iran but insisted that Tehran would not surrender.

“We will continue to stand firm and resist and we will overcome this difficult phase through our own capabilities,” he said.

The foreign minister also confirmed that an Iranian delegation had travelled to Qatar to continue consultations with mediators, including Qatar and Pakistan, over Tehran’s conditions.

“My aide is currently in Qatar to continue consultations. Qatari and Pakistani mediators are continuing consultations regarding our conditions,” he said.

However, Araghchi ruled out any immediate meeting with US officials, describing reports suggesting otherwise as media speculation.

“We see no need to meet with the Americans at present. Our conditions are clear, and mediators are continuing their consultations regarding them,” he said.

Khamenei orders unrestricted military response

Earlier, Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has ordered the armed forces to respond immediately and without "geographic limits to any enemy threat", according to a statement published on his official Telegram account on Saturday.

Khamenei said Iran would determine the timing and conditions for ending any renewed military or "terrorist attacks by its enemies," and ordered an update of the military target list to bring US and Israeli "physical and non-physical" assets within the reach of Iranian forces.

Iran provincial official says US attacked fishing boats off Qeshm Island, state media

Iranian state broadcaster IRIB, citing a Hormozgan province official, said on Saturday that the US attacked two fishing boats near Qeshm Island, leaving two fishermen missing and one wounded.

There was no immediate US confirmation of the attack.

The attack comes as spokesperson for the Iranian army Brigadier General Mohammad Akraminia said on Saturday that renewed war would “engulf a much wider area” if US President Donald Trump “resorts to another adventure in the region” alongside Israel.

“If the US president once again embarks on another military adventure in the region under pressure from and inducement by the Zionists, the flames of war will undoubtedly engulf a much wider geographical area,” Akraminia wrote on US social media company X.

“And the end of the conflict will not be in his (Trump’s) hands,” he warned.

Citing “the US President’s track record of betraying diplomacy,” Akraminia said the Iranian army is “continuously” enhancing its combat readiness and “closely monitoring” US movements in the region.

Iranian delegation arrives in Qatar for talks: report

An Iranian delegation, including a deputy to Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, is in Qatar for talks following a reported breakthrough in indirect negotiations between Tehran and Washington, a Qatari newspaper reported Saturday.

Citing an Iranian source, Al-Araby Al-Jadeed said the delegation was in the Qatari capital, Doha, "to facilitate engagement with the Qatari mediator."

The visit followed "intensive discussions held by a Qatari negotiating delegation in Tehran, which resulted in a breakthrough in indirect negotiations between Tehran and Washington," the newspaper reported, citing the source.

The discussions also paved the way for the Iranian negotiating team to accompany the Qatari delegation on its return trip to Doha, according to the report.

"Negotiations with the US side are taking place indirectly through the mediator, not directly," the Iranian source told the newspaper.

Sources close to Qatar- and Pakistan-led mediation efforts also told Al-Araby Al-Jadeed that an American delegation was expected to join the diplomatic process in Doha.

The sources said the US delegation could hold direct talks with Iranian negotiators in the Qatari capital.

Trump may order major Iran strike if Republicans suffer losses in midterm election: Axios

US President Donald Trump may be more inclined to approve a large-scale military operation against Iran if Republicans fare badly in the midterm elections next week, according to a report on Friday.

"If he feels embarrassed or disenfranchised, he will do something bold," a US official told Axios, adding that it is the message being passed to Iranian officials, who are being told their best chance for a deal is now.

A White House official rejected the idea, telling the outlet that election results will not factor into Trump's decisions on Iran.

The report said Qatari mediators spent more than 12 hours on Friday in Tehran, staying in regular contact with the White House, to restart direct talks between Washington and Tehran. A diplomatic source described "positive progress," and discussions are due to continue on Saturday in Doha.

Talks have stalled over competing demands, according to one US official. Washington wants nuclear concessions as part of any return to negotiations, while Tehran insists the US first lift its naval blockade, release frozen funds and allow oil sales.

The report said Doha is urging Iran to allow UN inspectors into its bombed nuclear sites in exchange for limited sanctions relief.

Pointing to divisions within Trump's circle, the report said Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio are sceptical of any deal and favour further weakening of Iran’s leadership. Vice President JD Vance and envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner back resuming talks.

The report comes amid heightened tensions between Iran and the US over the Strait of Hormuz, a strategic waterway for global energy shipments.

The navy’s public relations office said the supertanker, carrying more than 2 million barrels of crude oil, ignored repeated radio warnings against using the southern passage through the strategic waterway.

Oman evacuates injured crew from Indian boat targeted in Strait of Hormuz

Oman announced on Friday that it had medically evacuated an injured crew member from an Indian boat targeted in the Strait of Hormuz.

The military’s Directorate of Moral Guidance said the Royal Air Force of Oman, in coordination with relevant authorities, carried out the evacuation from an Indian boat that had come under attack in the strategic waterway.

The injured crew member was airlifted from Khasab Hospital in the northern governorate of Musandam to Khawla Hospital in the capital, Muscat, for specialized medical treatment, it said in a statement on X.

headline: Yemeni army captures strategic mountain range from Houthis in Al-Jawf
description: Coalition spokesman gives no details on launch site, damage
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
The Yemeni army has completed its capture of a strategic mountain range in the northern province of Al-Jawf following battles with Houthi forces, a field commander said Saturday.

Col Rabie al-Qurashi, an army field commander in Al-Jawf, told Anadolu that government forces had secured the entire Huwayshian mountain range east of Al-Hazm, the provincial capital.

He said the advance followed fighting with the Houthis and was backed by warplanes that destroyed dozens of vehicles belonging to the group. The military operation remains underway, he added.

The mountains form the first line of defense for Al-Hazm, which remains under Houthi control, al-Qurashi said.

According to local Yemeni media, capturing the high ground enables government forces to cut Houthi supply routes in the province. The mountains also overlook key Houthi positions near Al-Hazm.

Government forces seized parts of the range during clashes Friday before completing their capture Saturday, according to an Anadolu correspondent.

Al-Jawf is strategically important because it borders Saudi Arabia and lies close to the Houthi-controlled provinces of Saada, Amran and Sanaa. It also borders the oil-producing provinces of Hadramout and Marib, which are under government control.

Control of Al-Jawf remains divided, with the Houthis holding Al-Hazm and other areas, while government forces control other parts of the province. Both sides continue to contest strategic positions.

Fighting has intensified in recent weeks as government-aligned forces backed by the Saudi-led coalition have carried out military operations against Houthi positions in Taiz and other provinces.

The escalation comes amid renewed hostilities between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia, with both sides reporting attacks and military operations across Yemen and the wider region.

Saudi-led coalition intercepts drones in multiple areas of kingdom

The Saudi-led coalition said on Saturday thait had intercepted and destroyed a hostile drone over the "Riyadh region." launched by the Houthi group over the kingdom's southern region.

Coalition spokesperson Turki al-Maliki said in a statement on US social media platform X that the drone was intercepted and destroyed, without providing details on its launch site, intended target or damage. He added that the interception fragments fell without injuries, "and the site is currently being directly addressed by the competent authorities."

Earlier on Saturday, on two separate occasions, the spokesperson said that the coalition destroyed a Houthi drone in the southern region of the kingdom launched by the Houthis.

Additionally, around midnight on Saturday, the spokesperson said a drone was intercepted and destroyed in the Madina region.

The coalition, formally known as the Coalition to Support Legitimacy in Yemen, has been fighting the Houthi group in Yemen.

The incident came amid escalating hostilities between the Houthis and the coalition, including attacks targeting Saudi airports and energy facilities.

Saudi Arabia has led a military coalition supporting Yemen’s government against the Houthis since 2015.

The group has controlled the capital, Sanaa, and parts of Yemen since 2014.

The escalation comes amid renewed hostilities between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia, with both sides reporting attacks and military operations across Yemen and the wider region.
Saudi-led coalition intercepts drones in multiple areas of kingdom
The Saudi-led coalition said on Saturday thait had intercepted and destroyed a hostile drone over the "Riyadh region." launched by the Houthi group over the kingdom's southern region.

Coalition spokesperson Turki al-Maliki said in a statement on US social media platform X that the drone was intercepted and destroyed, without providing details on its launch site, intended target or damage. He added that the interception fragments fell without injuries, "and the site is currently being directly addressed by the competent authorities."
Earlier on Saturday, on two separate occasions, the spokesperson said that the coalition destroyed a Houthi drone in the southern region of the kingdom launched by the Houthis.
Additionally, around midnight on Saturday, the spokesperson said a drone was intercepted and destroyed in the Madina region.
The coalition, formally known as the Coalition to Support Legitimacy in Yemen, has been fighting the Houthi group in Yemen.
The incident came amid escalating hostilities between the Houthis and the coalition, including attacks targeting Saudi airports and energy facilities.
Saudi Arabia has led a military coalition supporting Yemen’s government against the Houthis since 2015.
The group has controlled the capital, Sanaa, and parts of Yemen since 2014.

BENGALURU: ​Pacer ​Auqib Nabi has been added to India's squad for the first three one-day internationals ‌against New Zealand, the country's cricket board said on Saturday.

The ‌29-year-old, who made his ⁠India ​debut against West ​Indies in ‌September, was initially named in ​the squad for the fourth and fifth ODIs but has now been ⁠drafted in from the start of the ‌five-match series.

headline: Pakistan urges Afghan Taliban to take 'decisive action' against terrorist groups
description: UN envoy highlights nexus between Taliban, terrorist groups; calls for end to restrictions on Afghan girls
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Pakistan urged Afghan Taliban authorities to "take decisive action" against terrorist groups operating from Afghan territory, questioning the Taliban's "complicity and support" for groups including the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and reaffirming its right to self-defence.

The Permanent Mission of Pakistan to the United Nations, in a press release, noted that Counsellor Muhammad Jawad Ajmal, addressing the Interactive Dialogue with the Special Rapporteur on the situation of human rights in Afghanistan in the Third Committee of the UN General Assembly, underscored that "terrorism remained at the heart of Afghanistan's challenges."

He expressed concern over the presence and activities of terrorist groups including the TTP, the Balochistan Liberation Army, Majeed Brigade, the ISIL-K, and the ETIM, along with their affiliates operating from Afghan territory.

Highlighting the nexus between the Afghan Taliban regime and these groups, Ajmal noted "the role of external actors supporting proxy elements targeting Pakistan and other neighbouring countries."

The Taliban's continued failure to publicly denounce these groups raised serious concern about their complicity and support, he said.

Relations between Pakistan and Afghanistan have strained due to recurring cross-border terrorism and security concerns. Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Afghan Taliban administration to prevent terrorist organisations, particularly the TTP, from using its territory to launch attacks inside Pakistan.

The release noted that Ajmal highlighted the civilian cost of the complicity, saying that more than 4,700 innocent Pakistanis had lost their lives over the past three years alone in terrorist attacks emanating from Afghan territory.

Referring to Pakistan's actions on March 16, the counsellor stated that Islamabad had "precisely targeted military installations and terrorist support infrastructure including drone and ammunition storage facilities used by the TTP to target innocent Pakistani civilians."

Ajmal stressed that Pakistan "could not remain passive in the face of continued terrorist attacks against its people and national security," stating that it would "exercise its right to self-defence, whenever necessary and in accordance with international law, against any threat to its citizens and national security."

He called on the Afghan Taliban authorities to "honour their international commitments and obligations," reaffirming Pakistan's commitment to a stable, peaceful and prosperous Afghanistan that "lives in harmoney with itself and its neighbours."

Meanwhile he also "observed the denial of fundamental freedoms and basic dignity to women and girls," calling on the Afghan Taliban authorities to end their restrictions on women and girls.

This, the release said, was "reflected in the Taliban's continued retreat from their international commitments." Ajmal also stressed that "such discriminatory and abusive practices" remained inconsistent with Islamic laws, traditions and the fundamental tenets of the Muslim faith.

In this regard, the counsellor recalled that Pakistan had hosted the 9th Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) Ministerial Conference on Women in Islamabad in July this year, undertaking the adoption of the Islamabad Declaration "expressing concern over the Taliban's continued restrictions on women and girls as being contrary to Islamic values."

Further, Ajmal noted Pakistan's "longstanding humanitarian contribution," highlighting that it had hosted millions of Afghan refugees over several decades, "often in the absence of adequate international support."

The counsellor argued that while Pakistan "continued to facilitate vulnerable Afghans within its available capacity," the international community had to step up and share the resposibility of addressing the refugee situation.

headline: AI chatbots face scrutiny over failure to report criminal confessions
description: AI chatbots face scrutiny over failure to report criminal confessions
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots can be told about crimes, but uncertainties surrounding legal frameworks or measures that would mandate these tools to report confessions to law enforcement cast doubt on the pace of AI development.

AI chatbots have entered daily life, with many users worldwide using and sometimes misusing these tools, often making headlines around the world.

In August, a 19-year-old University of Missouri student reportedly confessed to ChatGPT that he damaged 17 parked cars on campus late at night and asked, “Will I go to jail?”

ChatGPT responded with “tips about the potential outcome of getting caught” but urged the user to dial 911 after the messages grew increasingly aggressive, police documents showed.

The chat history was uncovered after the student allowed investigators to examine his phone, and the history was used as evidence against him in court, becoming instrumental in the felony property-damage charges against him.

In a similar instance, court records in Florida showed that days before two college students went missing in April and were later found dead, their roommate had asked ChatGPT, “What happens if a human has put in a black garbage bag and thrown in a dumpster.”

Canada’s British Columbia provincial government filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, the developer of ChatGPT.

The lawsuit, filed in February, concerned a mass school shooting that left nine people, mostly children, dead and 27 injured.

The case alleged that the firm failed to report the shooter’s chat with ChatGPT to law enforcement and argued that the attack could have been prevented if OpenAI had warned police.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman apologised in a letter, but whistleblowers told The Wall Street Journal that the conversation between the shooter and ChatGPT had allegedly already been flagged in June 2025. However, Altman and the firm’s leadership reportedly overrode the safety team’s recommendations to contact police.

The ethical implications of these interactions continue to deepen, as a study in Australia found that children are more likely to report sexual abuse online to chatbots than to responsible adults.

The same privacy principles that apply between lawyers and clients or doctors and patients do not apply to AI chatbot conversations, so tech firms can share logs with investigators.

While researchers debate whether chatbots should report crimes, the prospect is further complicated by algorithms misinterpreting intent.

For instance, Anthropic’s Claude 5 gave a false tip about an unsolved murder to a US police hotline in July.

AI chatbots should not be used in crime prediction

Matthew Trail, an American legal scholar and researcher at Goethe University in Germany, told Anadolu that each company developing AI chatbots adopts different rules and that these chatbots are not designed to respond to inquiries about planning murders and similar acts.

Trail stated that chatbots are trained to avoid certain topics, especially those regarding child sexual abuse, and refer these conversations to human moderators. However, users can compose their prompts in a certain way, such as by pretending to ask for help with writing fiction, to circumvent these filters and obtain AI-generated answers to otherwise inappropriate questions or requests.

Trail noted that while law enforcement could request a person’s chat history from AI firms when the person is suspected of having committed a crime, the primary goal of AI chatbots must not be to predict crimes before they are committed, as laws and policies surrounding this prospect are very unclear.

He added that allowing these AI models to collect more data than they already do to make more accurate assessments of crime potential is not a good idea, either.

Can AI chatbot conversations ever be private?

People across the globe discuss a myriad of topics with AI chatbots, especially personal matters ranging from health issues to psychological support and life advice.

As more and more people turn to AI for conversations, ethical debates over privacy have come to the fore.

Altman said in July 2025 that conversations with AI chatbots must be based on confidentiality.

Robert Diab, a law professor at Thompson Rivers University in Canada, stated that laws do not treat communications between accomplices as confidential, arguing that chats between humans and AI chatbots could be treated according to the same principle.

Diab said models like ChatGPT appear to be capable of detecting when users are prone to criminal behaviour and argued that chatbot developers could prevent crime by notifying law enforcement.

He mentioned that alerting law enforcement based on all suspicious messages could also increase the workload of human teams due to false alarms.

He added that users will always find a way to circumvent security measures to use AI to commit a crime.

headline: Selma Blair says ‘I am so sorry’ in public apology following plane incident
description: The actress says she never intended to hurt or frighten anyone as she faces assault charges in New York
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Selma Blair has publicly apologised following an incident aboard a flight from Los Angeles to New York that led to her arrest and criminal charges.

The Cruel Intentions and Legally Blonde actress, 54, shared a video statement on Instagram on October 30, addressing the October 11 incident at John F Kennedy International Airport. She allegedly injured a flight attendant and kicked a nurse after being removed from the aircraft.

View this post on Instagram

Blair is facing two second-degree assault charges related to alleged attacks on the nurse and a Port Authority officer. In her video, the actress said her legal team had advised her against discussing the case in detail.

“What I can tell you, though, is very simple, and the truest thing I know about myself, and that not one day ever have I intended to hurt or frighten anyone a day in my life,” Blair said.

She then addressed those affected by the incident, adding: “To the people that I disappointed, that I hurt, I frightened, alarmed: I am so sorry.”

Blair’s representatives previously attributed the episode to a medical emergency. Her attorney, Shawn Barnes, told the court that she had boarded the flight after missing several doses of medication used to control neurological symptoms.

According to her lawyer, the missed medication, combined with the effects of altitude, resulted in severe confusion and disorientation. Barnes also said Blair had fallen and hit her head during the flight.

The actress was released from custody on $20,000 bail the day after the incident.

Blair is scheduled to return to court in Queens on January 19, where proceedings related to the charges are expected to continue.

The case remains ongoing, and the allegations have not been established in court. Her apology marks her first public statement addressing the incident directly, as she continues to face legal proceedings in New York.

The Cruel Intentions and Legally Blonde actress, 54, shared a video statement on Instagram on October 30, addressing the October 11 incident at John F Kennedy International Airport. She allegedly injured a flight attendant and kicked a nurse after being removed from the aircraft.

View this post on Instagram

Blair is facing two second-degree assault charges related to alleged attacks on the nurse and a Port Authority officer. In her video, the actress said her legal team had advised her against discussing the case in detail.

“What I can tell you, though, is very simple, and the truest thing I know about myself, and that not one day ever have I intended to hurt or frighten anyone a day in my life,” Blair said.

She then addressed those affected by the incident, adding: “To the people that I disappointed, that I hurt, I frightened, alarmed: I am so sorry.”

Blair’s representatives previously attributed the episode to a medical emergency. Her attorney, Shawn Barnes, told the court that she had boarded the flight after missing several doses of medication used to control neurological symptoms.

According to her lawyer, the missed medication, combined with the effects of altitude, resulted in severe confusion and disorientation. Barnes also said Blair had fallen and hit her head during the flight.

The actress was released from custody on $20,000 bail the day after the incident.

Blair is scheduled to return to court in Queens on January 19, where proceedings related to the charges are expected to continue.

The case remains ongoing, and the allegations have not been established in court. Her apology marks her first public statement addressing the incident directly, as she continues to face legal proceedings in New York.

headline: Leclerc quickest in Mexico GP practice
description: Monegasque driver clocks a best lap in one minute and 17.827 seconds
author: AFP
article_text:
Ferrari's Charles Leclerc dominated practice for the Mexico City Grand Prix on Friday, clocking the fastest times in both sessions for the second weekend running.

The Monegasque driver clocked a best lap in one minute and 17.827 seconds in the second practice session to outpace McLaren's world champion Lando Norris by 0.103 seconds with George Russell finishing third ahead of his Mercedes team-mate runaway championship leader Kimi Antonelli.

Antonelli, 20, who was absent on Thursday to recover from a virus, can become the sport's youngest champion on Sunday, and Italy's first since 1963, if he finishes in the top nine.

He can also take the title if his two remaining rivals – Russell and Ferrari's seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton – fail to win.

Leclerc's success on Friday repeated his showing in Austin, Texas, at last weekend's United States Grand Prix.

Red Bull's four-time champion Max Verstappen, a record five-time winner in Mexico, was fifth ahead of team-mate Isack Hadjar after an early clash with Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson which left him with damaged bodywork.

Lawson's team-mate Arvid Lindblad was seventh ahead of Alpine's Pierre Gasly, Lawson and Oscar Piastri in the second McLaren.

Seven-time champion Hamilton was down in 11th for Ferrari after suffering a power failure that ended his running midway through.

The session began with Gasly leading Alpine team-mate Franco Colapinto out ahead of Cadillac’s local hero Sergio Perez, set for his 300th race start, the seventh driver to reach this landmark. He was promptly cautioned for a pit lane infringement.

After the inclusion of 10 rookie reserves in free practice one, all 22 full-timers were back with a wide range of tyres on show – Ferrari taking mediums, Verstappen softs and others hards on the low-grip track.

A red flag paused the action after 15 minutes to clear debris in the Foro Sol after Verstappen clashed with stable-mate Lawson and damaged his car’s bargeboard.

The frustrated Dutchman's actions seemed excessively aggressive and required a Red Bull pit-stop for repairs. The incident was noted by the stewards and set for investigation afterwards.

Ferrari dominated the early stages with Leclerc on top before Norris, on softs, took command as McLaren bounced back shortly before Hamilton lost power and pulled up on the straight.

He had just switched to softs and completed one lap.

It was a setback for Hamilton who lost vital learning time on softs while Leclerc regained the initiative ahead of Norris, Russell and Antonelli before the field switched to heavier fuel loads and medium tyres.

headline: Verstappen slams Red Bull stable-mate
description: Dutch driver faces one-place grid penalty for the Mexico City GP
author: AFP
article_text:
Max Verstappen slammed his Red Bull stable-mate Liam Lawson as "not very smart" after a Friday practice crash that saw both hit with one-place grid penalties for the Mexico City Grand Prix.

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc topped the times ahead of world champion Lando Norris of McLaren in an eventful session that saw Kimi Antonelli wind up fourth as he closes in on the title.

Red Bulls' four-time champion Verstappen was embroiled in an incident that left him with damaged bodywork, tangling with Racing Bulls' Lawson in a feisty fight for track position going into the Foro Sol section.

Verstappen said New Zealand's Lawson caused the trouble near turn 12, their minor collision spewing debris over the circuit and causing the session to be red-flagged for the track to be cleared.

"It was not unlucky," said the Dutchman. "It was not very smart behaviour by him in what he was trying to do there. But it is not going to change my weekend."

Both drivers were summoned by the stewards, who found they behaved in a manner that was "unacceptable" and handed out the penalty.

"I think it is just not very smart behaviour when you are fighting for your seat," Verstappen said, a reference to Lawson's admission this week that he does not know if he will retain his place next season with Racing Bulls, despite an impressive season with the sister team to Red Bull.

Racing Bulls may move to promote Red Bull junior driver Nikola Tsolov, who on Friday became the first Bulgarian driver to take part in an official practice session at a Grand Prix when he drove in FP1.

Lawson has impressed throughout the year and outperformed team-mate rookie Arvid Lindblad comprehensively.

On Thursday he told reporters that finding consistency in formula one is hard, but he believed he has "maximised a lot this year.

"I’m not really sure what more is expected, but I’m not really sitting here thinking too much about the whole seat selection thing.

"I overthought things last year so I’m trying a different mindset this year to score as many points as I can."

Lawson is ninth in the drivers' championship with 77 points while teammate Lindblad is 11th on 38.

His performances have helped lift Racing Bulls to fifth in the constructors' title race behind the big four of Mercedes, Ferrari, Red Bull and McLaren.

He ended up ninth in Friday FP2 while Verstappen was fifth behind the Mercedes of George Russell and 20-year-old Italian Antonelli -- who is poised to become the sport’s youngest champion on Sunday if he finishes in the top nine.

Verstappen, a five-time winner in Mexico, admitted: "It could have gone better, but we're not too far off and just have some fine tuning to do. No one has much grip here but it is the same for us all and nothing new."

headline: Abbas puts Pakistan in Hong Kong Sixes Plate final
description: Skipper hits 13-ball 55 as Green-shirts chase 107 in the fifth over against Hong Kong
author: Sports Desk
article_text:
Captain Abbas Afridi smashed a blistering 55 as Pakistan defeated hosts Hong Kong by five wickets in the Plate semi-final of the Hong Kong Sixes on Saturday to set up a final against Oman.

Hong Kong posted 106-3 in their allotted six overs at Mission Road Ground in Mong Kok, but Pakistan chased down the target in just 4.3 overs despite losing five wickets.

Abbas led the charge with 55 off only 13 deliveries, hitting three fours and seven sixes. Khawaja Nafay added 34 from 10 balls, including two fours and four sixes, before Abdul Samad struck a rapid 17 off four deliveries to complete the chase.

Hong Kong had made a strong start after being sent in, with Nizakat Khan top-scoring with 38 off 10 balls, including one four and five sixes.

Anshy Rath contributed 37 from 15 deliveries, striking four boundaries and three sixes, while Babar Hayat made 12 off six balls.

Nasrulla Rana provided a late boost with 16 from just three deliveries, hitting one four and two sixes. Hong Kong captain Yasim Murtaza was dismissed for a duck.

Irfan Khan took two wickets for Pakistan, conceding 16 runs in his only over, while Ahmed Daniyal claimed one.

Six-time champions and defending title-holders Pakistan were knocked out of contention for the main Cup semi-finals after finishing second in Group C.

Abbas's side suffered a last-ball defeat to the United Arab Emirates in their opening match on Friday, despite posting 106-3 with the captain scoring 53.

Pakistan bounced back by beating arch-rivals India, restricting them to 88-5 before reaching 91-2 in 3.5 overs. Nafay scored 41 and Abbas contributed 35.

But the UAE secured the group’s sole Cup semi-final berth by winning both matches, including a dominant victory over India, whom they chased down for 95 without losing a wicket in four overs.

headline: Pakistan crowned ODI tri-series champions
description: Fakhar (127), Saad (74) and Minhas (61) star in superb victory over Sri Lanka
author: Sports Desk
article_text:
KARACHI: Fakhar Zaman slammed superb hundred as Pakistan were crowned champions when they overhelmed Sri Lanka by three wickets in the final of the ODI tri-series at Gaddafi Stadium Lahore on Saturday.

Fakhar smashed 127 as hosts chased down the 326-run target with nine balls to spare after losing seven wickets in the process.

Fakhar, who had hit his previous century three years ago, added 149 for the third wicket partnership with Saad Baig who hammered 75-ball 74. Saad, who hit his maiden fifty, smashed 11 well-timed fours before being held off his own bowling by spinner Maheesh Theekshana.

Fakhar, who scored his 12th century of his career, also completed 4000 runs when he reached 108.

Left-hander, who reached his century off 84 balls, then added 57 for the fourth wicket association with Agha Salman before being bowled by pacer Madushanka.

Fakhar struck six sixes and 11 fours in his 99-ball match-winning knock.

Dunith Wellalage then got rid of Agha Salman (17) to create some hopes for Sri Lanka.

However, Arafat Minhas and Hasan Nawaz thwarted that threat by sharing 94 runs for the sixth wicket partnership to make things easier for the hosts.

Asitha Fernando removed Arafat who struck a fiery 31-ball 61, clobbering four sixes and three fours.

Fernando had Faheem Ashraf (0) off his next delivery but Hasan and Shaheen (6*) did the rest of the work to seal a fine win.

Hasan struck two fours in his 45-ball 37 not out.

Dilshan Madushanka was the pick of the bowlers with 3-63 in 9.3 overs.

Chasing a stiff target Pakistan had a poor start when Dilshan Madushanka removed Maaz Sadaqat (5) and Babar Azam (0) cheaply to put Pakistan in deep trouble.

Earlier opener Kamindu Mendis struck a brilliant 131 while Pavan Rathnayake contributed 77 as Sri Lanka posted a fighting total of 325-8.

After Pakistan elected to field, Sri Lanka made a steady start through openers Avishka Fernando and Kamindu, who put on 87 for the first wicket.

Salman Ali Agha broke the stand in the 18th over when he had Fernando, trapped lbw, for 38. He faced 49 balls and hammered three fours and a six in his nice knock.

Salman struck again when he dismissed captain Kusal Mendis (8) cheaply to leave Sri Lanka at 109-2.

Kamindu then joined forces with Rathnayake to rebuild the innings. The pair added 146 for the third wicket stand to put Sri Lanka in a commanding position.

Kamindu brought up his maiden century off 107 balls while Rathnayake reached his fifty off 47 deliveries.

The partnership ended in the 42nd over when Kamindu was dismissed by Haris Rauf for 131 off 128 balls. His innings included 12 fours and two sixes.

Rathnayake, who has also hit two centuries in the series, continued to score freely before falling to Rauf for 77 off 65 balls, having struck eight fours.

Sri Lanka were 255-3 when Kamindu departed. However Pakistan fought back with regular wickets in the closing overs.

Dasun Shanaka struck a nine-ball 17, hitting two fours and a six before Shaheen Afridi dismissed him.

Janith Liyanage managed six before falling to Naseem Shah, who also removed Sahan Arachchige for 15.

Maheesh Theekshana remained not out on nine while Asitha Fernando chipped in with an unbeaten seven to help Sri Lanka finish at a decent total.

Shaheen, Naseem, Agha Salman and Haris Rauf claimed two wickets each. Haris conceded 61 runs in 9.6 overs while Naseem remained the expensive bowler as he conceded 80 runs in his quota of ten overs.

Pakistan made one change, brining in Faheem Ashraf in place of Shadab Khan.

Sri Lanka dropped Eshan Malinga and brought in spinner Maheesh Theekshana to boost their bowling.

Earlier Pakistan won the toss and opted to bowl first. Pakistan made one change, brining in Faheem Ashraf in place of Shadab Khan who was not feeling well. Sri Lanka dropped Eshan Malinga and brought in Maheesh Theekshana.

headline: US approves $2.1 billion Patriot missile sale to Ukraine
description: Delayed missile deliveries have added to Ukraine's tensions with US after Trump announced diesel deal with Russia
author: Reuters
article_text:
The US State Department said on Friday it approved the sale of 500 Patriot PAC-3 missiles to Ukraine for an estimated $2.1 billion, one of the most significant steps to supply defensive weapons to Kyiv since the start of the second Trump administration.

Delayed missile deliveries have added to Ukraine's tensions with the US after President Donald Trump announced a diesel deal with Russia and criticised Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy ​for Ukraine's unwillingness to stop attacks on Russian refineries.

Ukraine has long said it urgently needs more missile interceptors to knock down ​the growing waves of missiles Russia's military fires at the country. The Patriot missile system is the most effective ⁠weapon to counter fast-moving ballistic missiles.

On Thursday, a Russian drone strike killed at least 14 people on a crowded rail platform in the Ukrainian ​city of Dnipro, while 5 died in daytime strikes on two other provincial cities and a late-evening missile strike killed 1 person in the ​capital Kyiv, officials said.

Zelenskiy said on Monday that Ukraine had been waiting for almost a month for the US to sign off on critical missile supplies, as Russia stepped up attacks on energy and civilian infrastructure.

But despite Ukraine's urgency, it will likely not receive the missile interceptors quickly. Weapons sales typically take years to fulfil, and ​two people briefed on the US decision said the missiles — which are yet to be manufactured — are not expected to be delivered until ​a couple of years into the 2030s.

One of the people said Ukraine's Ministry of Defence is encouraging the Pentagon to bring forward the delivery date, possibly by ‌giving Kyiv ⁠missiles already in the US arsenal and backfilling with the new Patriot interceptors.

Ukraine will pay for the missiles with contributions from Canada, Germany and Norway routed through a program called US JUMPSTART, along with national funds financed by the European Union's Ukraine Support Loan, the State Department said in a statement.

The program uses donations from allies to buy weapons, services and training for Ukraine to support its self-defence following Russia's invasion, according to ​a Pentagon website.

The JUMPSTART program was ​used in August to buy ⁠3,350 air-launched cruise missiles worth $825 million made by Zone 5 Technologies and CoAspire.

Lockheed Martin is the principal contractor for the sale of the Patriot interceptors.

The US has supplied large quantities of weapons to allies while also ​using munitions in its own military operations in Iran, raising concerns about inventories of key air defence ​and precision-guided weapons.

In July, ⁠the US Army awarded Lockheed a contract worth up to $58.6 billion to produce Patriot interceptor missiles.

Lockheed has said that deal would allow it to follow through on a promise to triple PAC-3 MSE production capacity by the end of 2030 and increase jobs at its Camden, Arkansas, plant by 50%, to ⁠about 1,850 ​from 1,200. Lockheed previously announced Patriot PAC-3 missile interceptor production would go to 2,000 units ​annually.

Pentagon negotiators are pressing contractors to move much faster, with tentative production agreements struck earlier this year at the center of efforts to increase missile output.

headline: France braces for fresh unrest, government vows tough response
description: Interior minister warns of 'extremely firm response to any trouble' as authorities on alert
author: Reuters
article_text:
France will deploy a 70,000-strong police presence to contain a widely expected bout of fresh unrest on Saturday in the latest nationwide protests driven by anger over living costs, public services and President Emmanuel Macron's government.

The nationwide demonstrations, which fall on Halloween, come two weeks after riots and looting caught security forces off guard, leaving damaged shops, public buildings and businesses in cities across France.

Interior Minister Laurent Nunez has vowed not to let a repeat happen. "Everyone is on deck to ensure an extremely firm response to any trouble," Nunez told a news conference earlier this week as he set out details of security arrangements for a day he described as carrying "a very high risk" of unrest.

Authorities are also alert to the possibility that rioters could use Halloween masks to conceal their identities. Nunez noted that laws already allow police to ban face coverings when public order is at risk.

The United States Embassy advised travellers to avoid areas where demonstrations or large gatherings are planned.

The protests gathered pace in late September as Macron's minority government launched 2027 budget talks. Facing public debt approaching 120% of economic output and rising borrowing costs, the government is under pressure to rein in spending, narrowing its room for manoeuvre.

Students angry at the dilapidated state of many schools, crowded classes and a university admissions system widely seen as unfair have been joined by trade unions and a re-emergent "Yellow Vest" movement demanding action on the cost of living.

Protests spread across Europe

The protests have inspired youth-led protests across Europe, with demonstrations planned in more than 30 German cities on Saturday.

The French government's promises to reform education and ease fuel costs have failed to calm discontent.

"When I was little, I was told young people were the future," said Aaron Berthier de Grandry, a 15-year-old high school student in the Paris suburb of Nogent-sur-Marne who plans to join his third consecutive weekend of protests. "Well, if we, as the future of France, lack resources, that means France will end up collapsing."

The unrest has handed a political boost to far-right leader Marine Le Pen, who leads opinion polls ahead of April's presidential election, while potential centrist successors to Macron remain divided.

The troubles are the latest blow to an economy which, data on Friday showed, was already shrinking in the third quarter.

The Chamber of Commerce estimates losses to retailers exceed €1 billion ($1.1 billion). Other estimates put the total at double when including uninsured damage and lost revenue.

Along Paris' main shopping boulevards, early Christmas lights glow around boarded-up windows and security grilles. Among the shops targeted in previous unrest were outlets belonging to luxury brands including Hermes, Louis Vuitton and Burberry.

The government is pushing ahead with a controversial law making rioters liable to pay up to €10,000 ($11,000) for damage caused either by themselves or by groups they are deemed to be part of. Rights groups and some lawyers say the measure risks undermining the right to peaceful protest.

article_html:
France will deploy a 70,000-strong police presence to contain a widely expected bout of fresh unrest on Saturday in the latest nationwide protests driven by anger over living costs, public services and President Emmanuel Macron's government.

The nationwide demonstrations, which fall on Halloween, come two weeks after riots and looting caught security forces off guard, leaving damaged shops, public buildings and businesses in cities across France.

Interior Minister Laurent Nunez has vowed not to let a repeat happen. "Everyone is on deck to ensure an extremely firm response to any trouble," Nunez told a news conference earlier this week as he set out details of security arrangements for a day he described as carrying "a very high risk" of unrest.

Read: ‘Threat exists’: Paris police warn of possible unrest ahead of protests

Authorities are also alert to the possibility that rioters could use Halloween masks to conceal their identities. Nunez noted that laws already allow police to ban face coverings when public order is at risk.

The United States Embassy advised travellers to avoid areas where demonstrations or large gatherings are planned.

The protests gathered pace in late September as Macron's minority government launched 2027 budget talks. Facing public debt approaching 120% of economic output and rising borrowing costs, the government is under pressure to rein in spending, narrowing its room for manoeuvre.

Students angry at the dilapidated state of many schools, crowded classes and a university admissions system widely seen as unfair have been joined by trade unions and a re-emergent "Yellow Vest" movement demanding action on the cost of living.

Protests spread across Europe

The protests have inspired youth-led protests across Europe, with demonstrations planned in more than 30 German cities on Saturday.

The French government's promises to reform education and ease fuel costs have failed to calm discontent.

"When I was little, I was told young people were the future," said Aaron Berthier de Grandry, a 15-year-old high school student in the Paris suburb of Nogent-sur-Marne who plans to join his third consecutive weekend of protests. "Well, if we, as the future of France, lack resources, that means France will end up collapsing."

The unrest has handed a political boost to far-right leader Marine Le Pen, who leads opinion polls ahead of April's presidential election, while potential centrist successors to Macron remain divided.

The troubles are the latest blow to an economy which, data on Friday showed, was already shrinking in the third quarter.

Read More: French PM calls for 'partial curfews' in cities hit by riots and looting

The Chamber of Commerce estimates losses to retailers exceed €1 billion ($1.1 billion). Other estimates put the total at double when including uninsured damage and lost revenue.

Along Paris' main shopping boulevards, early Christmas lights glow around boarded-up windows and security grilles. Among the shops targeted in previous unrest were outlets belonging to luxury brands including Hermes, Louis Vuitton and Burberry.

The government is pushing ahead with a controversial law making rioters liable to pay up to €10,000 ($11,000) for damage caused either by themselves or by groups they are deemed to be part of. Rights groups and some lawyers say the measure risks undermining the right to peaceful protest.

headline: Karachi court approves Iqrarul Hassan's bail plea
description: Orders his release against surety bonds of Rs200,000, forensic report awaited
author: Nasir Butt
article_text:
Karachi's city court on Saturday approved the bail application of media personality Iqrarul Hassan, ordering his release against surety bonds of Rs200,000 in a case of harming the state and national integrity through the dissemination of anti-state content on his social media platforms.

On October 13, Hassan was handed over to the NCCIA on a four-day physical remand. On October 15, the District and Sessions Court East dismissed a petition challenging Hassan's physical remand, with the defence counsel questioning the legality of the proceedings and arguing that the case concerned digital and cyber matters. A day later, his physical remand was extended by two days.

Judicial Magistrate Karachi East Judge Gulraiz Memon, as per the judgement, noted that Hassan's bail "cannot be withheld as a mechanism of pre-trial punishment," adding that the "learned AD Legal for the NCCIA has only half-heartedly opposed the application without pointing out any extraordinary grounds to justify keeping the accused incarcerated."

According to Advocate Ahmad Masood, the charge sheet had been submitted against Hassan while his mobile devices were taken into custody.

Meanwhile, the NCCIA noted that no further investigation was required against Hassan; however, the forensic report was still awaited.

According to the FIR, Hassan, "through his personal social media accounts on the platforms X, Instagram and Facebook, is intentionally disseminating false, fabricated, anti-state and defamatory content with the object of instigating the general public against the state, its institutions and its functionaries."

The FIR stated that the content of Hassan's social media posts portrayed the state, its institutions and its functionaries "in a false and distorted manner."

It also noted that Hassan "represented lawful measures as controversial with the intent to instigate and incite the general public at large against the state and the lawfully constituted authorities."

The FIR stated further, "The accused instigated a substantial following, including the general public, on the aforesaid platforms," adding that the content that he posted was published and broadcast "in an open, publicly accessible manner, without restriction, so as to reach and influence the public at large throughout Pakistan and abroad."

Hassan's wife Farah Iqrar told The Express Tribune on October 12 that a group of unidentified individuals posing as officials of the NCCIA had allegedly taken him away from their residence in Lahore’s Defence C area.

According to Farah, between five and seven people, including women, arrived at the house late on Sunday night, during the intervening hours of Sunday and Monday, and demanded that Hassan come outside. She alleged that the individuals threatened to break down the door if he was not handed over. They subsequently entered the house, forcibly took the journalist from a room and took him away.

headline: ‘Obsession’ director Curry Barker wants to collaborate with Nathan Fielder and has already pitched a project together
description: Barker made clear that his admiration extended to Fielder’s creative approach describing it as fresh and different
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Obsession director Curry Barker has expressed interest in working with Nathan Fielder after watching the filmmaker’s unconventional project You Can See Everything, revealing that he has already approached him about a possible collaboration.

Speaking to Variety at the Time100 Next Gala on Thursday, Barker praised the film, which explores the story of Elizabeth Holmes through a format that blurs the boundaries between documentary and narrative filmmaking.

“I thought it was freakin’ insane and awesome,” Barker said, admitting that he knew little about Holmes’ story before watching it. He also said he wished the three-hour film had been longer, describing that reaction as rare.

Barker made clear that his admiration extended to Fielder’s creative approach. He described You Can See Everything as fresh and different, adding that he found it difficult to categorise the project as a conventional documentary.

When asked whether he would consider working with Fielder, Barker revealed that he had already raised the possibility directly with him.

“I told him that. I said, ‘Hey!’ … I just put it out in the water,” the director said.

However, Barker did not reveal whether Fielder had responded with any concrete plans, and no collaboration has been announced.

The two filmmakers have attracted attention for projects that challenge familiar storytelling conventions. Barker directed Obsession, while Fielder’s You Can See Everything has drawn attention for its unusual approach to the story of Holmes.

Barker also shared another memorable moment from the gala, recalling that he froze when he encountered Emma Watson. Having grown up as a fan of the Harry Potter films, he admitted that meeting the actor left him unable to play it cool.

Barker’s next feature, Anything But Ghosts, is scheduled to arrive on May 7, 2027. Actor and filmmaker Seth Rogen, who wrote Barker’s Time100 Next profile, has already praised the upcoming film, saying it is even better than Obsession.

article_html:
Obsession director Curry Barker has expressed interest in working with Nathan Fielder after watching the filmmaker’s unconventional project You Can See Everything, revealing that he has already approached him about a possible collaboration.

Speaking to Variety at the Time100 Next Gala on Thursday, Barker praised the film, which explores the story of Elizabeth Holmes through a format that blurs the boundaries between documentary and narrative filmmaking.

“I thought it was freakin’ insane and awesome,” Barker said, admitting that he knew little about Holmes’ story before watching it. He also said he wished the three-hour film had been longer, describing that reaction as rare.

Barker made clear that his admiration extended to Fielder’s creative approach. He described You Can See Everything as fresh and different, adding that he found it difficult to categorise the project as a conventional documentary.

When asked whether he would consider working with Fielder, Barker revealed that he had already raised the possibility directly with him.

“I told him that. I said, ‘Hey!’ … I just put it out in the water,” the director said.

However, Barker did not reveal whether Fielder had responded with any concrete plans, and no collaboration has been announced.

The two filmmakers have attracted attention for projects that challenge familiar storytelling conventions. Barker directed Obsession, while Fielder’s You Can See Everything has drawn attention for its unusual approach to the story of Holmes.

headline: 2 Palestinians killed in Israel's ongoing violations of Gaza ceasefire
description: 1 killed in drone strike on Nuseirat refugee camp, another dies of wounds from earlier attack in Gaza City
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
A Palestinian was killed in an Israeli strike in central Gaza early Saturday, while another died of wounds sustained in an earlier attack, medical sources told Anadolu.

The deaths came amid continued Israeli army violations of a ceasefire agreement in the Gaza Strip that has been in effect since October 2025.

A medical source at Al-Awda Hospital in central Gaza said Diaa Abu al-Rous was killed in an Israeli strike north of the Nuseirat refugee camp.

Witnesses told Anadolu that an Israeli drone carried out the strike near the headquarters of an electricity company north of the camp.

Separately, Arafat al-Arair died of serious wounds sustained several days earlier in an Israeli strike targeting a vehicle in the Tel al-Hawa neighbourhood, southwest of Gaza City.

A medical source at Al-Shifa Hospital in western Gaza City confirmed his death to Anadolu.

Israeli shelling reported across Gaza

Meanwhile, local sources told Anadolu that Israeli military vehicles and artillery shelled several areas across the Gaza Strip.

The attacks targeted eastern parts of Beit Lahia in northern Gaza, Gaza City, Khan Younis in the south and Deir al-Balah in central Gaza, according to the sources.

Israeli warships also shelled the Gaza City coastline and opened machine-gun fire toward the shore. Israeli military vehicles fired heavily at homes near the al-Sanafour intersection in the eastern Tuffah neighbourhood of Gaza City.

In Khan Younis, local sources reported that Israeli military vehicles opened fire toward tents sheltering displaced Palestinians in the al-Iqlimi and Bir 19 areas south of the city.

Several tents were struck by gunfire, but no injuries were reported, according to the sources.

Ceasefire violations leave over 1,500 dead

Israeli violations of the Gaza ceasefire have killed 1,574 Palestinians and wounded 5,687 others as of Thursday, according to figures released by Gaza's Health Ministry.

Since October 2023, Israel's war in Gaza has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians and wounded over 175,000 others, according to the ministry.

The war has also destroyed around 90% of civilian infrastructure, according to the figures provided.

headline: Mass protests sweep Italy during nationwide strike
description: Grassroots union Unione Sindacale di Base called 24-hour general ​strike, with protests planned in more than 40 cities
author: Reuters
article_text:
Tens of thousands of people, mostly students and workers, ​took to the streets across Italy on Friday to demand ‌higher wages and stronger public services, protest against the rising cost of living and oppose increased military spending.

Grassroots union Unione Sindacale di Base called a 24-hour general ​strike, with protests planned in more than 40 cities.

The demonstrations, which came ​after clashes earlier this month in which protesters fought with ⁠police, looted shops and vandalised property, were largely peaceful, although tensions flared ​in some areas.

In Turin, police used a water cannon to push back ​students and left-wing activists who approached security cordons protecting the prefecture building.

A large march passed near the Colosseum, in Rome, where protesters said they planned to set up ​tents and remain over the weekend. Some rubbish bins were placed ​across streets and set on fire. In the evening, a large group tried to ‌march ⁠towards parliament, prompting police to use water cannon to disperse the crowd, Italian news agency ANSA reported. Eight people were detained after repeatedly trying to break through police barricades, it said.

In Milan, protesters marched onto the ​city’s ring road before ​ending the ⁠march in front of the Politecnico di Milano university. Demonstrators carried flares and set fire to objects.

Around 15,000 ​port workers, students and other demonstrators entered the port ​of Genoa, ⁠joining similar protests in Europe and elsewhere against the use of ports for arms shipments and highlighting the deaths of seafarers in conflicts from the Gulf ⁠to ​the Black Sea.

A wave of protests has ​swept across European countries including France, Spain, Belgium and Albania, driven by grievances including the cost ​of living.

headline: Marka-e-Haq victory enhanced Pakistan's prestige: Defence Minister Khawaja Asif
description: Says international media have also acknowledged Pakistan's success
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif said on Saturday that Pakistan's victory in Marka-e-Haq enhanced the country's international standing, Radio Pakistan reported.

The term Marka-e-Haq refers to the 2025 conflict with India, which began after India falsely blamed Pakistan for the April 22 Pahalgam attack and concluded with a ceasefire on May 10 following a successful Operation Bunyanun Marsoos launched by the country’s armed forces.

Addressing the annual convocation of the University of Central Punjab in Sialkot, the minister said Pakistan had defeated an enemy five times larger than itself, adding that the Pakistan Armed Forces had shot down several enemy aircraft.

“Pakistan's success has also been acknowledged by international media,” he stated during the speech.

He said the Pakistan Armed Forces had been fighting terrorism for several decades while continuing to fulfil their responsibility of safeguarding the country's borders.

The defence minister described the youth as the country's most valuable asset, emphasising that educated and skilled young people could play a vital role in national development and prosperity.

The 2025 Indo-Pak war

The tensions between the nuclear-armed neighbours, Pakistan and India, escalated following the April 22 attack in Pahalgam, located in the Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir (IIOJK), which claimed 26 lives. India accused Pakistan of involvement without evidence, while Islamabad categorically rejected the claims.

A day later, on April 23, India announced the closure of the Wagah border crossing, revocation of Pakistani visas and suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty. Pakistan condemned these measures as an act of aggression and announced reciprocal steps, warning that any further escalation would bear serious consequences.

The confrontation intensified on the night of May 6–7, when India launched military strikes against Pakistan, triggering the most serious military escalation between the two nuclear-armed neighbours in decades.

Pakistan's military response resulted in the downing of at least five Indian fighter jets, including three Rafale, one SU-30 and one MiG-29.

On May 7, Pakistan intercepted and destroyed 78 armed drones, identified as Israeli-origin Heron and Harop variants, deployed during the confrontation. An Indian missile projectile was also reportedly intercepted near Dinga, Punjab.

During the subsequent nights of May 8–9, Pakistan's air defence systems intercepted multiple BrahMos supersonic missiles. Pakistan further maintained that its retaliatory operations targeted 26 Indian military installations in response to attacks on seven Pakistani locations, while military sources reported the destruction of several Indian brigade and battalion headquarters along the Line of Control (LoC).

The deployment of indigenous Fateh-1 and Fateh-2 missiles was also presented as a significant demonstration of Pakistan's operational and defence capabilities.
