Addressing the annual convocation of the University of Central Punjab in Sialkot, the minister said Pakistan had defeated an enemy five times larger than itself, adding that the Pakistan Armed Forces had shot down several enemy aircraft.

“Pakistan's success has also been acknowledged by international media,” he stated during the speech.

India accused Pakistan of involvement without evidence, while Islamabad categorically rejected the claims.

headline: Shehzad questions late camp for SAFF Cup
description: Former Pakistan head coach warns a short training camp could leave players underprepared and increase risk of injuries
author: Alam Zeb Safi
article_text:
Former Pakistan head coach Shehzad Anwar has expressed his surprise over the way the Pakistan Football Federation (PFF) has started the national senior team's camp so late for the SAFF Cup, which will begin in Dhaka on November 5.

"It's strange," Shehzad told The Express Tribune on Saturday.

"You knew that the event was outside the FIFA window and foreign-based players would not be available, and you would have to go with local players, who were out of shape as there is no league or domestic football to keep them in shape," Shehzad said.

"You should have held a lengthy camp, but I don't know why it is being done," Shehzad said.

"You need at least a six-week camp for proper conditioning. In a week's time, players cannot even relax, so how will you train them?" Shehzad pointed out.

Shehzad, who has experience of serving as Pakistan head coach at the 2013 SAFF Cup, said even the world's top trainer could not do anything in this situation.

"If you bring in the world's top trainer, it will still be of no use. If you put a load on players who are not in shape, you will make them injured, and if they don't get injured, they will definitely go into the red zone and be on the brink of injury," Shehzad said.

This correspondent understands that players assembled for the camp on October 26 and were given their kits on October 28.

According to sources, even manager Shahzaib Khan was in Baku and joined the camp only recently.

The Pakistan team are scheduled to fly out for Dhaka on Monday.

Shehzad said that a league was very important.

"If you had a league, then only a week-long camp would have been enough, and you could have worked on tactical things. Now you will want the coach to produce results, and if he fails, he will be blamed. He cannot be blamed in this situation when you have not given him enough time to train the players for such an important assignment," Shehzad said.

This is not the first time that the PFF has mishandled things.

Last time, too, head coach Nolberto Solano could not get his visa in time and had to rush to Indonesia to join the squad directly for the ASEAN Cup.

Shehzad said that Pakistan always needed lengthy camps and that without them it was not possible to build a strong side.

"Even if your team delivers results at the cost of injuries to some players, it is also against the spirit of the game. Players need ample time in camp. If Bangladesh hold a camp late, they have their own league and their players are in perfect shape," Shehzad said.

It would be a real test for Nolberto Solano's charges to deliver at the SAFF Cup, which Pakistan have never won.

Pakistan are in Group B with India and Maldives, while Group A comprises Bangladesh, Bhutan and Sri Lanka.

The top two teams from each group will progress to the semi-finals.

Pakistan will face India in their opening match on November 5. India have announced a second-string side for the event. Their senior team will travel to New Zealand for two friendly matches. They will face the hosts in Auckland on November 12 and Christchurch on November 15.

Nepal is missing the event for the first tme in history due to suspension issue.

headline: Anti-encroachment drive will continue regardless of political influence, says Talal
description: Minister questions legality of guard cabin, generator at Fazl's residence after CDA issues encroachment notice
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry on Saturday said the capital's anti-encroachment campaign would continue regardless of political influence, questioning the legality of a security cabin and generator at the residence of Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, and terming the defence of encroachments ‘inappropriate’.

The remarks came a day after the Capital Development Authority (CDA) issued an encroachment notice at Fazl's residence, identifying illegal constructions and encroachments on its land and directing their removal within 15 days.

The notice came amid an escalating war of words between the government and Fazl, who had criticised what he described as the government's misuse of the Constitution. Federal ministers hit back, accusing the JUI-F chief of overlooking his own role in forming and toppling governments.

"There will be no encroachments of any kind, and there will be zero tolerance for this," Chaudhry said during a televised address, adding that the campaign had been running for more than a year and a half. He added that notices had gone out in "every other street" of Islamabad. "Whoever committed any illegal encroachment received one," he said.

Chaudhry noted that a notice was issued "in routine" to Amanullah. It was, the minister said, a "completely simple notice" pasted on the house, giving 15 days to remove a four-by-four security cabin.

Chaudhry described the cabin as a "cage-like structure" in which a guard sits in summer and winter, outside a house large enough to park some 10 cars worth millions. The minister said that for the guard inside, "there can be no shaded or any better place," calling this a "human matter" but also an illegal one.

The same applied to the generator, he said, adding that the house was no one-or-two-marla plot but stood in one of the capital's large upscale areas where neighbours had received and complied with similar notices.

"But because Maulana is living here," he said, the thought seemed to be that the same illegal construction would be protected, the minister said, calling it "highly inappropriate." Chaudhry also asked why permission was not taken for the constructions on the property, which he said run to thousands of square feet, and said no notice was issued for anything that was built lawfully.

"I have a simple question: Is the keeping of your cabin on the green area, the green belt, or what has been left out for your house legal? Is that lawful?" he asked. He further questioned whether it was legal to keep a large generator in people's path or on government land. "If it is legal in others' houses, then your house too would be legal," he said.

He also rejected the suggestion that oppression was being done to Fazl, saying action had been taken against everyone in Islamabad, rich or poor, powerful or not. "Action was taken against all," he said.

"No, oppression is not being done; there are many such things you yourself are doing that is illegal. Neither do you have justification for it, nor can you answer for it," the minister said.

Chaudhry said Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi had demolished a police station standing on government land and partly on a green belt "with his own hands" a day earlier. He said the FC, which had occupied a park for several decades, was also made to clear out, uprooting their offices, and a park was built in its place. Some five-star hotels and other major buildings, he said, also lost walls that stood outside their boundaries.

"So this operation will continue," he said, whether the house belonged to "some Amanullah" or was home to "some very big leader or very powerful people." "This will absolutely continue," he said.

The minister also cited operations carried out in the federal capital in this regard, saying that property was vacated behind the Prime Minister's House while illegal petrol pumps, marriage halls and other structures were removed along the Expressway.

In Sector E-11, allottees were given possession and allotment letters but could not get their plots back from illegal occupants, Chaudhry said. An operation two months ago removed the encroachments and returned the plots, he added. "In fact, a second generation has come along," he said, describing how one generation had waited for the plots it had been allotted.

The drive, Chaudhry said, was being carried out "without regard to whether anyone is very influential." In the capital's "posh sectors," he said, "this campaign has been running for several months."

Chaudhry added that security guard cabins, generators and illegal constructions of diplomats, bureaucrats and businessmen were removed from green areas and fines were imposed. "The proof of this you will find in the posh sectors of Islamabad, in every other street," he said.

Further, Chaudhry called on Fazl to answer the questions he had asked, arguing that in Peshawar, where houses of the poor or illegal buildings of businessmen on roads, in parks and on government land were being demolished, he claimed Fazl had occupied a road. "Why would we, in the name of religion, continue this illegal occupation?" he asked.

He also questioned a building named after Fazl's father, asking whether it was legal to block the path people used to pass by it, and whether it was religious to do so. "In our religion, there is talk of opening paths, not of blocking paths," he said.

"If someone is a political leader, there is a great deal of responsibility on him compared to an ordinary man," Chaudhry said, adding, "But if he is both political and a religious leader, then the responsibility on him is very great."

The minister termed the JUI-F chief a "renowned man" and asked, "What has this state not given you, what all has it not given?"

Further, he referred to the interior minister's earlier remarks and said, "you could not answer his words, could not answer his questions," arguing that Fazl had "made a personal attack on the interior minister."

"Personal attacks are made only by those who have no answers to questions, who have no answer to the real matter," he said.

He went on to question if "the providers of religious training have trained their leaders that they will make such vulgar, indecent personal attacks, will say such things for which neither our tradition permits, nor our society permits, and religion certainly does not permit?"

He also accused Fazl of trying to make martyrs controversial. "You may mock the martyrdoms and the martyrs, the plots of land they got, occupy them," arguing, "if you occupy their plots, that is fine, but if someone is martyred, then you try to make him controversial."

Chaudhry further stated, "From the martyrs to the state, which you call mother-like, which has raised children like you too, who occupy roads, who occupy plots, who, putting the Constitution, law, religion to one side, only for their own political power and in the name of their religion, are using their power to do illegal work."

The state, Chaudhry said, "kept giving a lot of leeway," and he asked why, if Fazl could give it nothing else, could not "just vacate the road, just vacate the park, just vacate the green belt, just give up illegal work."

The minister concluded by saying, "The questions that I have asked, I hope you will answer those questions, and answer them to the point." He reiterated, "Is keeping a generator on the road, building rooms for security guards on the green belt, legal?"

The state, Chaudhry said, "kept giving a lot of leeway," and he asked why, if Fazl could give it nothing else, could not "just vacate the road, just vacate the park, just vacate the green belt, just give up illegal work."

The minister concluded by saying, "The questions that I have asked, I hope you will answer those questions, and answer them to the point." He reiterated, "Is keeping a generator on the road, building rooms for security guards on the green belt, legal?"

headline: ‘Aerosmith’ singer Steven Tyler’s memoir resurfaces as legal battle involving teenage girl continues
description: Court proceedings focus on allegations tied to singer’s time with a teenage fan during an Aerosmith tour
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Steven Tyler is facing a legal battle over allegations that he sexually exploited a teenage girl during the 1970s, with a lawsuit against the Aerosmith frontman continuing in California after much of the case was dismissed.

The lawsuit was filed in 2022 by Julia Misley, formerly known as Julia Holcomb, who alleges that Tyler began a relationship with her when she was 16 and he was in his mid-20s. Tyler has denied the allegations.

The case has drawn renewed attention to passages in Tyler’s 2011 memoir, Does the Noise in My Head Bother You?, in which he described their relationship and recalled Misley being 16 when they met. His account included details about their time together and living arrangements.

Misley has alleged that Tyler used his celebrity and influence to exploit her while she was underage. She has also claimed that she became pregnant during the relationship and was pressured to have an abortion.

Earlier this year, a judge dismissed most of the lawsuit, citing statute of limitations restrictions. However, a claim connected to alleged conduct during a California trip remained active, allowing the legal proceedings to continue under provisions of the California Child Victims Act.

Tyler’s attorney described the ruling as a significant victory, saying only a limited part of the case involving an alleged incident decades ago could proceed.

The lawsuit has prompted renewed discussion about the treatment of underage girls in the music industry during the 1970s and the extent to which past behaviour should be examined under current legal standards.

Misley’s case is not the only allegation involving Tyler and a teenager. In 2022, another woman, Jeanne Bellino, alleged that he assaulted her when she was 17 in 1975. Her lawsuit was dismissed in New York because of statute of limitations rules.

The California case remains ongoing. Tyler has not been found liable in the allegations, and the claims against him have yet to be resolved in court.

headline: Jennifer Lawrence rules out playing Mystique again in future ‘X-Men’ films ‘absolutely f***ing not’
description: The Oscar winner says years of body paint, cold airbrushes and hair damage made the role physically demanding
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Jennifer Lawrence has ruled out returning as Mystique in future X-Men films, revealing that the extensive makeup and prosthetics required for the character made the experience particularly difficult.

The Oscar-winning actress played the blue-skinned mutant in four films between 2011 and 2019, beginning with X-Men: First Class. While Lawrence enjoyed performing the character’s stunts and physical training, she said the body paint remained her least favourite part of the role.

Asked by Allure whether she would consider undergoing such an extensive transformation again, Lawrence responded emphatically, “Never say never, but absolutely f***ing not.”

The actress explained that the process involved cold airbrushes, discomfort and long hours in the makeup chair. She also described herself as particularly ticklish, which made the experience even harder.

Lawrence further recalled the physical and mental toll of the demanding process, saying she discovered how little sleep she could function on and how difficult it became to maintain patience.

During an appearance on the Call Her Daddy podcast, Lawrence discussed her experience filming X-Men: First Class, revealing that applying Mystique’s makeup took approximately eight hours each time.

“For First Class, it was all body paint and glue. It was eight hours every time and ticklish,” she said, describing the sensation of cold airbrushes moving across her body.

Lawrence also recalled the preparation for her Mystique screen test, during which her hair was dyed several different colours in a single day, including red, brown, black and blonde. She said the process permanently damaged her hair.

Despite the difficult preparation, Lawrence has fond memories of the physical performance involved in playing Mystique. She praised her stunt double, Renee Moneymaker, who also worked with her on The Hunger Games, and described training for the role as a rewarding experience.

Lawrence also recalled the preparation for her Mystique screen test, during which her hair was dyed several different colours in a single day, including red, brown, black and blonde. She said the process permanently damaged her hair.

Despite the difficult preparation, Lawrence has fond memories of the physical performance involved in playing Mystique. She praised her stunt double, Renee Moneymaker, who also worked with her on The Hunger Games, and described training for the role as a rewarding experience.

headline: Ben Affleck donates $100K to support children battling epilepsy, shares personal connection to the cause
description: The Care & Cure Institute’s 20th anniversary gala raised nearly $2 million to expand specialist care for children
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Ben Affleck has donated $100,000 to support children living with epilepsy, sharing a personal connection to the condition during a charity event honouring his philanthropic efforts.

The actor attended The Care & Cure Institute’s 20th Anniversary Gala on October 28, where he was recognised for his longstanding charitable work. The nonprofit aims to address the shortage of specialists trained to diagnose and treat epilepsy in children.

Ahead of National Epilepsy Awareness Month in November, Affleck spoke about witnessing people close to him deal with the condition and stressed the importance of families gaining timely access to medical specialists.

“Epilepsy is not abstract to me. I have watched people I care about deal with it, and I have seen how much it matters when a family can get in front of the right doctor quickly,” he said.

Affleck also praised physicians who dedicate their careers to treating children and commended the organisation for helping train more specialists.

The gala raised nearly $2 million, with Affleck expressing gratitude to attendees who contributed to the cause. He also promised to continue supporting efforts to raise awareness and funds.

Addressing the audience, the actor emphasised that illness can affect any family and encouraged people to take action to help children in need.

“None of us get to choose whether it is our child or someone else’s child who gets sick,” Affleck said. “But all of us get to choose what we are going to do about the children who do get sick.”

He highlighted the organisation’s impact over the past two decades, noting that doctors trained through its efforts have cared for more than 350,000 children.

Affleck concluded by urging supporters to continue building on that progress and ensuring more young patients can access specialised care.

The event also celebrated the work of Care & Cure Institute co-founders Andrew Gumpert and Mark Borman, whose organisation continues to focus on improving treatment access for children with epilepsy.

headline: Trump administration plans to deport Afghan refugees to Pakistan: report
description: Proposed deportation flights could start from Monday, raising concerns refugees may be returned to Afghanistan
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
The Trump administration is preparing to deport Afghan refugees to Pakistan as early as Monday, despite concerns that they could subsequently be returned to Afghanistan under Taliban rule, media reports said Friday.

The proposed deportation flight has not been publicly announced, but rights advocates and families of detainees said it could take place in the coming days, according to NBC News.

The reported plans come amid continued uncertainty surrounding Afghan refugees housed at Camp As Sayliyah in Qatar, where the US government has repeatedly extended deadlines for removing residents.

The State Department initially announced that everyone would be removed from the facility by March 31, but the deadline was subsequently extended to Sept. 30.

In September, the Trump administration postponed the camp’s closure by another nine months, according to the report.

Earlier this year, the administration also considered transferring Afghan refugees from Camp As Sayliyah to the Democratic Republic of Congo, where an Ebola outbreak was reported.

The possibility of deportation to Pakistan has raised concerns among rights advocates and detainees’ families about the refugees’ safety and the risk of their eventual return to Afghanistan.

AfghanEvac, an organisation advocating for Afghan refugees, criticised the administration’s reported deportation plans in a statement Friday.

The group accused the administration of preparing the flight while public attention was focused on the upcoming US midterm elections, “hoping no one is watching.”

“The government won’t say where these flights land, because it knows what happens to the people on them when they do,” the outlet quoted AfghanEvac as saying.

“A government confident in what it is doing does not hide it,” the organisation added.

The reported flight would come after months of uncertainty over the future of Afghan refugees at the Qatar facility, as the administration continues considering arrangements for their removal.

The destination and timing of the proposed flight have not been officially confirmed.

headline: 1 killed, 6 injured in shooting at Halloween store in California
description: At least 3 victims remain in critical condition following shooting at Fairfield mall, as police search for suspect
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
At least 3 victims remain in critical condition following shooting at Fairfield mall, as police search for suspect

One person was killed and six others injured in a shooting at a Halloween store inside a shopping mall in California, US media reported Saturday.

Police responded to the shooting at a Spirit Halloween store in Solano Town Center in Fairfield around 8.30 pm Friday, according to ABC News.

Officers found seven people suffering from gunshot wounds, one of whom later died.

The six surviving victims were transported to local hospitals, with at least three in critical condition.

Authorities have not released the identities of the victims.

"We encourage anyone in the community with information to contact the Fairfield Police Department," ABC News quoted Police Chief Dan Marshall as saying.

Detectives are interviewing witnesses and working to identify the suspect, while the shooting scene remains under investigation.

On October 11, 9 people died in a shooting in Erie, Pennsylvania, where a 45-year-old man opened fire in a neighbourhood.

Two children and a pregnant woman were among the slain.

There have been more than 400 mass shootings in the US in 2026, according to data compiled by Gun Violence Archive, which defines a mass shooting ⁠as one ​in which four or more people are shot, excluding ​the shooter. The last recorded mass shootings in Pennsylvania took place in July in Philadelphia, according to the ​data.

headline: PM criticises PTI's 13-year rule in K-P, urges PML-N leadership to prioritise public welfare projects
description: ​​​​​​​Premier highlights sacrifices of people, questions provincial government’s performance over past 13 years
author: aamir.ilyas.rana
article_text:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday criticised the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf’s (PTI) 13-year rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), saying the province’s residents had suffered years of developmental neglect, and urged the provincial leadership of the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) to prioritise short-term public welfare projects.

Addressing the PML-N parliamentary party meeting at Parliament House in Islamabad, the prime minister said the people, police, armed forces, and political leadership had made unprecedented sacrifices in the war against terrorism in K-P.

“Pakistan suffered enormous human and economic losses in the war against terrorism,” he said, recalling that the entire nation and state institutions had joined hands during former prime minister Nawaz Sharif's tenure to eliminate the menace.

Two days ago, the Ministry of Interior told the National Assembly that security forces neutralised 2,410 terrorists during 5,143 intelligence-based operations in the first nine months of 2026.

Reminiscing about the Army Public School (APS) tragedy in Peshawar, PM Shehbaz said the horrific incident remains fresh in the nation's memory. The martyrdom of innocent children, he added, would remain one of the darkest chapters of the past.

He said the sacrifices of the people of K-P, who had remained on the frontline of the fight against militancy, must never be overlooked.

Two days ago, the Ministry of Interior told the National Assembly that security forces neutralised 2,410 terrorists during 5,143 intelligence-based operations in the first nine months of 2026.

headline: Who won ‘The Celebrity Traitors’ season 2? Finale leaves viewers stunned with unexpected twist
description: A tense final roundtable brings shocking revelations and unexpected decisions inside the castle
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
The second season of The Celebrity Traitors ended with an unexpected outcome as Faithfuls Sebastian Croft and Romesh Ranganathan emerged victorious after both remaining Traitors, King Kenny and Maya Jama, were banished in a tense finale.

The result followed a major turning point involving comedian James Acaster, whose revelation that he had secretly been recruited as a Traitor disrupted what had appeared to be a strong position for the group. His admission at the roundtable changed the direction of the game and put further pressure on the remaining players.

Maya Jama was eventually banished after Faithful Michael Sheen, who had been murdered earlier in the game, had worked out her identity. With both Traitors eliminated, Croft and Ranganathan secured the victory for the Faithfuls.

The finale also brought disappointment for James Blunt, who left the competition despite being a Faithful. His confidence in identifying the Traitors had made him a prominent voice at the roundtable, but some of his suspicions proved inaccurate and contributed to his downfall.

The season had faced challenges following the early departures of Richard E Grant and Professor Hannah Fry. Grant revealed his Traitor status shortly after being selected, while Fry was later recruited. Neither remained in the game long enough to establish a lasting dynamic among the Traitors.

As Variety noted in its finale coverage, the second series had a difficult task following the first season, which became memorable for Alan Carr’s unlikely success as a Traitor.

Despite a less predictable run of suspense and an ending that divided the season’s dramatic moments, the format continued to attract a substantial audience. The BBC reportedly said the series had reached 15 million viewers, underlining the programme’s popularity.

The latest result gives the Faithfuls a memorable victory, although the season’s twists and early exits made the journey to the final considerably different from its predecessor.

The latest result gives the Faithfuls a memorable victory, although the season’s twists and early exits made the journey to the final considerably different from its predecessor.

headline: Gaza charities ‘incredibly grateful’ for Macklemore’s support as Free Palestine tour concludes
description: The proceeds feom all three sold out concerts will go to 12 organisations and charities supporting Palestinians
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Gaza charities have expressed their gratitude to Macklemore for using his platform to support Palestinians, as the rapper prepares to conclude his sold-out Free Palestine Tour in London.

The Seattle-born artist launched the three-show European tour after being dropped as a supporting act on Ed Sheeran’s US stadium tour in September, following comments he made about Gaza.

Macklemore, 43, has spoken out in support of Palestinians during performances, calling for a “Free Palestine” and describing the situation in Gaza as a “genocide”.

All proceeds from the three sold-out concerts will go to 12 organisations and charities supporting Palestinians, including those providing humanitarian aid, medical care, education and community support.

Shabby Amini, director of fundraising and marketing at Medical Aid for Palestinians, said the organisation was “incredibly grateful” for Macklemore’s support.

“We are incredibly grateful to Macklemore for his generous support and for using his platform to keep the experiences of Palestinians in the spotlight, especially at a time when many are choosing to stay silent,” Amini said.

“Macklemore’s support is a powerful reminder that Palestinians must not be forgotten when the headlines move on.”

A spokesperson for Anera, an aid organisation supporting displaced Palestinians, also praised the rapper’s efforts to bring people together through music.

“Music has always had the power to bring people together, inspire action and unite us in the pursuit of something greater,” the spokesperson said.

“Seeing thousands of people come together through song and love in solidarity with the people of Gaza moves us deeply.”

Macklemore’s Free Palestine Tour began in Dublin on October 26, followed by a show in Paris on October 29. The final concert is scheduled to take place at London’s OVO Arena Wembley on Friday evening.

The organisations set to benefit from the tour include Anera, Glia, Gaza Soup Kitchen, Taawon, Heal Palestine, Palestinian Youth Movement, Middle East Children’s Alliance, Jewish Voice for Peace, Medical Aid for Palestinians, Institute for Middle East Understanding, Palestine Children’s Relief Fund and UNRWA USA.

The rapper announced the tour 10 days after being removed from Sheeran’s The Loop tour.

Macklemore has said that Robert Kraft, owner of the New England Patriots and Gillette Stadium, contacted Sheeran and said the rapper would not be allowed to perform at the venue if he remained on the bill.

Sheeran later said the decision to remove Macklemore was made by his promoter, after venues indicated they would not host the shows with the rapper as a supporting act.

Several other artists subsequently withdrew from Sheeran’s tour in solidarity with Macklemore.

The Free Palestine Tour has brought together musicians and supporters to raise funds and maintain attention on the humanitarian crisis facing Palestinians.

headline: Hakimi stars as PSG rip Le Havre
description: PSG's nearest Ligue 1 rivals Rennes suffer defeat at Nice
author: AFP
article_text:
Achraf Hakimi rose to the occasion scoring a glorious hat-trick on Friday as a heavily rotated Paris Saint-Germain thumped rock-bottom Le Havre 5-1 in Ligue 1.

PSG's nearest Ligue 1 rivals Rennes lost 5-2 at Nice to drop four points adrift while Olivier Giroud's late goal lifted Lille second after their 1-0 home win over Lens.

The former World Cup and Champions League winner Giroud is now 40 and came off the bench to net his third goal of the season to settle a tense, tight struggle.

PSG have won six league games in a row after a slow start this term and top the table with 20 points. Lille are second on 18 but Monaco can join them should they beat Paris FC on Sunday, while Rennes have 16.

On just two points so far, Le Havre gave their opponents a game early on as they suddenly surged forward in numbers with the PSG backline scampering in retreat before striker Josh Maja hammered in the opener against the run of play on 18 minutes.

Pushing for a second, Le Havre were carved open in a quick-fire move with Belgian winger Mika Godts racing onto a Hakimi pass to level on 26 minutes.

Two minutes later Hakimi left the defence trailing and his blistering low drive just inside the near post made it 2-1.

The European champions were running the Normandy side ragged before Hakimi scored his second with a fierce free-kick that curled low past the 'keeper Arnaud Bodard to put PSG 3-1 up.

Le Havre poured everyone forward in a brave effort to get back into the game, only for PSG to burst back, catching the home goalkeeper way off his line with not a single defender in his half.

Senny Mayulu ran around Bodard, and his cool long-range finish hit the back of the net to effectively end the contest, just after the hour.

Hakimi completed his hat-trick when Bodard saved his initial effort, only for the ball to rebound off the Morocco international and loop into the net on 69 minutes. He had hardly finished a triumphant celebration when coach Luis Enrique subbed him off.

"He's a striker when we have the ball. He's free to do that when we are in possession, but obliged to defend when we aren't," said Luis Enrique.

The Spanish coach left stars Desire Doue, Vitinha and Joao Neves on the bench, while Ousmane Dembele was absent through injury and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia faces the prospect of missing the rest of the season after tearing his ACL in last week's Champions League win over Barcelona.

headline: Marquez stretches MotoGP championship lead
description: Marco Bezzecchi late surge takes him to third at Sepang
author: AFP
article_text:
Marc Marquez extended his lead in the MotoGP standings when he finished second in a thrilling Malaysian sprint race Saturday behind Pedro Acosta, with title rival Jorge Martin out injured.

Acosta crossed the finish line in 20min 04.098 sec, with fellow Spaniard Marquez 0.578sec behind in second for Ducati.

Italian Marco Bezzecchi mounted a late challenge to take third at Sepang.

Reigning world champion Marquez went 19 points clear of closest challenger Martin, who withdrew from the weekend action earlier in the day after failing to recover from a broken wrist.

The seven-time world champion Marquez survived an early scare when he almost collided with Ai Ogura on a sharp turn after the lights went green, as younger brother Alex Marquez retained the early lead from pole.

Alex Marquez crashed out on Lap 3 after he skidded off on a sweeping turn, allowing Japan's Ogura to become the new race leader.

A light drizzle swept across the Sepang circuit and the race changed momentum when Acosta overtook Ogura to become the third race leader on the seventh lap, before the Japanese was gobbled up by Marquez into second.

Marquez had to use his experience to fend off the challenge of Ogura as both men traded places, before the Spaniard accelerated past the Trackhouse rider on a tight corner to pursue Acosta right to the finish line.

Marquez said he did not enjoy the race, despite now being in a strong position in his title duel with Martin.

"I enjoyed zero. Today was real work, we did what we needed to do," he said.

"It's a circuit which some years I have struggled a lot, but we are saving well.

"Will be super concentrated for tomorrow."

Martin's premature exit from Sepang dealt a huge blow to the Spaniard's title hopes, with just three race weekends to go after this.

The Aprilia rider fears his chances of reclaiming the title he won in 2024 could be over.

"Maybe I can win it, but for me it's already a loss," said the Spaniard.

"So for sure I will fight till the end. Not only for me, because at the end of the day I'm already champion, but for my team, for my people, I will fight till the end."

The main race is on Sunday.

headline: West Indies crush Bangladesh in first Test
description: Visitors take a 1-0 lead in the two-match series
author: AFP
article_text:
Brandon King struck a career-best 81 not out as West Indies cruised to an eight-wicket win over Bangladesh in the first Test on Saturday to take a 1-0 lead in the two-match series.

King hit 10 fours and a six in his 115-ball knock to help the visitors chase down the target of 170 in 35.1 overs on the fourth day in Mirpur after Bangladesh were bowled out for 142 in their second innings.

Jomel Warrican, who was named player of the match, claimed 4-63 to follow up his five-wicket haul in Bangladesh's first innings as the hosts were bowled out in 48.4 overs.

West Indies captain Roston Chase took 5-36 in the second innings, his fifth five-wicket haul in Test cricket.

Chase said the team was determined to win the series and go up in the rankings.

"The guys were determined, even though we didn't have a good start in the first innings," Chase said.

"We lost the lead, but we were still determined to fight back and try to win the game, and that's what we did."

Bangladesh had resumed the fourth day at 79-6, holding a lead of 106, but their hopes of setting a challenging target suffered an early blow when Jaker Ali edged Warrican to slip, where Chase took the catch.

Jaker, who scored 22 off 34 balls, was the second-highest scorer for Bangladesh in the innings.

Nayeem Hasan survived two dropped catches off Chase, on 21 and 29, to keep Bangladesh going.

- 'Intention was good' -

He added 26 runs with Hasan Mahmud before Warrican trapped the latter lbw for eight.

Taijul Islam contributed eight in a 17-run partnership with Nayeem before Chase dismissed him to leave Bangladesh at 127-9.

Nayeem then reached his maiden Test half-century off 87 balls, with four boundaries, but his resistance ended when he attempted to hit Chase over long-on and was caught by Joshua Bishop.

He made 52 off 91 balls, while Shoriful Islam remained unbeaten on seven as Bangladesh were dismissed cheaply.

Bangladesh skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto said his team failed to execute their plans.

"All three departments didn't do well, especially in the field. These things can happen sometimes, but I believe the intention and preparation were quite good," he said.

"Going forward, we need to look at those areas and work out how we can do better in these conditions."

West Indies started confidently, with openers King and John Campbell continuing their aggressive approach to take the visitors to 64 without loss in 14.1 overs before rain interrupted play.

After a delay of around an hour, they added another 23 runs before bad light and lightning forced a further stoppage of 45 minutes.

King was dropped on 70 by substitute fielder Ebadot Hossain off Taijul after the break, but the opener made Bangladesh pay with his fine, unbeaten knock.

Campbell fell just short of a half-century, bowled by Shoriful for 49 off 55 balls, with six fours and a six.

The second Test will be played in Sylhet from November 5.

headline: UK PM Burnham says he is 'open' to formal apology for slavery, but rules out reparations
description: UK PM Burnham says he is 'open' to formal apology for slavery, but rules out reparations
author: Reuters
article_text:
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he was open to calls for a formal apology for Britain's historical role in slavery, ​before attending next week's Commonwealth summit at which he is likely ‌to face demands for financial reparations.

Writing in the Guardian newspaper, Burnham said Britain was "offering a structured dialogue with those affected by the transatlantic slave trade", in which at ​least 12.5 million Africans were abducted and sold into slavery.

"Listening to ​calls for a formal apology on behalf of the British ⁠state will form an important part of this process, and I am ​open to them," he added.

But Burnham rejected calls for financial reparations, writing: "I do ​not think that British people today can be held liable for historical wrongs, however heinous, that happened in a different age under different laws and in which they played ​no personal part."

From the 15th to the 19th century, millions of Africans ​were sold into slavery by European traders, with Britain transporting an estimated 3.2 million ‌people ⁠across the Atlantic, according to the Transatlantic Slave Trade Database.

Ahead of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda next week, King Charles, who is touring the Caribbean, said it was "only right that we should ​acknowledge the great suffering ​and injustices of ⁠the past".

Caribbean leaders are expected to press demands for reparations, which they have often framed in terms of ​debt relief, development finance, education, healthcare and climate resilience.

Burnham ​also wrote ⁠in the Guardian that he wanted to "launch a new drive on debt", including by helping more vulnerable countries "repay over a longer time period and with better ⁠rates".

Antigua ​and Barbuda Prime Minister Gaston Browne welcomed Burnham's ​comments and proposals for practical assistance, though he added in a Facebook post: "The Caribbean's longstanding ​position on reparatory justice remains unchanged."

headline: ‘It: Welcome to Derry’ drops surprise Halloween episode on HBO Max
description: The 30-minute special takes viewers hundreds of years before Pennywise, introducing an ancient supernatural threat
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
It: Welcome to Derry has surprised horror fans with a new episode released on HBO Max for Halloween, offering an unexpected addition to the series based on Stephen King’s terrifying universe.

The surprise instalment, titled “A Story of Derry”, arrived on October 31, with viewers discovering the release without a lengthy promotional campaign. The special reportedly runs for approximately 30 minutes and takes place hundreds of years before the events associated with Pennywise.

The story follows three young characters who venture into the Western Wood, where they encounter an ancient supernatural presence. The episode explores the origins of the terrifying forces connected to Derry, expanding the mythology established in the television series and the original It films.

The release has generated excitement among fans, many of whom had been anticipating additional material from the franchise. However, further plot details were initially kept under wraps, leaving audiences to discover the episode’s revelations themselves.

The surprise arrives following HBO’s renewal of It: Welcome to Derry for a second season. The upcoming instalment is expected to move the story back to 1935, during the Great Depression, and focus on the Bradley Gang, a group of bank robbers whose arrival in Derry leads to horrifying events.

The series is executive produced by Andy and Barbara Muschietti, who previously directed the It film adaptations, alongside other members of the creative team. Brad Caleb Kane is set to continue as showrunner for the second season.

Season one has established itself as a major addition to the franchise, drawing audiences into the town’s disturbing history and the mysteries surrounding Pennywise.

With the Halloween special adding another chapter to the mythology, fans now have fresh material to examine while awaiting the next season. All nine episodes listed as available in the current streaming announcement can be watched on HBO Max.

headline: Did Jennifer Lawrence accidentally reveal the big ‘Sunrise on the Reaping’ secret casting news? The cast gives hilarious reactions
description: The cast and director were caught off guard but shared how emotional it was to welcome the original stars back to Panem
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Jennifer Lawrence appears to have let a major The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping casting secret slip, leaving the upcoming film’s cast surprised after confirming that she, Josh Hutcherson and Woody Harrelson are returning to the franchise.

During an appearance on the Call Her Daddy podcast, Lawrence revealed her involvement in the new film. Her comments quickly became a talking point at a red carpet event, where members of the Sunrise on the Reaping cast were asked about the original stars coming back.

Mckenna Grace, who plays Maysilee Donner, initially appeared caught off guard when a reporter mentioned Lawrence’s confirmation.

“Who said that? She did?” Grace responded, before acknowledging the news and adding that it was cool to have the actors returning.

Her reaction was particularly amusing because she seemed unsure whether she was allowed to discuss the casting news. She also spoke emotionally about the scale of the franchise and the experience of being part of the new film, describing her fellow cast members as family.

Other cast members shared similarly warm reactions. One described the reunion involving Hutcherson and the returning actors as emotional, recalling how closely they stayed together on set. The cast also expressed excitement that the news was finally public after months of carefully avoiding questions about the original stars.

View this post on Instagram

They highlighted how meaningful the returning actors’ involvement would be for the film and its connection to the wider franchise.

Sunrise on the Reaping is based on Suzanne Collins’ novel and takes place during the 50th Hunger Games, decades before the events of the original films. The new story follows a younger Haymitch Abernathy, the character previously played by Hutcherson in the franchise.

Lawrence’s apparent confirmation has now added fresh excitement around the prequel, particularly for fans eager to see familiar faces return to Panem.

headline: Margaret Qualley and Jack Antonoff file for divorce after three years of marriage
description: The couple reportedly separated in July, just weeks before their third wedding anniversary
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Actor Margaret Qualley and Grammy-winning musician Jack Antonoff have filed for divorce after three years of marriage, according to court records.

The divorce case was filed on Friday, October 30, in Kings County Supreme Court in Brooklyn, New York. Qualley is listed as the plaintiff and Antonoff as the defendant in the uncontested matrimonial action.

The couple reportedly separated in July, just weeks before their third wedding anniversary. Their representatives have not immediately responded to requests for comment.

Qualley, 32, is known for her roles in films including The Substance and Once Upon a Time in Hollywood. Antonoff, 42, is a 14-time Grammy Award winner who has worked with major artists including Taylor Swift, Lana Del Rey and Sabrina Carpenter. He is also the frontman of the band Bleachers.

The pair began dating in 2021 and married in August 2023. Their wedding in New Jersey was attended by several high-profile guests, including Taylor Swift, Lana Del Rey and Zoë Kravitz.

News of their separation emerged in July, after Antonoff attended celebrations for Swift and Travis Kelce’s wedding without Qualley. The couple had also prompted speculation after Qualley removed wedding photographs from her Instagram account.

Qualley’s representatives previously denied reports that trust issues or infidelity had contributed to the separation, describing those claims as “categorically untrue”.

headline: Masood Khan receives warm welcome after completing Peshawar-Karachi run
description: The ultra-endurance athlete receives a warm welcome in Peshawar and a Rs500,000 cash award after completing the gruelling journey on foot.
author: Riaz Ahmad
article_text:
Record-holding ultra-endurance athlete Masood Khan received a warm welcome at the Peshawar Sports Complex after completing an extraordinary 1,850-kilometre journey from Peshawar to Karachi on foot in 24 days.

Director General Sports Wasal Khan, Additional Deputy Commissioner Dawood Salimi, Additional Director General Sports Rasheeda Ghaznavi, Director Operations Jamshed Baloch and other officials welcomed the athlete with floral garlands and congratulated him on the achievement.

Speaking at the reception, Wasal Khan said Masood had brought honour to Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and Pakistan through his determination, courage and hard work.

He described the feat as an inspiration for young people and said the provincial government was committed to supporting talented athletes and promoting sports.

Wasal Khan also announced that the Sports Department would organise a marathon along the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) route in November, along with other sporting competitions. He announced a cash award of Rs500,000 for Masood in recognition of his accomplishment.

Dawood Salimi praised the athlete’s perseverance, saying the achievement demonstrated that difficult goals could be reached through dedication and consistent effort. He said the district administration would continue supporting sports and positive activities for young people.

Masood said his main motivation was to honour the memory of his late father and bring recognition to Pakistan.

He described the 24-day journey as an immense test of physical endurance, saying he faced scorching heat, rain and other hardships along the way. At one point, he lost consciousness but continued with the challenge after recovering.

The athlete said he covered between 70 and 85 kilometres each day, depending on the circumstances. He prepared for the feat with 90 days of intensive training, spending around eight hours daily on physical preparation.

Masood said he had won 49 medals in full and half-marathon competitions across Pakistan, including 24 gold medals.

He also recalled completing another endurance challenge by covering approximately 808 kilometres on foot from Peshawar to Skardu in nine days.

headline: Rawalpindi police says legal action underway after man dies of 'police brutality' at Taxila check post
description: The victim's family says children pleaded with cops to spare the 30-year-old man, to no avail
author: Imran Asghar
article_text:
The Rawalpindi police on Saturday initiated legal proceedings following the death of a 30-year-old man at the Gangu Police Check Post in Taxila, with a police spokesperson assuring that a fair investigation would be conducted and those responsible would be held accountable.

The incident reportedly occurred when a man, travelling from Khanpur towards Taxila, was stopped by police personnel at the Gangu checkpost for a search of his vehicle.

Local residents and the victim's family alleged that the man was subjected to severe physical assault by police personnel during the search. His family claimed that the man repeatedly pleaded with the officers to stop beating him with batons, while children at the scene also cried and appealed to the police to spare him.

According to the family, the 30-year-old died at the scene as a result of the alleged police torture.

News of his death triggered protests in the area, with angry residents blocking the Taxila-Khanpur Road and surrounding police personnel, The Express Tribune witnessed on the site.

According to Rawalpindi Police Spokesperson Inspector Sajjadul Hassan, senior police officials reached the scene after the incident sparked the road blockade and widespread protest.

“Legal proceedings are underway, and the matter would be investigated on merit to apprehend those found guilty of homicide,” Inspector Hassan told The Express Tribune.

Eyewitnesses said some protesters also assaulted police officers, leaving one policeman seriously injured.

The incident sparked tensions in the area, prompting senior police officials to reach the site.

The police spokesperson said the road, which had been blocked during the protest, had subsequently been reopened to traffic.

The incident comes amid a series of allegations of police brutality and misconduct reported in Rawalpindi this year. In several of these cases, police authorities announced inquiries or departmental action following complaints and the emergence of video footage. The latest incident at the Gangu checkpost in Taxila, however, has raised further questions about police conduct during roadside checks and the use of force against civilians.

In August, a police constable was suspended and issued a charge sheet following the emergence of a video showing the alleged mistreatment of a citizen at Gujjar Khan Police Station.

In April, three students accused plainclothes police personnel of assaulting them at the Dahgal checkpoint on Adiala Road before taking them to Adiala Police Post, where they were allegedly tortured and threatened with false charges. One of the students subsequently approached the Rawalpindi city police officer, seeking legal and departmental action against the officials involved.

In February, a 12-year-old boy was allegedly tortured at Rawat Police Station, prompting the suspension of three police officials and an inquiry into the incident. The same month, a resident accused personnel at RA Bazaar Police Station of torture, blackmail and extortion, while another case involved a 45-year-old man who sustained severe burn injuries after allegedly setting himself on fire at a police post. His family accused police personnel of torture, although the police disputed the allegations and said an inquiry had been initiated.

headline: South Africa beat Australia to win Test series
description: Simon Harmer takes a career-best six for 16 to complete a stunning victory
author: AFP
article_text:
South Africa beat Australia by 176 runs and clinched a series victory when Australia were bowled out for 111 on the fifth day of the third Test at Newlands on Saturday.

Kagiso Rabada took two wickets in the first over and followed up with a third in a devastating opening spell which ripped out Australia's top three batsmen after they had started the day needing 288 to win.

Off-spinner Simon Harmer took a career-best six for 16 in 21.1 overs as South Africa completed their win shortly before tea.

Josh Inglis was run out to add to Australia's woes after Rabada's initial burst before Harmer took two wickets in three balls to plunge the tourists to 42 for six.

Australia were 60 for seven at lunch when Mitchell Starc was caught at short leg but in keeping with a series of multiple changes of fortune, South Africa were kept in the field for another two hours before completing their win.

South Africa, the defending World Test champions, were projected to depose Australia at the top of the International Cricket Council world Test rankings at the end of a series in which all three matches produced a result on the fifth day.

Travis Head scored a single off Rabada's second delivery but Matt Renshaw, Australia's most successful batsman in the series, was out first ball, glancing Rabada down the leg side to a diving wicketkeeper Ryan Rickelton.

Three balls later the out-of-form Marnus Labuschagne padded up to a ball which swung in sharply and was given out leg before wicket, with a review showing umpire's call on off stump.

Head fell to a reflex catch by Marco Jansen at gully as the left-hander flashed at Rabada and the South African players celebrated the demise of a batsman capable of playing a match-changing innings.

headline: Police constable martyred, two injured in firing at Lakki Marwat judicial complex
description: Injured shifted to Bannu hospital as police heighten security, initiate investigation
author: Nasruminallah
article_text:
A police constable was martyred and two other people were injured when unidentified gunmen opened fire outside the courtroom of an additional sessions judge inside the Judicial Complex in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa's (K-P's) Lakki Marwat on Saturday.

District Headquarters (DHQ) Hospital spokesperson Jalal Khan said Constable Karamatullah was killed on the spot, while PPP District Information Secretary Advocate Javed Iqbal received bullet wounds. Another individual, identified as Inshaullah, was also wounded in the firing.

Both the injured were taken to Bannu for medical treatment, with Khan confirming that one body and two injured persons had been brought to the hospital for medical treatment.

The armed assailants reportedly opened indiscriminate fire outside the courtroom, triggering panic and prompting lawyers, litigants and other visitors to rush for safety as gunshots rang out.

Following the incident, a heavy contingent of police reached the complex and initiated an investigation to determine the circumstances surrounding the shooting and identify those responsible. Authorities subsequently sealed the complex and suspended all entry and exit movements, with the area placed under heightened security.

The incident also raised security concerns due to the judicial complex being a sensitive government facility where lawyers, litigants, judges and members of the public visit daily.

Investigations were initiated to ascertain further details regarding the motive behind the attack and the identity of the assailants.

Pakistan has witnessed a surge in terrorist activity over the past three months, with a series of attacks across the country resulting in the martyrdom of security personnel and civilians.

A day earlier, three policemen were martyred in separate incidents in K-P's Bannu, Lakki Marwat and Bajaur, while unidentified armed men abducted a head constable in Bannu.

In Bajaur, unidentified armed men launched a late-night attack on the Salai Pati Police Post, martyring Constable Khaista Main Syed. In Bannu, unidentified gunmen opened fire on Counter-Terrorism Department Constable Sadiq Zaman, killing him on the spot.

In Lakki Marwat, unidentified armed men opened fire on Constable Mumtaz near a bank, martyring him.

K-P has faced the brunt of terrorist incidents, which increased by 195% between March 1, 2024, and September 23, 2026, while drone attacks rose sharply. 73% of terrorist attacks recorded in K-P during 2026 targeted police and security personnel.

headline: Syria says discussions underway on joining Makkah Defence Alliance
description: Syrian FM says talks are underway on joining Mecca alliance with Türkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani said on Saturday that "discussions are currently underway to evaluate Syria's entry into the Makkah alliance", a regional pact that brings together Türkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia.

Shaibani’s remarks came during a regional security session at the Manama Dialogue 2026, according to the Syrian Arab News Agency (SANA).

He said Damascus was an "integral" part of regional security and would support any framework aimed at protecting regional stability.

The minister stressed that the region was "in greater need than ever" of developing joint deterrence and defence systems.

Addressing the conflict in Yemen, Shaibani reaffirmed Syria's support for the Yemeni government in restoring its sovereignty and stability across the country.

He also urged all parties to support the unity and sovereignty of states.

Separately, the Syrian foreign minister said Israel has carried out more than 1,000 attacks on his country in less than two years, killing dozens of people.

“Our territory has been subjected to more than 1,000 Israeli attacks in less than two years, killing dozens.

“How can calls for border control and placing weapons exclusively under state control be justified while Syrian sovereignty is violated and targeted on a daily basis?” he asked.

Condemning the Israeli attacks, Shaibani called for a return to the lines in place before December 8, 2024, and implementation of the 1974 Disengagement Agreement.

He stressed that the Golan Heights is Syrian territory and that UN Security Council Resolution 497 serves as the reference on this matter.

Since the fall of the Assad regime in Syria on Dec 8, 2024, Israel has occupied the Syrian buffer zone established under the 1974 Disengagement Agreement and set up military positions inside and outside it, a move the UN described as a violation of the agreement.

Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani said on Saturday that "discussions are currently underway to evaluate Syria's entry into the Makkah alliance", a regional pact that brings together Türkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia.

Shaibani’s remarks came during a regional security session at the Manama Dialogue 2026, according to the Syrian Arab News Agency (SANA).

He said Damascus was an "integral" part of regional security and would support any framework aimed at protecting regional stability.

The minister stressed that the region was "in greater need than ever" of developing joint deterrence and defence systems.

Addressing the conflict in Yemen, Shaibani reaffirmed Syria's support for the Yemeni government in restoring its sovereignty and stability across the country.

He also urged all parties to support the unity and sovereignty of states.

Separately, the Syrian foreign minister said Israel has carried out more than 1,000 attacks on his country in less than two years, killing dozens of people.

“Our territory has been subjected to more than 1,000 Israeli attacks in less than two years, killing dozens.

Read More: Pakistan brings regional rivals together

“How can calls for border control and placing weapons exclusively under state control be justified while Syrian sovereignty is violated and targeted on a daily basis?” he asked.

Condemning the Israeli attacks, Shaibani called for a return to the lines in place before December 8, 2024, and implementation of the 1974 Disengagement Agreement.

He stressed that the Golan Heights is Syrian territory and that UN Security Council Resolution 497 serves as the reference on this matter.

Since the fall of the Assad regime in Syria on Dec 8, 2024, Israel has occupied the Syrian buffer zone established under the 1974 Disengagement Agreement and set up military positions inside and outside it, a move the UN described as a violation of the agreement.

headline: Power bills and data centers cast rare spotlight on utilities in US midterms
description: US household electricity prices have risen over 10% since 2024, outpacing broader inflation
author: Reuters
article_text:
US electricity prices had flown under the radar in past national elections, but they have become a major political issue in this year's midterms as Americans grow angry over rising utility bills and deals for power-hungry ​data centers.

Nationwide, according to Energy Information Administration data, electricity prices for homes have risen more than 10% since 2024 when President Donald Trump was elected along with Republican majorities in ‌both houses of the US Congress. Higher electricity prices have outpaced the rise in costs for other goods and services.

Power bills have grown even faster in political battleground states of Ohio, Michigan and Pennsylvania, which are also hot spots for new data centers. In some cases, electricity bills have soared by triple the inflation rate.

Many politicians vying for top statehouse seats across the country this year have backed cracking down on utilities. Some have proposed freezing utility rate increases and slashing guaranteed returns, steps ​that could have sweeping consequences for the country's utility industry.

"It could be the first election to feature utilities and electricity, specifically, as a prominent issue in the midterms," said Charles Hua, executive ​director of PowerLines, a nonprofit that advocates reforming utility policy to favor consumers. "Part of that is because people's utility bills have gone up and up, and ⁠they don't see any end in sight."

Utilities are heavily regulated. State regulators generally must approve utilities’ requests to spend on the grid and to recover those costs through rate increases. Regulators also set the return on equity ​utilities can earn on their grid investments.

This year, utilities are on track to match last year's record high $31 billion in rate increase requests to regulators, a PowerLines survey showed. Last year's spending was double the previous record.

The investor-owned ​companies are also expected to carry out a record of nearly $1.3 trillion in capital spending over the next five years, according to an analysis by S&P Global’s Regulatory Research Associates.

Utilities spotlighted

Seats on nine state public utility commissions are up for election this year, nearly all the US states where voters elect their utility regulators. These include burgeoning data center hubs Arizona and Georgia.

Governors will be chosen in 36 US states this year, and governors appoint utility regulators in states where commissioners are not ​directly elected.

In Ohio, Democrat Amy Acton has promised to lower energy bills if she is elected governor. Her campaign said she will also appoint a public utilities commission that was "not beholden to utility companies" and ​work with the state attorney general to crack down on "excessive rate hikes and predatory practices."

Ohio's residential electricity bills have grown by more than 20% over the last two years, according to EIA data.

Acton has also said she supports a ‌data center ⁠moratorium. Her Republican opponent Vivek Ramaswamy said he would assure Ohioans living near data centers would not pay electricity bills at all.

Bully pulpit

Some governors who are up for reelection have used their political weight to pressure the power industry to keep prices down.

In April, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro announced that prominent utility, PECO Energy Company, had acceded to his demand that it withdraw its proposal with state regulators to increase rates. Shapiro, a Democrat running for reelection, said the move would reduce future utility bills by as much as $34 a month.

He followed up with a letter to more utility CEOs seeking changes in how utilities justify spending and returns ​on equity.

"The governors are using this crisis on energy ​affordability as an opportunity to take a ⁠deeper dive into the utility regulatory model and see if it makes any sense," said Jamie Van Nostrand, senior fellow at the Kleinman Center for Energy Policy at the University of Pennsylvania and former chair of the Massachusetts Department of Public Utilities.

Power bills tracked low inflation for roughly a decade, and were not an ​issue in most mainstream elections until last year, when Mikie Sherrill successfully ran for New Jersey governor on the promise of freezing utility bills. She ​did so the same day ⁠she took office.

In Virginia, home to the largest concentration of data centers in the world, Governor Abigail Spanberger took a similar approach, which industry analysts said could offer a playbook for those who win this year’s elections.

Utility advocates say reducing guaranteed returns and freezing rates will not make a meaningful difference in household bills but could lead to a long-term reduction of investments in the grid.

"The grid is America's greatest machine, and it doesn't operate on ⁠the political calendar,” ​said Drew Maloney, president of Edison Electric Institute, a trade organization for investor-owned electric utilities. “It requires consistent investment every year to ​deliver reliable energy to our customers."

Credit rating agency Fitch downgraded the North American utility sector to "deteriorating" from "neutral" in June, citing political pressure in the midterms to limit electricity bills and utility profits.

For an industry that plans in decades, it is hard to predict the ​result of short-term political moves aimed at saving money for households.

"I do think the real meat will come after the election," Hua said.

headline: China's first shipborne stealth combat drone completes maiden carrier landing
description: China's GJ-21 stealth drone completes its first takeoff and landing aboard Type 076 ship Sichuan
author: xinhua.
article_text:
China's first shipborne stealth reconnaissance-strike integrated drone completes first takeoff, landing on amphibious assault ship

China's first shipborne stealth reconnaissance-strike integrated drone GJ-21 has recently completed its first takeoff and landing operation aboard the Sichuan, China's first Type 076 amphibious assault ship, a navy source said.

This represents yet another breakthrough made by China in the development of amphibious assault ships and marks that the Chinese Navy has acquired the capability to operate fixed-wing stealth drones from large maritime combat platforms, the navy source noted.

The Sichuan, hull number 51, is the first Type 076 amphibious assault ship designed and built independently by China. It was launched on Dec. 27, 2024, and is named after southwest China's Sichuan Province.

The Sichuan has a full-load displacement of over 40,000 tonnes and features a dual-island superstructure along with a full-length flight deck.

The vessel features the innovative application of automated landing guidance system, integrated electric power system, and electromagnetic catapult and arrestor technologies. It is designed to carry fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles, helicopters and amphibious equipment.

Since beginning its first sea trials in November 2025, the Sichuan has steadily conducted various maritime tests as planned, successfully completing the debugging of various equipment and overall operational stability testing, the source said.

headline: Strange beaked 'hell chicken' is the first fruit-eating dinosaur
description: vInfernogallus, meaning hell chicken, is named after its bird-like look and Hell Creek fossil site
author: Reuters
article_text:
While dinosaurs ate a lot of different things, including each other, fruit long seemed to have been absent from their menu. But scientists now have found fossils of ​a turkey-sized and toothless dinosaur possessing a parrot-like head that exhibited multiple adaptations for a specialized fruit diet.

This first-known frugivorous dinosaur, named Infernogallus jamesi, lived about ‌66 million years ago during the Cretaceous Period at the twilight of the age of dinosaurs and displayed traits on its beak and jaws for mashing soft food like fruit. It is known from fossils unearthed in Montana and North Dakota.

The name Infernogallus means "hell chicken," a nod to its bird-like appearance and the fact that its fossils were found in the Hell Creek rock formation, which spans the US states of Montana, North Dakota, South Dakota and ​Wyoming and has yielded the remains of some of the most famous dinosaurs.

It would have eaten fruit and other soft plants in the subtropical coastal floodplain ecosystem it ​shared with the likes of apex predator Tyrannosaurus, three-horned herbivore Triceratops and tank-like armored plant-eater Ankylosaurus.

Infernogallus was about 5 feet (1.5 meters) long and weighed around ⁠25 pounds (11.3 kg). While the fossils — one nearly complete skeleton and isolated bones from a jaw and palate — did not reveal feathers, the researchers believe Infernogallus was covered in them, based on ​fossils of close relatives.

It belonged to a group called theropods that includes T. rex and all the meat-eating dinosaurs, as well as some that took to eating plants and the entire bird ​lineage.

"This definitely expands the range of lifestyles we thought dinosaurs had, and it shows how adaptable theropods were," said paleontologist Greg Funston of Stony Brook University in New York, lead author of the research published in the journal Nature Communications.

Fruits are the reproductive structures of angiosperms, also called flowering plants. Angiosperms first appeared earlier in the Cretaceous, around 130 to 140 million years ago, and subsequently took over landscapes previously dominated by plants called gymnosperms ​like conifers and ginkgoes.

Infernogallus shows that some dinosaurs may have had a close ecological relationship with flowering plants.

"It has been proposed before that some groups of dinosaurs ate fruits, but there was ​never evidence to back it up," said study co-author Thomas Dudgeon, a postdoctoral researcher at the Royal Ontario Museum in Toronto.

"The discovery of Infernogallus shows that dinosaur diets were likely far more diverse than we ‌previously thought. Prior ⁠to this discovery, there was a bit of a mystery in dinosaur evolution. The evolution of flowering plants introduced a brand-new food source that undoubtedly had consequences for the animals living alongside them," Dudgeon said.

The fruit available for Infernogallus may have included various berries as well as drupes, a broad category that today includes types with a central pit like peaches and cherries as well as others like mangoes and olives.

Three key features

Infernogallus showed a range of features indicating a frugivorous diet. The three most important, Funston said, were the organization of jaw muscles that powered back-and-forth chewing ​motions, a mobile joint that enabled the jaw ​to slide forward, and a series of ⁠ridges and grooves on the beak to help mash and shear soft plants like fruits.

"We see these features separately in birds and turtles today that eat soft foods, like the fig-eating vulturine parrot or green sea turtles that chew soft sea grass. But no living animal has all ​three adaptations, showing just how specialized Infernogallus was," Funston said.

Infernogallus also shows how adaptable beaks are compared to teeth.

"Once you've lost your teeth ​and developed a beak ⁠instead, the range of foods available dramatically increases, including plants, as long as you have some way to digest them," Funston said.

Most herbivorous theropods used stomach stones called gastroliths to grind food. But Infernogallus and other members of a lineage called caenagnathids chewed their food instead.

Fruit-eating animals play an important role for angiosperms by dispersing seeds.

"Mammals and birds would probably also have eaten fruit, but they didn't show the ⁠same kinds ​of specializations for a frugivorous diet that Infernogallus does, so it might have been a less important resource for ​them. Mammals and birds also were quite small in the Cretaceous, so it's unlikely that they were spreading very large seeds, or that they were spreading them big distances," Funston said.

"We know that these big-seeded fruits were proliferating and spreading, ​and it seems like caenagnathids could have fit this role — although we feel more evidence is needed before drawing that link confidently," Funston said.

headline: Chelsea deepen Manchester United's crisis
description: Carrick faces mounting pressure due to below-par showing of his charges
author: AFP
article_text:
Michael Carrick's stay of execution as Manchester United boss may not last long after his team imploded in a 2-0 Premier League loss at Chelsea on Saturday.

The visitors wasted a string of chances to take the lead at Stamford Bridge before Morgan Rogers waltzed through the heart of the United defence to open the scoring on 50 minutes.

Lisandro Martinez then ruined any chance of a revival from Carrick's men with two quickfire yellow cards, the second of which also conceded a penalty converted by Cole Palmer.

Winless in nine games, defeat leaves the 20-time English champions still just one point above the relegation zone and in danger of ending the weekend in the bottom three.

Many expected Carrick to be axed following last weekend's 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth.

The former United midfielder was instead given the chance to turn his side's fortunes around and will lament a lack of ruthlessness during the first half.

Carrick recalled captain Bruno Fernandes after he was left out last weekend in the wake of criticising his manager's tactics during a 4-1 thrashing at Como in the Champions League.

Fernandes should have marked his return with the opener when he blazed over from Bryan Mbeumo's inviting cross.

The roles were reversed when Mbeumo could not stretch to meet Fernandes's delivery at the back post before twice Amad Diallo was denied by Chelsea's stand-in goalkeeper Mike Penders.

United did finally get the ball in the net when Matheus Cunha turned in Harry Maguire's header from a corner, but the Brazilian had strayed just offside.

Carrick could not hide his frustration in a half-time interview to broadcasters and his mood soured further with a disastrous start to the second period.

Martinez sent off

Rogers credits Carrick for revitalising his career during a spell together at Middlesbrough but dealt a potentially decisive blow to his former boss.

The England international collected the ball inside the centre circle but was allowed to drive directly towards the United goal before dinking the ball over Senne Lammens.

Martinez also spoke out publicly in recent weeks to criticise United's lack of spending in the transfer market to bolster Carrick's squad.

But on this season's evidence, Martinez is one of those most in need of replacing.

The Argentine international could not cope with Rogers's strength moments later as he was penalised for hauling back the Chelsea forward.

From the resulting free-kick, Martinez then needlessly crashed into Wesley Fofana with a raised forearm.

After a VAR review, referee Peter Banks awarded a penalty and showed Martinez a second yellow card.

Lammens got hands to Palmer's spot-kick but still allowed the ball to trickle into the bottom corner.

On a rare start since Xabi Alonso took charge of the Blues, Estevao had a third goal disallowed for offside when he crashed Palmer's pass into the top corner.

Cries of "sacked in the morning" rained down from the Chelsea fans as their side toyed with United for the final quarter without adding to their lead.

Another big decision awaits the United hierarchy before a massive Champions League clash at home to Roma on Tuesday.

Beaten in two of their three European games so far, United face both the embarrassment and financial shock of an early exit should they fall to another defeat against the Italians at Old Trafford.
